title.zh: 卷七十四 列傳第三十四 臧質 魯爽 沈攸之
title.en: Volume 74 Biographies 34: Zang Zhi, Lu Shuang, Shen Youzhi
title.raw: 卷七十四 列傳第三十四 臧質 魯爽 沈攸之 Volume 74 Biographies 34: Zang Zhi, Lu Shuang, Shen Youzhi

sentences.zh: 列傳第三十四 臧質 魯爽 沈攸之

translations.literal: Biographies 34: Zang Zhi, Lu Shuang, Shen Youzhi
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 34: Zang Zhi, Lu Shuang, and Shen Youzhi

sentences.zh: 臧質，字含文，東莞莒人。

translations.literal: Zang Zhi, style name Hanwen, was a native of Ju in Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Zhi, whose style name was Hanwen, came from Ju in Dongguan commandery.

sentences.zh: 父熹，字義和，武敬皇后弟也。

translations.literal: His father Xi, style name Yihe, was a younger brother of Empress Wujing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zang Xi, style name Yihe, was a younger brother of Empress Wujing.

sentences.zh: 與兄燾並好經籍。

translations.literal: He and his elder brother Tao both loved the classics.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Tao were both devoted students of the classics.

sentences.zh: 隆安初，兵革屢起，熹乃習騎射，志在立功。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Long'an, as warfare broke out repeatedly, Xi then practiced mounted archery, his ambition set on achieving merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Long'an era opened and warfare erupted again and again, Xi took up horsemanship and archery, determined to win distinction on campaign.

sentences.zh: 嘗至溧陽，溧陽令阮崇與熹共獵，值虎突圍，獵徒並奔散，熹直前射之，應弦而倒。

translations.literal: Once he went to Liyang; the magistrate of Liyang, Ruan Chong, hunted with Xi, when a tiger burst through the encirclement; the hunters all fled in panic, but Xi went straight forward and shot it, and it fell at the twang of the bowstring.
translations.idiomatic: Once, on a visit to Liyang, he went hunting with the county magistrate Ruan Chong when a tiger broke through the beaters' ring. The party scattered in terror, but Xi rode straight at the beast and brought it down with a single shot.

sentences.zh: 高祖入京城，熹族子穆斬桓脩。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor entered the capital, Xi's clansman Mu beheaded Huan Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: When the High Ancestor marched into the capital, Xi's kinsman Zang Mu slew Huan Xiu.

sentences.zh: 進至京邑，桓玄奔走，高祖使熹入宮收圖書器物，封閉府庫。

translations.literal: Advancing to the capital district, as Huan Xuan fled in disarray, the High Ancestor had Xi enter the palace to collect books, instruments, and vessels, and to seal the treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: As the army pressed on to the capital and Huan Xuan fled, the High Ancestor sent Xi into the palace to gather books, ritual objects, and furnishings and to seal the imperial storehouses.

sentences.zh: 有金飾樂器，高祖問熹：「卿得無欲此乎？」

translations.literal: There were gold-inlaid musical instruments; the High Ancestor asked Xi: "Sir, would you not desire these?"
translations.idiomatic: Among the goods were musical instruments inlaid with gold. The High Ancestor asked Xi, "Surely you would not want these for yourself?"

sentences.zh: 熹正色曰：「皇上幽逼，播越非所。

translations.literal: Xi said with a stern countenance: "The Son of Heaven is held in duress and driven far from his proper place.
translations.idiomatic: Xi answered gravely, "Our sovereign is held captive and driven from his throne.

sentences.zh: 將軍首建大義，劬勞王家。

translations.literal: The general was first to raise the great cause and to toil on behalf of the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: You, General, were the first to raise the righteous cause and labor for the house of Liu.

sentences.zh: 雖復不肖，無情於樂。」

translations.literal: Though I am unworthy, I am without appetite for music."
translations.idiomatic: Unworthy though I am, I have no heart for music."

sentences.zh: 高祖笑曰：「聊以戲卿爾。」

translations.literal: The High Ancestor laughed and said: "I was only teasing you."
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor laughed and said, "I was only joking with you."

sentences.zh: 行參高祖鎮軍事，員外散騎侍郎，重參鎮軍軍事，領東海太守。

translations.literal: He then served as staff officer on the High Ancestor's Pacification Army staff, as Supernumerary Palace Attendant, again on the Pacification Army staff, and concurrently as Administrator of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a staff officer on the Pacification Army, made Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant at Court, served a second tour on that staff, and was given concurrent charge as Administrator of Donghai commandery.

sentences.zh: 以建義功封始興縣五等侯。

translations.literal: For merit in establishing the righteous cause he was enfeoffed as Marquis of the fifth rank of Shixing county.
translations.idiomatic: For his service in founding the restoration he was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Marquis of Shixing county.

sentences.zh: 又參高祖車騎、中軍軍事。

translations.literal: He also served on the staffs of the High Ancestor's Chariots-and-Cavalry and Central Army commands.
translations.idiomatic: He also held staff posts on the High Ancestor's Chariots-and-Cavalry and Central Army headquarters.

sentences.zh: 高祖將征廣固，議者多不同。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor was about to campaign against Guanggu, many in council disagreed.
translations.idiomatic: When the High Ancestor prepared to campaign against Guanggu, many at court opposed the plan.

sentences.zh: 熹從容言曰：「公若淩威北境，拯其塗炭，寧一六合，未為無期。」

translations.literal: Xi said calmly: "If my lord displays his might on the northern frontier and rescues the people from their misery, to bring peace to all under heaven is not beyond reach."
translations.idiomatic: Xi spoke calmly: "If you carry your authority to the northern marches and deliver the people from their suffering, to unite the realm need not lie far off."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「卿言是也。」

translations.literal: The High Ancestor said: "Your words are right."
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor said, "You are right."

sentences.zh: 及行，熹求從，不許，以為建威將軍、臨海太守。

translations.literal: When the army marched, Xi asked to accompany it but was not permitted; he was made General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: When the army set out, Xi asked to go along but was refused; instead he was appointed General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 郡經兵寇，百不存一，熹綏緝綱紀，招聚流散，歸之者千餘家。

translations.literal: The commandery had suffered military ravages and scarcely one household in a hundred remained; Xi restored order and discipline, gathered the displaced, and more than a thousand families returned.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery had been ravaged by war until scarcely one household in a hundred survived. Xi restored law and order, gathered the displaced, and brought back more than a thousand families.

sentences.zh: 孫季高海道襲廣州，路由臨海，熹資給發遣，得以無乏。

translations.literal: Sun Jigao raided Guangzhou by sea; his route passed through Linhai, and Xi supplied and dispatched him so that he wanted for nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Jigao struck Guangzhou by sea, his fleet passed through Linhai; Xi provisioned and sent him on so that the expedition never lacked supplies.

sentences.zh: 徵拜散騎常侍，母憂去職。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Regular Palace Attendant, then left office on account of his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as Regular Palace Attendant but resigned when his mother died.

sentences.zh: 頃之，討劉毅，起為寧朔將軍，從征。

translations.literal: Before long, in the campaign against Liu Yi, he was recalled as General Who Pacifies the North and accompanied the expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, when Liu Yi was attacked, he was recalled from mourning as General Who Pacifies the North and joined the campaign.

sentences.zh: 事平，高祖遣朱齡石統大眾伐蜀，命熹奇兵出中水，以本號領建平、巴東二郡太守。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, the High Ancestor sent Zhu Lingshi to command a great host against Shu, ordering Xi to lead a striking force out by the Zhong River, and with his existing title to hold concurrently the administrations of Jianping and Badong.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory the High Ancestor sent Zhu Lingshi at the head of a great army against Shu and ordered Xi to take an elite column down the Zhong River, retaining his rank while serving concurrently as Administrator of Jianping and Badong.

sentences.zh: 蜀主譙縱遣大將譙撫之萬餘人屯牛脾，又遣譙小苟重兵塞打鼻。

translations.literal: The lord of Shu, Qiao Zong, sent the great general Qiao Fuzhi with more than ten thousand men to camp at Niupi, and also sent Qiao Xiaogou with a heavy force to block Dani.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zong of Shu sent his general Qiao Fuzhi with more than ten thousand men to hold Niupi and dispatched Qiao Xiaogou with a strong force to block the Dani pass.

sentences.zh: 熹至牛脾，撫之戰敗退走，追斬之。

translations.literal: When Xi reached Niupi, Fuzhi was defeated and fled; Xi pursued and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi reached Niupi, routed Fuzhi in battle, pursued him, and cut off his head.

sentences.zh: 小苟聞撫之死，即便奔散。

translations.literal: When Xiaogou heard of Fuzhi's death, his troops at once scattered in flight.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaogou learned that Fuzhi was dead, his army broke and fled at once.

sentences.zh: 成都既平，熹遇疾。

translations.literal: After Chengdu was pacified, Xi fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: After Chengdu had fallen, Xi fell gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 義熙九年，卒於蜀郡牛脾縣，時年三十九。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yixi he died in Niupi county, Shu commandery, at the age of thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yixi he died at Niupi in Shu commandery, aged thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 追贈光祿勳。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 質年始出三十，屢居名郡，涉獵史籍，尺牘便敏，既有氣幹，好言兵權。

translations.literal: Zhi had just passed thirty; he had repeatedly held famous commanderies, ranged through historical records, was quick and adept with documents, possessed force of character, and loved to discourse on military authority.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi had only just turned thirty, yet he had already held several prestigious prefectures, read widely in history, and wrote dispatches with ease. Bold in temperament, he delighted in talk of strategy and command.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂可大任，欲以為益州事，未行，徵為使持節、都督徐、兗二州諸軍事、寧遠將軍、徐、兗二州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen judged that he could bear heavy responsibility and wished to put him in charge of Yi Province affairs; before this was carried out, he was summoned as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Xu and Yan provinces, General of Distant Peace, and Inspector of Xu and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen considered him fit for great trust and intended to place him in charge of Yi Province, but before that appointment took effect he was recalled as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, supreme commander of Xu and Yan, General of Distant Peace, and Inspector of both provinces.

sentences.zh: 在鎮奢費，爵命無章，為有司所糾，遇赦。

translations.literal: While in his province he was extravagant in expenditure and irregular in bestowing ranks and appointments; the responsible officials impeached him, but he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In his provincial post he spent lavishly and handed out titles without proper warrant. The censorate impeached him, but he received an amnesty.

sentences.zh: 與范曄、徐湛之等厚善，曄謀反，量質必與之同，會事發，復為建威將軍、義興太守。

translations.literal: He was on close terms with Fan Ye, Xu Chengzhi, and others; when Ye plotted rebellion, it was judged that Zhi would surely join him, but the plot was exposed in time, and Zhi was again made General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: He was intimate with Fan Ye, Xu Chengzhi, and their circle. When Ye conspired to rebel, the court assumed Zhi would side with him, but the plot was uncovered in time and Zhi was merely restored to his post as General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十六年，太祖謁京陵，質朝丹徒，與何勗、檀和之竝功臣子，時共上禮。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia, when Emperor Wen visited the capital tombs, Zhi presented himself at Dantu; together with He Qian, Tan Hezhi, and other sons of meritorious ministers, they all offered tribute at that time.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia, when Emperor Wen paid homage at the imperial tombs near the capital, Zhi came to Dantu to attend court. He and He Qian, Tan Hezhi, and other sons of founding ministers together presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 太祖設燕盡歡，賜布千匹。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen held a banquet and enjoyed himself to the full, bestowing a thousand bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave a feast at which all rejoiced freely and granted them a thousand bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 二十七年春，遷南譙王義宣司馬、寧朔將軍、南平內史。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-seventh year he was transferred to be Chief Administrator to Prince Yi of Nanqiao, General Who Pacifies the North, and Interior Secretary of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-seventh year he was promoted to Chief Administrator on the staff of Prince Yi of Nanqiao, made General Who Pacifies the North, and appointed Interior Secretary of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 未之職，會索虜大帥拓跋燾圍汝南，汝南戍主陳憲固守告急。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post, it happened that the great chief of the northern enemy, Tuoba Tao, besieged Runan; the garrison commander Chen Xian held firm and sent an urgent appeal.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the new post, the northern enemy's paramount leader Tuoba Tao besieged Runan. The garrison commander Chen Xian held the city and sent desperate appeals for relief.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣質輕往壽陽，即統彼軍，與安蠻司馬劉康祖等救憲。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen sent Zhi swiftly to Shouyang, there to take command at once of that army, and with the Pacification of the Barbarians staff officer Liu Kangzu and others to rescue Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen dispatched Zhi posthaste to Shouyang to assume immediate command of the forces there and, together with Liu Kangzu, staff officer of the Pacification of the Barbarians command, to relieve Xian.

sentences.zh: 虜退走，因使質伐汝南西境刀壁等山蠻，大破之，獲萬餘口，遷太子左衛率。

translations.literal: The barbarians retreated; he was then sent to attack the mountain tribes of Daobi and the like on the western border of Runan, inflicted a great defeat, and captured more than ten thousand persons; he was promoted to Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy withdrew, and Zhi was then ordered to campaign against the mountain tribes at Daobi and elsewhere on Runan's western marches. He routed them utterly, taking more than ten thousand captives, and was promoted to Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard.

sentences.zh: 坐前伐蠻，枉殺隊主嚴祖，又納面首生口，不以送臺，免官。

translations.literal: On account of the earlier campaign against the tribes—having wrongly killed the platoon chief Yan Zu, and having taken handsome captives without sending them to the capital—he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of office because, during the tribal campaign, he had unjustly executed the platoon chief Yan Zu and kept handsome captives for himself instead of forwarding them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 是時上大舉北討，質白衣與驃騎司馬王方回等率軍出許、洛，安北司馬王玄謨攻滑臺，不拔，質請乘驛代將，太祖不許。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor launched a great northern expedition; Zhi, in plain dress, with the Rapid Cavalry staff officer Wang Fanghui and others led troops out toward Xu and Luoyang; the Pacification of the North staff officer Wang Xuemo attacked Huatai but could not take it; Zhi asked to ride post relays and replace the commander, but Emperor Wen did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The court then mounted a major northern offensive. Though out of office, Zhi served in commoner's dress alongside Wang Fanghui, staff officer to the Rapid Cavalry general, leading troops toward Xu and Luoyang, while Wang Xuemo attacked Huatai without success. Zhi asked to ride post-horses and replace the failing commander, but Emperor Wen refused.

sentences.zh: 虜侵徐、豫，拓跋燾率大眾數十萬遂向彭城，以質為輔國將軍、假節、置佐，率萬人北救。

translations.literal: The barbarians invaded Xu and Yu; Tuoba Tao led a great host of several hundred thousand straight toward Pengcheng; Zhi was made General Who Supports the State, with provisional staff and insignia, and led ten thousand men north to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy overran Xu and Yu, Tuoba Tao marched several hundred thousand men directly on Pengcheng. Zhi was appointed General Who Supports the State with provisional insignia and a full staff, and led ten thousand men north to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 始至盱眙，燾已過淮，冗從僕射胡崇之領質府司馬，崇之副太子積弩將軍毛熙祚亦受統於質。

translations.literal: When he had just reached Xuyi, Tao had already crossed the Huai; the Supernumerary Attendant Hu Chongzhi headed Zhi's headquarters as Chief Administrator; Chongzhi's deputy, the Crown Prince's Accumulated Crossbows General Mao Xizuo, was also placed under Zhi's command.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi had only just reached Xuyi when Tao was already south of the Huai. Hu Chongzhi, Supernumerary Attendant and chief of Zhi's staff, served under him, as did Mao Xizuo, General of Accumulated Crossbows to the Crown Prince, who was Chongzhi's deputy.

sentences.zh: 盱眙城東有高山，質慮虜據之，使崇之、澄之二軍營於山上，質營城南。

translations.literal: East of Xuyi city there was a high mountain; fearing the enemy would seize it, Zhi had the two armies of Chongzhi and Chengzhi camp on the mountain, while he encamped south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: A high hill lay east of Xuyi, and fearing the enemy would occupy it, Zhi posted the divisions of Chongzhi and Chengzhi on the summit while he made his own camp south of the walls.

sentences.zh: 虜攻崇之、澄之二營，崇之等力戰不敵，眾散，並為虜所殺。

translations.literal: The enemy attacked the two camps of Chongzhi and Chengzhi; Chongzhi and the others fought fiercely but could not withstand them; their forces scattered and all were killed by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy assaulted the camps on the hill. Chongzhi and his men fought hard but were overwhelmed; their troops broke, and all were slain.

sentences.zh: 虜又攻熙祚，熙祚所領悉北府精兵，幢主李灌率厲將士，殺賊甚多。

translations.literal: The enemy next attacked Xizuo; those under Xizuo's command were all elite troops of the Northern Headquarters; the banner chief Li Guan roused the officers and men and killed a great many of the foe.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy then turned on Xizuo, whose command consisted entirely of crack Northern Headquarters troops. The banner chief Li Guan exhorted his men and killed a great many of the attackers.

sentences.zh: 隊主周胤之、外監楊方生又率射賊，賊垂退，會熙祚被創死，軍遂散亂。

translations.literal: The platoon chief Zhou Yinzhi and the outer inspector Yang Fangsheng also led archers against the enemy; the foe was on the verge of retreat when Xizuo was wounded and died, and the army thereupon fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Platoon chief Zhou Yinzhi and outer inspector Yang Fangsheng led bowmen against the foe as well, and the enemy was nearly driven off—until Xizuo was struck down and killed, whereupon that wing collapsed in disorder.

sentences.zh: 其日質案兵不敢救，故二營一時覆沒。

translations.literal: That day Zhi held his troops in check and dared not go to the rescue, and so the two camps were destroyed at once.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Zhi held his main force back and would not commit it to the rescue, so both outlying camps were lost together.

sentences.zh: 初，仇池之平也，以崇之為龍驤將軍、北秦州刺史，宋百頃，行至濁水，為索虜所克，舉軍敗散；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chouchi was pacified, Chongzhi had been made Dragon-soaring General and Inspector of Northern Qin, with a fief of a hundred qing in Song territory; marching as far as Zhuoshui, he was overcome by the northern enemy and his whole army was defeated and scattered;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after the pacification of Chouchi, Chongzhi had been made Dragon-Soaring General and Inspector of Northern Qin, with a fief of a hundred qing within Song territory. Marching as far as Zhuoshui, he was crushed by the northern enemy and his entire force scattered;

sentences.zh: 崇之及將佐以下，皆為虜所執，後得叛還，至是又為虜所敗焉。

translations.literal: Chongzhi and his officers and staff down to the lowest ranks were all captured by the enemy; later he escaped and returned, and now he was again defeated by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi and all his officers and men were taken prisoner, though he later escaped and made his way back—only to be defeated by the enemy once more on this occasion.

sentences.zh: 熙祚，司州刺史脩之兄子也。

translations.literal: Xizuo was a nephew of Xiu, Inspector of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: Xizuo was the nephew of Mao Xiu, Inspector of Si province.

sentences.zh: 崇之、熙祚並贈正員郎；

translations.literal: Chongzhi and Xizuo were both posthumously awarded the rank of Regular Gentleman;
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi and Xizuo were both posthumously granted the rank of Regular Gentleman of the Palace;

sentences.zh: 澄之事在祖父燾傳。

translations.literal: The affair of Chengzhi is set forth in the biography of the clan elder Tao.
translations.idiomatic: The account of Chengzhi appears in the biography of his kinsman Zang Tao.

sentences.zh: 三營既敗，其夕質軍亦奔散，棄輜重器甲，單七百人投盱眙。

translations.literal: After the three camps were defeated, that same evening Zhi's army also fled in disorder, abandoning baggage, heavy equipment, and armor; only seven hundred men threw themselves into Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Once all three camps had fallen, Zhi's own army broke that same night. He abandoned wagons, heavy gear, and armor and fled into Xuyi with only seven hundred men.

sentences.zh: 盱眙太守沈璞完為守戰之備，城內有實力三千，質大喜，因共守。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Xuyi, Shen Pu, had made complete preparations for defense; within the city there were three thousand seasoned troops; Zhi was greatly pleased and joined in the defense.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Pu, Administrator of Xuyi, had made thorough preparations for a siege. Three thousand seasoned troops stood within the walls, and Zhi was overjoyed to join him in the defense.

sentences.zh: 虜初南出，後無資糧，唯以百姓為命。

translations.literal: When the enemy first marched south, they had no supplies in the rear and relied solely on the common people for their livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: When the invaders first marched south they had brought no stores with them and lived entirely off the countryside.

sentences.zh: 及過淮，食平越、石鱉二屯穀，至是抄掠無所，人馬饑困，聞盱眙有積粟，欲以為歸路之資。

translations.literal: After crossing the Huai they ate the grain of the Pingyue and Shibie garrisons; by now there was nothing left to plunder, men and horses were famished and exhausted, and hearing that Xuyi had stored grain, they wished to make it the resource for their homeward road.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Huai they consumed the grain of the Pingyue and Shibie stockades, but now there was nothing left to seize and men and horses were starving. Learning that Xuyi held great stores of grain, they meant to seize it to sustain their retreat.

sentences.zh: 既破崇之等，一攻城不拔，便引眾南向。

translations.literal: Having already defeated Chongzhi and the others, they assaulted the city once but could not take it, and then led their masses southward.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating Chongzhi's force they assaulted the city once, failed to take it, and marched their main body southward.

sentences.zh: 城內增修守備，莫不完嚴。

translations.literal: Within the city they further strengthened the defenses, until nothing was left incomplete or lax.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the walls the defenders redoubled every preparation until the fortifications were impregnable.

sentences.zh: 二十八年正月初，燾自廣陵北返，便悉力攻盱眙，就質求酒，質封溲便與之。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of the twenty-eighth year, Tao returned north from Guangling and at once threw all his strength against Xuyi; he asked Zhi for wine, and Zhi sealed urine in a vessel and sent it to him.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the first month of the twenty-eighth year Tao turned back north from Guangling and threw his full strength against Xuyi. He asked Zhi for wine; Zhi sent him a jar sealed full of urine instead.

sentences.zh: 燾怒甚，築長圍，一夜便合，開攻道，趣城東北，運東山土石填之。

translations.literal: Tao was furious; he built a long encirclement that was joined in a single night, opened assault trenches toward the northeast of the city, and hauled earth and stone from East Hill to fill them in.
translations.idiomatic: Tao flew into a rage, threw up a continuous siege line overnight, opened assault trenches against the northeast wall, and hauled in earth and stone from East Hill to fill them.

sentences.zh: 虜又恐城內水路遁走，乃引大船，欲於君山作浮橋，以絕淮道。

translations.literal: The enemy also feared that the city might escape by water routes; they therefore brought up great ships and wished to build a pontoon bridge at Jun Hill to cut off the Huai route.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that the garrison might slip away by water, the enemy brought up large ships and tried to span the Huai with a pontoon bridge at Jun Hill.

sentences.zh: 城內乘艦逆戰，大破之。

translations.literal: Within the city they took ships to meet them in battle and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders sortied in war junks and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 明旦，賊更方舫為桁，桁上各嚴兵自衛。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day the enemy lashed boats side by side into rafts, and on each raft they stationed troops in tight array for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the next day the enemy lashed their boats into square platforms, each manned by a dense guard.

sentences.zh: 城內更擊不能禁，遂於軍山立桁，水陸路竝斷。

translations.literal: The city forces attacked again but could not stop them; they then erected rafts at Jun Hill, and both water and land routes were cut off together.
translations.idiomatic: Another sortie from the city could not break them, and the enemy finally anchored their platforms at Jun Hill, severing the garrison's routes by both land and water.

sentences.zh: 燾與質書曰：「吾今所遣鬥兵，盡非我國人，城東北是丁零與胡，南是三秦氐、羌。

translations.literal: Tao wrote to Zhi: "The fighting men I now send are none of them natives of my state; northeast of the city are Dingling and Hu, south are Di and Qiang of the Three Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Tao wrote to Zhi: "The assault troops I am sending now are none of them my own countrymen. Northeast of your city are Dingling and Hu; to the south are Di and Qiang from the Three Qin.

sentences.zh: 設使丁零死者，正可減常山、趙郡賊；

translations.literal: If Dingling should die, that would only reduce the bandits of Changshan and Zhao commanderies;
translations.idiomatic: If the Dingling die, you will only have cut down the brigands of Changshan and Zhao;

sentences.zh: 胡死，正減并州賊；

translations.literal: if Hu die, that would only reduce the bandits of Bing province;
translations.idiomatic: if the Hu die, you will only have cut down the brigands of Bing province;

sentences.zh: 氐、羌死，正減關中賊。

translations.literal: if Di and Qiang die, that would only reduce the bandits of Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: if the Di and Qiang die, you will only have cut down the brigands of the Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 卿若殺丁零、胡，無不利。」

translations.literal: If you, sir, kill Dingling and Hu, nothing but advantage will come of it."
translations.idiomatic: If you slaughter the Dingling and the Hu, you lose nothing by it."

sentences.zh: 質答書曰：「省示，具悉姦懷。

translations.literal: Zhi replied in a letter: "I have read your communication and fully understand your treacherous intent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi wrote back: "I have read your letter and understand your treacherous mind perfectly.

sentences.zh: 爾自恃四腳，屢犯國疆，諸如此事，不可具說。

translations.literal: You rely on your four legs and have repeatedly violated our state's borders; matters such as these cannot all be recounted.
translations.idiomatic: You trust in your four-legged mounts and have violated our borders again and again—there is no end to such offenses.

sentences.zh: 王玄謨退于東，梁坦散於西，爾謂何以？

translations.literal: Wang Xuemo retreated in the east and Liang Tan was scattered in the west—what do you make of that?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuemo was driven back in the east and Liang Tan routed in the west—what do you make of that?

sentences.zh: 不聞童謠言邪：『虜馬飲江水，佛狸死卯年。』

translations.literal: Have you not heard what the children's rhyme says: 'The barbarians' horses drink the river's water; Foli dies in a mao year.
translations.idiomatic: Have you never heard the children's rhyme? 'The barbarians' horses will drink the Yangzi; Foli will die in a mao year.

sentences.zh: 此期未至，以二軍開飲江之徑爾，冥期使然，非復人事。

translations.literal: That term has not yet arrived; it is only because your two armies opened the path for drinking the river—destiny ordains it, no longer a matter of human agency.
translations.idiomatic: That hour has not yet come; your two armies have merely opened the way for the horses to drink the river. Fate decrees it—this is no longer in human hands.

sentences.zh: 寡人受命相滅，期之白登，師行未遠，爾自送死，豈容復令生全，饗有桑乾哉！

translations.literal: I have received Heaven's mandate to destroy you in turn; I fix my term at Baideng; the army has not marched far, yet you deliver yourselves to death—how could I again allow you to live whole and feast on the Sanggan!
translations.idiomatic: I have received Heaven's mandate to destroy you. I have marked Baideng as the place and the hour. Your army has scarcely marched, yet you rush to your deaths—how could I let you live to feast again on the Sanggan!

sentences.zh: 但爾往攻此城，假令寡人不能殺爾，爾由我而死。

translations.literal: Only go on and attack this city; even if I cannot kill you, you will die by my hand.
translations.idiomatic: Go on and assault this city. Even if I cannot kill you myself, you will die by my doing.

sentences.zh: 爾若有幸，得為亂兵所殺。

translations.literal: If you are fortunate, you will be killed by disorderly troops.
translations.idiomatic: If you are lucky, you will be cut down in the confusion of battle.

sentences.zh: 爾若不幸，則生相剿縛，載以一驢，直送都市。

translations.literal: If you are unfortunate, you will be taken alive, bound, loaded on a donkey, and sent straight to the capital market.
translations.idiomatic: If you are unlucky, you will be taken alive, trussed up, loaded on a donkey, and hauled straight to the execution ground at the capital.

sentences.zh: 我本不圖全，若天地無靈，力屈於爾，齏之粉之，屠之裂之，如此未足謝本朝。

translations.literal: I never planned to come back whole; if Heaven and Earth are without spirit and my strength is broken before you, to grind you to powder, to mince you fine, to slaughter and rend you—such would still not suffice to answer to our dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: I never expected to return unscathed. If Heaven and Earth have lost their power and I am broken before you, then to grind you to dust, mince you fine, slaughter and rend you—even that would not be enough to answer to my dynasty.

sentences.zh: 爾識智及眾力，豈能勝苻堅邪！

translations.literal: Your wisdom and the mass of your strength—can they surpass Fu Jian!
translations.idiomatic: With all your wit and all your troops, do you imagine you surpass Fu Jian!

sentences.zh: 頃年展爾陸梁者，是爾未飲江，太歲未卯年故爾。

translations.literal: The reason you have strutted about these recent years is that you had not yet drunk the river, and the Year Star had not reached a mao year.
translations.idiomatic: The only reason you have strutted about these past years is that your horses had not yet drunk the river and the Year Star had not yet reached a mao year.

sentences.zh: 斛蘭昔深入彭城，值少日雨，隻馬不返，爾豈憶邪？

translations.literal: Hulan once penetrated deeply to Pengcheng; he met with a few days of rain, and not a single horse returned—do you not recall?
translations.idiomatic: Remember Hulan's deep raid on Pengcheng? A few days of rain, and not one horse came back—have you forgotten?

sentences.zh: 即時春雨已降，四方大眾，始就雲集，爾但安意攻城莫走。

translations.literal: Right now the spring rains have already fallen, and great hosts from the four quarters are beginning to gather like clouds; you need only set your mind at ease in attacking the city and do not flee.
translations.idiomatic: The spring rains are already falling, and great armies from every quarter are gathering like clouds. Set your mind at ease, keep assaulting the city, and do not run.

sentences.zh: 糧食闕乏者告之，當出廩相飴。

translations.literal: Those who lack food and grain should report it; I will open the granaries and feed you.
translations.idiomatic: If you run short of grain, say so—I will open the granaries and feed you myself.

sentences.zh: 得所送劍刀，欲令我揮之爾身邪！

translations.literal: Having received the swords and blades you sent—do you wish me to wield them upon your persons!
translations.idiomatic: You sent me swords and blades—do you want me to use them on you in person?

sentences.zh: 甚苦，人附反，各自努力，無煩多云。」

translations.literal: It is very wearisome; men are turning back on their own—each exert yourselves; no need for more idle words."
translations.idiomatic: Enough of this. Your own men are already deserting. Do your best—no need for more words."

sentences.zh: 是時虜中童謠曰：「軺車北來如穿雉，不意虜馬飲江水。

translations.literal: At that time a children's rhyme in the enemy camp ran: "Light carriages come from the north like piercing pheasants; who expected the barbarians' horses to drink the river's water.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a children's rhyme circulating in the enemy camp ran: "Light carriages come from the north like bolts through a pheasant—who dreamed the barbarians' horses would drink the Yangzi?

sentences.zh: 虜主北歸石濟死，虜欲渡江天不徙。」

translations.literal: When the barbarian lord returns north, Shiji will die; when the barbarians wish to cross the river, Heaven will not shift."
translations.idiomatic: When the barbarian lord turns north, Shiji will die; when the barbarians try to cross the river, Heaven itself will not move."

sentences.zh: 故質答引之。

translations.literal: Therefore Zhi cited it in his reply.
translations.idiomatic: This was the prophecy Zhi quoted in his reply.

sentences.zh: 燾大怒，乃作鐵床，於其上施鐵鑱，云破城得質，當坐之此上。

translations.literal: Tao was furious; he had an iron bed made, fitted with iron spikes upon it, declaring that if the city were taken and Zhi captured, he would be made to sit upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Tao was beside himself with rage. He had an iron bed built and fitted with iron spikes, vowing that if the city fell and Zhi was taken alive, he would be impaled upon it.

sentences.zh: 質又與虜眾書曰：「示詔虜中諸士庶：狸伐見與書如別，等正朔之民，何為力自取如此。

translations.literal: Zhi also wrote to the enemy masses: "Proclamation to all gentlemen and commoners among the barbarians: Liba has sent a letter as attached; you are subjects of the true calendar—why exert yourselves to bring such suffering on yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi also addressed the enemy host: "To all officers and commoners among you: 'Liba' has written as attached. You are people of the true calendar—why struggle so hard to destroy yourselves?

sentences.zh: 大丈夫豈可不知轉禍為福邪！

translations.literal: Can a true man not know how to turn calamity into blessing!
translations.idiomatic: Surely a true man knows how to turn disaster into good fortune!

sentences.zh: 今寫臺格如別書，自思之。」

translations.literal: I now copy out the court's register as in the attached document—ponder it yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: I enclose the court's price list as in the attached notice—think it over for yourselves."

sentences.zh: 時購斬燾封開國縣侯，食邑一萬戶，賜布絹各萬匹。

translations.literal: At that time a bounty was posted for beheading Tao, with enfeoffment as Marquis of a founding county, a fief of ten thousand households, and gifts of ten thousand bolts each of cloth and silk.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court offered a reward for Tao's head: enfeoffment as Marquis of a founding county with a fief of ten thousand households, plus ten thousand bolts each of cloth and silk.

sentences.zh: 虜以鉤車鉤垣樓，城內繋以驅絙，數百人叫喚引之，車不能退。

translations.literal: The enemy used hook-carts to hook the parapet towers; within the city they tied on thick ropes, and several hundred men shouted and hauled, but the carts could not be pulled back.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy sent up hook-carts to seize the parapet towers. The defenders lashed on heavy ropes, and several hundred men hauled and shouted together until the enemy's machines could not be withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 既夜，以木桶盛人，懸出城外，截其鉤獲之。

translations.literal: When night came, they placed men in wooden tubs, lowered them outside the walls, cut off the hooks, and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: That night men were lowered outside the walls in wooden tubs, cut off the hooks, and brought them back into the city.

sentences.zh: 明日，又以衝車攻城，城土堅密，每至，頹落不過數升。

translations.literal: The next day they again used battering rams against the city; the wall earth was firm and dense, and each time they struck, no more than a few sheng of material crumbled away.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the enemy brought up battering rams again. The ramparts were so solid that each blow loosened no more than a few handfuls of earth.

sentences.zh: 虜乃肉薄登城，分番相代，墜而復升，莫有退者，殺傷萬計，虜死者與城平。

translations.literal: The enemy then pressed close to scale the walls, rotating in relays by shift; fallen men climbed again—none retreated. Casualties numbered in the tens of thousands, and enemy dead piled level with the walls.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy then pressed in close under the walls and climbed up in relay shifts. Men who fell climbed again; none fell back. Casualties ran into the tens of thousands, and the enemy dead piled as high as the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 又射殺高梁王。

translations.literal: They also shot and killed the Prince of Gaoliang.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders also shot and killed the Prince of Gaoliang.

sentences.zh: 如此三旬，死者過半。

translations.literal: After thirty days like this, more than half were dead.
translations.idiomatic: After thirty days of this, more than half the attackers were dead.

sentences.zh: 燾聞彭城斷其歸路，京邑遣水軍自海入淮，且疾疫死者甚眾。

translations.literal: Tao heard that Pengcheng had cut off his line of retreat, that the capital had sent a naval force from the sea into the Huai, and that plague deaths were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Tao learned that Pengcheng had severed his retreat, that the capital had dispatched a fleet from the sea into the Huai River, and that plague was killing men in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 二月二日，乃解圍遁走。

translations.literal: On the second day of the second month, he then lifted the siege and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day of the second month he raised the siege and fled.

sentences.zh: 上嘉質功，以為使持節、監雍、梁、南、北秦四州諸軍事、冠軍將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史，封開國子，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: The emperor commended Zhi's merit and appointed him Envoy Bearing the Staff, Supervisor of Military Affairs for the four provinces of Yong, Liang, Southern Qin, and Northern Qin, Champion General, Colonel Quieting the Barbarians, and Governor of Yong Province, enfeoffing him as Viscount of a Founding State with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Zhi's achievement and appointed him Bearer of the Staff of Authority, supervisor of military affairs for Yong, Liang, Southern Qin, and Northern Qin, Champion General, Colonel Quieting the Barbarians, and Governor of Yong Province, enfeoffing him as Viscount of a Founding State with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 明年，太祖又北伐，使質率所統見力向潼關，質頓兵近郊，不肯時發，獨遣司馬柳元景屯兵境上，不時進軍。

translations.literal: The next year the High Ancestor again marched north and ordered Zhi to lead his available forces toward Tong Pass. Zhi halted his army in the suburbs and refused to set out on schedule, sending only his Chief of Staff Liu Yuanjing to encamp on the border without advancing promptly.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Emperor Wen marched north again and ordered Zhi to lead his available troops toward Tong Pass. Zhi halted in the suburbs and would not move on time, sending only his chief of staff Liu Yuanjing to camp on the frontier without pressing the advance.

sentences.zh: 質又顧戀嬖妾，棄營單馬還城，散用臺庫見錢六七百萬，為有司所糾，上不問也。

translations.literal: Zhi also doted on a favorite concubine, abandoned camp and rode alone back to the city, spending freely six or seven million cash from the treasury stores on hand. Supervisory officials censured him, but the emperor did not inquire into it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi also clung to a favorite concubine, abandoned camp, and rode back to the city alone, squandering six or seven million cash from the imperial treasury. The supervisory offices censured him, but the emperor did not pursue the matter.

sentences.zh: 元兇弑立，以質為丹陽尹，加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: When the usurper Shao seized the throne by regicide, he made Zhi Governor of Danyang and added the title General Who Subdues the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: After the usurper Shao murdered his way to the throne, he appointed Zhi Governor of Danyang and added the title General Who Subdues the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 質家遣門生師顗報質，具太祖崩問。

translations.literal: Zhi's household sent his retainer Shi Yan to report to Zhi with full details of the High Ancestor's death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's household sent his retainer Shi Yan to inform him with full particulars of Emperor Wen's death.

sentences.zh: 質疏顗所言，馳告司空義宣，又遣州祭酒從事田穎起銜命報世祖，率眾五千，馳下討逆，自陽口進江陵義宣。

translations.literal: Zhi kept Shi Yan's report at arm's length, galloped to inform the Minister of Works Yi Xuan, and also dispatched the provincial Libationer-attendant Tian Ying bearing sealed orders to report to Emperor Xiaowu. Leading five thousand men, he raced down to punish the usurper and advanced from Yangkou toward Jiangling to join Yi Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi treated Shi Yan's report with reserve, galloped to inform Prince Yi of Nanqiao, Minister of Works Yi Xuan, and also sent the provincial libationer-attendant Tian Ying with sealed orders to report to Emperor Xiaowu. Leading five thousand men, he raced south to punish the usurper and advanced from Yangkou toward Jiangling to join Yi Xuan.

sentences.zh: 質諸子在都邑，聞質舉義，並逃亡。

translations.literal: When Zhi's sons in the capital heard that their father had risen in righteous arms, they all fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's sons in the capital, hearing that their father had taken up arms in the righteous cause, all fled.

sentences.zh: 劭欲相慰悅，乃下書曰：「臧敦等無因自駭，急便竄逸，迷昧過甚，良可怪歎。

translations.literal: Shao wished to reassure and win him over, and issued a letter saying: "Zang Dun and the others, without cause, frightened themselves and fled in haste—their confusion is excessive and truly lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shao tried to soothe and win Zhi over and issued a letter saying, "Zang Dun and the others, without cause, panicked and bolted—their confusion is extreme and truly deplorable.

sentences.zh: 質國戚勳臣，忠誠篤亮，方當顯位，贊翼京輦，而子弟波迸，傷其乃懷。

translations.literal: Zhi is a royal kinsman and meritorious minister, loyal and steadfast; he should soon hold high office and assist the capital, yet his sons have scattered—I am grieved at this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi is a royal kinsman and meritorious minister, loyal and upright, soon to hold high office and assist the capital, yet his sons have scattered—I am grieved at heart.

sentences.zh: 可遣宣譬令還，咸復本位。」

translations.literal: Send messengers to explain and summon them back; all shall resume their former posts."
translations.idiomatic: Send messengers to explain and call them back; all shall return to their former posts."

sentences.zh: 劭尋錄得敦，使大將軍義恭行訓杖三十，厚給賜之。

translations.literal: Shao soon tracked down Dun, had the Grand General Yigong administer thirty strokes of disciplinary punishment, and richly rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: Shao soon tracked down Dun, had Grand General Liu Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, administer thirty strokes of disciplinary punishment, and richly rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 義宣得質報，即日舉兵，馳信報世祖，板進質號征北將軍。

translations.literal: When Yi Xuan received Zhi's report, he raised troops that same day, sent urgent word to Emperor Xiaowu, and by provisional commission promoted Zhi to General Who Campaigns North.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi Xuan received Zhi's report, he raised troops that same day, sent urgent word to Emperor Xiaowu, and by provisional commission promoted Zhi to General Who Campaigns North.

sentences.zh: 質逕赴尋陽，與世祖同下。

translations.literal: Zhi went straight to Xunyang and descended together with Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi went straight to Xunyang and marched downstream together with Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 世祖至新亭即位，以質為都督江州諸軍事、車騎將軍、開府儀同三司、江州刺史，加散騎常侍，持節如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu reached Xinting and took the throne, he appointed Zhi Commander of Military Affairs for Jiang Province, Chariots-and-Cavalry General, Grand Master with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Jiang Province, adding Senior Adjunct in the Palace Secretariat, with Bearer of the Staff as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu reached Xinting and took the throne, he appointed Zhi commander of military affairs for Jiang Province, Chariots-and-Cavalry General, Grand Master with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Jiang Province, adding Senior Adjunct in the Palace Secretariat and retaining Bearer of the Staff of Authority.

sentences.zh: 使質率所領自白下步上，直至廣莫門，門者不守。

translations.literal: He ordered Zhi to lead his troops on foot from Baixia straight to the Gate of Broad Darkness; the gate guards did not hold.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Zhi to lead his troops on foot from Baixia straight to the Gate of Broad Darkness; the gate guards offered no resistance.

sentences.zh: 薛安都、程天祚等亦自南掖門入，與質同會太極殿，生禽元兇。

translations.literal: Xue Andu, Cheng Tianzuo, and others also entered through the Southern Flank Gate; they joined Zhi at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate and captured the usurper Shao alive.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Andu, Cheng Tianzuo, and others also entered through the Southern Flank Gate, joined Zhi at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, and captured the usurper Shao alive.

sentences.zh: 仍使質留守朝堂，甲仗百人自防。

translations.literal: Zhi was then left to guard the audience hall, with a hundred men in armor as his personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was then left to guard the audience hall, with a hundred armored men as his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 封始興郡公，食邑三千戶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Shixing commandery with a fief of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Shixing commandery with a fief of three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 之鎮，舫千餘乘，部伍前後百餘里，六平乘竝施龍子幡。

translations.literal: When he went to his post, he had more than a thousand boats; his formation stretched more than a hundred li fore and aft; on each of the six ordinary four-horse carriages dragon banners were displayed together.
translations.idiomatic: When he went to his post, his fleet numbered more than a thousand vessels and his column stretched more than a hundred li from van to rear; on each of six ordinary four-horse carriages dragon banners were displayed together.

sentences.zh: 時世祖自攬威柄，而質以少主遇之，是事專行，多所求欲。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xiaowu was personally wielding authority, but Zhi treated him as a young lord; on every matter he acted on his own and made many demands.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Xiaowu was personally wielding authority, but Zhi treated him as a young sovereign; on every matter he acted on his own and made many demands.

sentences.zh: 及至尋陽，刑政慶賞，不復諮稟朝廷。

translations.literal: When he reached Xunyang, punishments, administration, rewards, and grants were no longer referred to the court for approval.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached Xunyang, punishments, administration, rewards, and grants were no longer referred to the court for approval.

sentences.zh: 盆口、鉤圻米，輒散用之，臺符屢加檢詰，質漸猜懼。

translations.literal: He freely distributed the grain stored at Pankou and Gouqi; repeated imperial orders demanded audits, and Zhi grew suspicious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: He freely distributed the grain stored at Pankou and Gouqi; repeated imperial orders demanded audits, and Zhi grew suspicious and afraid.

sentences.zh: 自謂人才足為一世英傑，始聞國禍，便有異圖，以義宣凡闇，易可制勒，欲外相推奉，以成其志。

translations.literal: He considered himself talent enough to be the hero of the age; as soon as he heard of the national calamity he already harbored a separate design, thinking Yi Xuan dull and easily controlled, intending to promote him outwardly to achieve his own aim.
translations.idiomatic: He considered himself talent enough to be the hero of the age; as soon as he heard of the national calamity he already harbored a separate design, thinking Yi Xuan dull and easily controlled, intending to elevate him outwardly to achieve his own aim.

sentences.zh: 及至江陵，便致拜稱名。

translations.literal: When he reached Jiangling, he addressed Yi Xuan with a bow using his personal name.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Jiangling, he bowed to Yi Xuan and addressed him by personal name.

sentences.zh: 質於義宣雖為兄弟，而年大近十歲，義宣驚曰：「君何意拜弟？」

translations.literal: Though Zhi and Yi Xuan were sworn brothers, Zhi was nearly ten years older. Yi Xuan was startled: "Why do you bow to your younger brother?"
translations.idiomatic: Though Zhi and Yi Xuan were sworn brothers, Zhi was nearly ten years older. Yi Xuan was startled and said, "Why do you bow to your younger brother?"

sentences.zh: 質曰：「事中宜然。」

translations.literal: Zhi said: "Under the circumstances this is fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi said, "Under the circumstances this is fitting."

sentences.zh: 時義宣已推崇世祖，故其計不行。

translations.literal: Yi Xuan had already pledged loyalty to Emperor Xiaowu, so his scheme did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Xuan had already pledged loyalty to Emperor Xiaowu, so the scheme did not succeed.

sentences.zh: 質每慮事泄，及至新亭，又拜江夏王義恭，義恭愕然，問質所以。

translations.literal: Zhi always feared the plot would leak; when he reached Xinting he again bowed to Prince Yigong of Jiangxia. Yigong was astonished and asked Zhi his reason.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi always feared the plot would leak out; when he reached Xinting he again bowed to Liu Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia. Yigong was astonished and asked Zhi why.

sentences.zh: 質曰：「天下屯危，禮異常日，前在荊州，亦拜司空。」

translations.literal: Zhi said: "The realm is in dire peril and ritual differs from ordinary days; previously in Jing Province I also bowed to the Minister of Works."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi said, "The realm is in dire peril and ritual differs from ordinary days; previously in Jing Province I also bowed to the Minister of Works."

sentences.zh: 會義宣有憾於世祖，事在義宣傳。

translations.literal: Just then Yi Xuan had grievances against Emperor Xiaowu—the matter is related in Yi Xuan's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Yi Xuan had grievances against Emperor Xiaowu—the matter is related in Yi Xuan's biography.

sentences.zh: 質因此密信說誘，陳朝廷得失。

translations.literal: Zhi therefore sent secret letters to persuade him, setting forth the court's failings and merits.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi therefore sent secret letters to persuade him, setting forth the court's strengths and failings.

sentences.zh: 又謂：「震主之威，不可持久，主相勢均，事不兩立。

translations.literal: He also said: "A power that shakes the ruler cannot last; when sovereign and chief minister are evenly matched, the two cannot stand together.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "A power that shakes the ruler cannot endure; when sovereign and chief minister are evenly matched, the two cannot stand together.

sentences.zh: 今專據閫外，地勝兵強，持疑不決，則後機致禍。」

translations.literal: Now you hold exclusive command beyond the passes, with superior terrain and strong troops; if you hesitate and do not decide, missing your chance will bring disaster."
translations.idiomatic: Now you hold exclusive command beyond the passes, with superior terrain and strong troops; if you hesitate and fail to decide, missing your chance will bring disaster."

sentences.zh: 質女為義宣子采妻，謂質無復異同，納其說。

translations.literal: Zhi's daughter was wife to Yi Xuan's son Cai; he believed Zhi would not again dissent and accepted his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's daughter was married to Yi Xuan's son Liu Cai; believing Zhi would not again dissent, Yi Xuan accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 且義宣腹心將佐蔡超民之徒，咸有富貴之情，願義宣得，欲倚質威名，以成其業，又勸獎義宣。

translations.literal: Moreover Yi Xuan's trusted generals and aides, such as Cai Chaomin, all burned with ambition for wealth and rank; they wished Yi Xuan to prevail and wanted to lean on Zhi's renown to accomplish their enterprise, and they also urged and encouraged Yi Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Yi Xuan's trusted generals and aides, such as Cai Chaomin, all burned with ambition for wealth and rank; they wished Yi Xuan to prevail and wanted to lean on Zhi's renown to accomplish their enterprise, and they also urged and encouraged Yi Xuan.

sentences.zh: 義宣時未受丞相，質子敦為黃門侍郎，奉詔敦勸，道經尋陽，質令敦具更譬說，并言世祖短長，義宣乃意定。

translations.literal: Yi Xuan had not yet accepted the title of Chancellor; Zhi's son Dun, as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, was sent by imperial order to urge him onward. Passing through Xunyang, Zhi had Dun deliver a fuller persuasion and speak of Emperor Xiaowu's strengths and flaws, and Yi Xuan's mind was made up.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Xuan had not yet accepted the title of chancellor; Zhi's son Dun, as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, was sent by imperial order to urge him onward. Passing through Xunyang, Zhi had Dun deliver a fuller persuasion and speak of Emperor Xiaowu's strengths and flaws, and Yi Xuan's mind was made up.

sentences.zh: 馳報豫州刺史魯爽，期孝建元年秋同舉。

translations.literal: He sent urgent word to Lu Shuang, Governor of Yu Province, fixing the autumn of the first year of Xiaojian for a joint rising.
translations.idiomatic: He sent urgent word to Lu Shuang, Governor of Yu Province, fixing the autumn of the first year of Xiaojian for a joint rising.

sentences.zh: 爽失旨，即便起兵。

translations.literal: Lu Shuang fell from favor and immediately raised troops.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shuang had fallen from favor and immediately raised troops.

sentences.zh: 遣人至京邑報弟瑜，瑜席捲奔叛。

translations.literal: He sent men to the capital to inform his brother Yu; Yu gathered his belongings and fled in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He sent men to the capital to inform his brother Yu; Yu packed up and fled in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 瑜弟弘為質府佐，世祖遣報質，質於是執臺使，狼狽舉兵。

translations.literal: Yu's brother Hong served as an aide in Zhi's staff; Emperor Xiaowu sent a messenger to report to Zhi, whereupon Zhi seized the imperial envoy and raised troops in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's brother Hong served as an aide on Zhi's staff; Emperor Xiaowu sent a messenger to report to Zhi, whereupon Zhi seized the imperial envoy and raised troops in haste.

sentences.zh: 上表曰：

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial stating:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial stating:

sentences.zh: 臣聞執藥隨親，非情謬於甘苦；

translations.literal: I have heard that one who administers medicine at a parent's side does not misjudge bitterness and sweetness through mere sentiment;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that one who administers medicine at a parent's side does not misjudge bitterness and sweetness through mere sentiment;

sentences.zh: 揮斤斬毒，豈忘痛於肌膚。

translations.literal: one who swings the axe to cut away poison does not forget the pain to flesh and skin.
translations.idiomatic: one who swings the axe to cut away poison does not forget the pain to flesh and skin.

sentences.zh: 蓋以先疑後順，忠焉必往；

translations.literal: This is because, after initial doubt, loyalty must be pursued;
translations.idiomatic: This is because, after initial doubt, loyalty must be pursued;

sentences.zh: 忍小存大，雖愛必從。

translations.literal: enduring the small to preserve the great—though love is involved, one must comply.
translations.idiomatic: enduring the small to preserve the great—though love is involved, one must comply.

sentences.zh: 丞相臣義宣，育哲台鉉，拊聲聯服，定主勤王之業，勳越乎齊、晉；

translations.literal: Chancellor Yi Xuan has nurtured wisdom from the platform of state, united the realm in harmonious obedience, settled the great enterprise of restoring the ruler, his merit surpassing Qi and Jin;
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Yi Xuan has nurtured wisdom from the platform of state, united the realm in harmonious obedience, settled the great enterprise of restoring the ruler, his merit surpassing Qi and Jin;

sentences.zh: 宗戚懿親之寄，望崇於魯、衛。

translations.literal: entrusted as a kinsman of imperial grace, his standing exceeds that of the states of Lu and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: entrusted as a kinsman of imperial grace, his standing exceeds that of the states of Lu and Wei.

sentences.zh: 而惡直醜正，實繁有黨，或染凶作偽，疾害元功；

translations.literal: Yet those who hate the upright and loathe integrity are indeed numerous and faction-ridden; some stain virtue with wicked falsity and harm the foremost meritorious men;
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who hate the upright and loathe integrity are indeed numerous and faction-ridden; some stain virtue with wicked falsity and harm the foremost meritorious men;

sentences.zh: 或藉勞挾寵，乘威縱戾。

translations.literal: some lean on past labor and grasp favor, wielding power with reckless arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: some lean on past labor and grasp favor, wielding power with reckless arrogance.

sentences.zh: 自知愆深釁重，必貽剿戮，乃成紫毀朱，交間忠輔。

translations.literal: Knowing their guilt is deep and their offenses grave, sure to bring extermination, they turned purple into red and sowed discord among loyal ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing their guilt is deep and their offenses grave, sure to bring extermination, they turned black into red and sowed discord among loyal ministers.

sentences.zh: 崇樹私徒，招聚群惡，念舊愛老，無一而存，豈不由凶醜相扇，志肆讒惑。

translations.literal: They elevated private followers and gathered bands of evil; of those the emperor once cherished, not one remains—is this not because the wicked incite one another, their will set on spreading slander and delusion?
translations.idiomatic: They elevated private followers and gathered bands of evil; of those the emperor once cherished, not one remains—is this not because the wicked incite one another, their will set on spreading slander and delusion?

sentences.zh: 陛下垂慈狎達，不稍惟疑，遂令負扆席圖，蔽於流議，投杼市虎，成於十夫。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, benevolent and intimate with all, withheld even slight suspicion, so that seated at the screen with the map, you were shrouded by popular talk—like dropping the shuttle at the tale of the tiger in the market, truth ruined by ten men's words.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, benevolent and intimate with all, withheld even slight suspicion, so that seated at the screen with the map, you were shrouded by popular talk—like dropping the shuttle at the tale of the tiger in the market, truth ruined by ten men's words.

sentences.zh: 鑒古揆今，實懷危逼，故投袂樊、葉，立節於本朝；

translations.literal: Reflecting on antiquity and measuring the present, I truly feel peril pressing upon us; therefore I have thrown up my sleeves as at Fan and Ye and established my integrity for this dynasty;
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on antiquity and measuring the present, I truly feel peril pressing upon us; therefore I have thrown up my sleeves as at Fan and Ye and established my integrity for this dynasty;

sentences.zh: 揮戈晉陽，務清於君側。

translations.literal: I have raised my spear at Jinyang, striving to purge evil at the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: I have raised my spear at Jinyang, striving to purge evil at the ruler's side.

sentences.zh: 臣誠庸懦，奉教前朝，雖恧《緇衣》好賢之美，敢希《巷伯》惡惡之情，固已藉風聽而宵憤，撫短策而馳念。

translations.literal: I am indeed mediocre and timid, instructed by the former court; though I blush before the praise of "Dark Robes" for loving worthies, I dare aspire to the hatred of evil in "Lane Steward," and have already rested on rumor for nightly indignation, stroking my brief tally as my thoughts race.
translations.idiomatic: I am indeed mediocre and timid, instructed by the former court; though I blush before the praise of "Dark Robes" for loving worthies, I dare aspire to the hatred of evil in "Lane Steward," and have already rested on rumor for nightly indignation, stroking my brief tally as my thoughts race.

sentences.zh: 況乃宏命爰格，誠係宗社，今奉旨前邁，星言啟行。

translations.literal: Moreover the great mandate has descended, truly binding the altars of state; now receiving orders I advance, setting out at dawn's first word.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the great mandate has descended, truly binding the altars of state; now receiving orders I advance, setting out at dawn's first word.

sentences.zh: 臣本凡瑣，少無遠概，因緣際會，遂班槐鼎，素望既盈，愜心實足，豈應徼功非冀，更希異寵，直以蔓草難除，去惡宜速，是以無顧夷險，慮不及身。

translations.literal: I am by nature petty, with little far-reaching ambition; by chance I came to rank among the highest ministers, my modest hopes already fulfilled and my heart content—how should I grasp for unwarranted merit or further seek extraordinary favor? Only because invasive weeds are hard to uproot and evil must be removed swiftly, I disregard hardship and safety without thought for myself.
translations.idiomatic: I am by nature petty, with little far-reaching ambition; by chance I came to rank among the highest ministers, my modest hopes already fulfilled and my heart content—how should I grasp for unwarranted merit or further seek extraordinary favor? Only because invasive weeds are hard to uproot and evil must be removed swiftly, I disregard hardship and safety without thought for myself.

sentences.zh: 仰恃天眷，察亮丹款，苟血誠不照，甘心罪戮。

translations.literal: Trusting in Heaven's favor, I ask Your Majesty to discern my sincere devotion; if my blood loyalty is not recognized, I accept punishment and death willingly.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting in Heaven's favor, I ask Your Majesty to discern my sincere devotion; if my blood loyalty is not recognized, I accept punishment and death willingly.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下先鑒元輔匪躬茂節，末錄庸瑣奉國微誠，不遂淟涊之情，以失四海之望，昭戮馬劍，顯肆市朝，則結旌向國，全鋒凱歸，九流凝序，三光並耀，斯則仰說宗廟，俯愜兆民。

translations.literal: I humbly pray Your Majesty will first recognize the selfless excellence of the chief minister, and last record this petty man's slight loyalty to the state; deny not the honest impulse lest you disappoint the hope of all within the four seas. Let the saber of justice blaze in public execution, then banners may turn homeward and full blades return in triumph, the nine currents settle into order, sun moon and stars shine together—thus satisfying the ancestral temple above and the myriad people below.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray Your Majesty will first recognize the selfless excellence of the chief minister, and last record this petty man's slight loyalty to the state; deny not the honest impulse lest you disappoint the hope of all within the four seas. Let the saber of justice blaze in public execution, then banners may turn homeward and full blades return in triumph, the nine currents settle into order, sun, moon, and stars shine together—thus satisfying the ancestral temple above and the myriad people below.

sentences.zh: 裁表感慨，涕言無已。

translations.literal: This memorial, constrained with emotion, ends my tearful words.
translations.idiomatic: This memorial, constrained with emotion, ends my tearful words.

sentences.zh: 加魯弘輔國將軍，下戍大雷。

translations.literal: Lu Hong was promoted to General Who Assists the State and sent down to garrison Dalei.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Hong was promoted to General Who Assists the State and sent down to garrison Dalei.

sentences.zh: 馳報義宣，義宣遣諮議參軍劉諶之萬人就弘。

translations.literal: Zhi sent urgent word to Yi Xuan; Yi Xuan dispatched Senior Adviser-attendant Liu Chenzhi with ten thousand men to join Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi sent urgent word to Yi Xuan; Yi Xuan dispatched Senior Adviser-attendant Liu Chenzhi with ten thousand men to join Hong.

sentences.zh: 世祖遣撫軍將軍柳元景統豫州刺史王玄謨等水軍，屯梁山洲內，兩岸築偃月壘，水陸待之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu sent Pacifying Army General Liu Yuanjing to command the naval forces of Wang Xuamo, Governor of Yu Province, and others; they encamped within Liangshan Isle, building crescent fortifications on both banks, awaiting the rebels by land and water.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu sent Pacifying Army General Liu Yuanjing to command the naval forces of Wang Xuamo, Governor of Yu Province, and others; they encamped within Liangshan Isle, building crescent fortifications on both banks, awaiting the rebels by land and water.

sentences.zh: 殿中將軍沈靈賜領百舸，破其前軍於南陵，生禽軍主徐慶安、軍副王僧，質至梁山，亦夾陣兩岸。

translations.literal: Palace General Shen Lingci led a hundred warships, defeated their vanguard at Nanling, and captured alive the army commander Xu Qing'an and deputy Wang Seng. When Zhi reached Liangshan, he also deployed battle lines on both banks.
translations.idiomatic: Palace General Shen Lingci led a hundred warships, defeated their vanguard at Nanling, and captured alive the army commander Xu Qing'an and deputy Wang Seng. When Zhi reached Liangshan, he also deployed battle lines on both banks.

sentences.zh: 元景檄書宣告曰：

translations.literal: Yuanjing's proclamation declared:
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuanjing's proclamation declared as follows:

sentences.zh: 夫革道應運，基命之洪符；

translations.literal: When the Way is transformed to meet the age's turn, it is the great token of founding mandate;
translations.idiomatic: When the Way shifts to meet the age, that is the great sign of a founding mandate;

sentences.zh: 嗣業興邦，紹歷之明筭。

translations.literal: succeeding the enterprise and raising the state is the clear calculation of continuing the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: to carry on the work and raise the state is the clear design of continuing the dynastic line.

sentences.zh: 自非瑞積神衷，德充民極，孰能升臨寶位，景屬天居。

translations.literal: Unless accumulated auspice fills the divine heart and virtue fulfills the people's ideal, who could ascend the precious throne and align with Heaven's dwelling?
translations.idiomatic: Only when omens gather in the sacred breast and virtue fills the people's utmost need can one ascend the throne and take up Heaven's seat.

sentences.zh: 大宋啟期，理高中世，皇根帝葉，永流無疆。

translations.literal: Great Song opened its era, its governing principle towering in mid-antiquity; imperial root and dynastic branch flow on without end.
translations.idiomatic: Great Song has opened its age, its principle towering in mid-antiquity; imperial root and dynastic branch shall flow on without end.

sentences.zh: 夷陂遞來，遘茲凶難，國禍冤深，人綱鬱滅。

translations.literal: Calamities succeeded one another in waves, until we met this deadly trial; the national tragedy runs deep with grievance, human bonds are smothered and extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Disaster has rolled in wave after wave until we met this deadly trial; national grief runs deep, and the bonds of human order are smothered.

sentences.zh: 主上聖略聰武，孝感通神，義變草木，哀動精緯，躬幸南郢，親掃大逆，道援橫流，德模靈造，三光重照，七廟載興。

translations.literal: Our lord's sacred wisdom and keen martial prowess, filial responsiveness reaching the spirits, righteousness transforming even plants, grief moving the celestial threads—he personally went to Southern Yong, swept away the great rebel himself; the Way rescued the drowning flood, virtue modeled creation; sun, moon, and stars shine anew, the seven temples rise again.
translations.idiomatic: Our lord's sacred wisdom and martial keenness move Heaven through filial piety; his righteousness transforms even plants, his grief stirs the constellations. He went in person to Southern Yong and swept away the great rebel; the Way rescued the drowning tide, virtue shaped creation anew—sun, moon, and stars shine again, and the seven temples are raised once more.

sentences.zh: 臧質少負疵釁，衣冠不齒，昧利誣天，著於觸事。

translations.literal: Zang Zhi from youth bore stains and offenses, unfit among the gentry; deceiving Heaven for profit appears in everything he touches.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Zang Zhi carried a tainted name; the gentry would not rank him among themselves. He deceived Heaven for gain, and it shows in everything he does.

sentences.zh: 受任述職，不以宣效為心；

translations.literal: Given office and charged with duty, he did not take spreading effectiveness as his aim;
translations.idiomatic: When given office and charged with duty, he did not set his heart on serving the realm;

sentences.zh: 專方蒞民，惟以侵剝為務。

translations.literal: holding sole regional power over the people, he made exploitation his only business.
translations.idiomatic: holding sole power in his province, he made squeezing the people his only task.

sentences.zh: 官自賄至，族以貨傾。

translations.literal: From office came bribes; his clan was ruined by greed for goods.
translations.idiomatic: Offices came through bribery; his clan was ruined by greed for goods.

sentences.zh: 是以康周陀覆命屠宗，冤達蒼昊；

translations.literal: Hence Kang Zhoutuo was killed and his clan exterminated, grievance reaching the azure Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Kang Zhoutuo was killed and his clan wiped out, grievance reaching to Heaven itself;

sentences.zh: 郭伯、西門遺出自皁隸，寵越州朝。

translations.literal: Guo Bo and Ximen Yi rose from menial status, yet favors in the province exceeded those at court.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Bo and Ximen Yi rose from menial status, yet favors in the province exceeded those at court.

sentences.zh: 往蒞東守，鬻爵三千。

translations.literal: When he previously held the eastern post, he sold three thousand offices.
translations.idiomatic: When he previously held the eastern post, he sold three thousand offices.

sentences.zh: 率卒西討，竊俘取黜。

translations.literal: Leading troops west on campaign, he secretly kept captives and avoided dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Leading troops west on campaign, he secretly kept captives and avoided dismissal.

sentences.zh: 荷恩彭、泗，貪虐以逞，坑戮邊氓，忽若草芥，傾渴倉庾，割沒軍糧。

translations.literal: Favored at Peng and Si, he indulged greed and cruelty, slaughtering border folk as casually as grass, draining granaries dry and seizing army rations.
translations.idiomatic: Favored at Peng and Si, he indulged greed and cruelty, slaughtering border folk as casually as grass, draining granaries dry and seizing army rations.

sentences.zh: 作牧漢南，公盜府蓄，矯易文簿，專行欺妄。

translations.literal: As governor of Han South he openly plundered treasury stores, falsified registers, and practiced deception on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of Han South he openly plundered treasury stores, falsified registers, and practiced deception on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 及受命北伐，憚役緩期，師出有辰，顧懷私愛，匹馬棄眾，宵行獨返，遂復攜嬪擁姬，淫宴軍幕。

translations.literal: When ordered on the northern campaign, he feared labor and delayed; though the army had its set day, he clung to private loves, abandoned his troops on a single horse and returned alone by night, then again brought concubines into camp for debauched feasting in the command tent.
translations.idiomatic: When ordered on the northern campaign, he feared labor and delayed; though the army had its set day, he clung to private loves, abandoned his troops on a single horse and returned alone by night, then again brought concubines into camp for debauched feasting in the command tent.

sentences.zh: 孔、范之變，顯於逆辭。

translations.literal: The affair of Kong and Fan was manifest in his rebellious words.
translations.idiomatic: The affair of Kong and Fan was manifest in his rebellious words.

sentences.zh: 凡此諸釁，皆彰著於憲簡，振曝於觀聽。

translations.literal: All these offenses are clearly recorded in the law tablets and broadcast to all who hear.
translations.idiomatic: All these offenses are clearly recorded in the law tablets and broadcast to all who hear.

sentences.zh: 去歲義舉，雖豫誠款，而淹留西楚，私相崇戴，奉書致命，形於心跡。

translations.literal: Last year's righteous rising, though he shared in sincerity, he lingered in Western Chu, privately elevating another, sending letters pledging loyalty—the evidence lies in his heart and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Last year's righteous rising, though he shared in sincerity, he lingered in Western Chu, privately elevating another, sending letters pledging loyalty—the evidence lies in his heart and conduct.

sentences.zh: 新亭之捷，大難已夷，凶命假存，懸在晷刻，廣莫之軍，曾無遺矢，重關自開，偽眾已潰，質猶復盤桓衢巷，後騎陳師。

translations.literal: At Xinting's victory the great peril was already cleared; the usurper's life hung by a thread on the sundial's shadow; at the Gate of Broad Darkness not an arrow was wasted, the heavy passes opened themselves, the false host already routed—yet Zhi still loitered in the streets and lanes, his rear guard displaying battle order.
translations.idiomatic: At Xinting's victory the great peril was already cleared; the usurper's life hung by a thread on the sundial's shadow; at the Gate of Broad Darkness not an arrow was wasted, the heavy passes opened themselves, the false host already routed—yet Zhi still loitered in the streets and lanes, his rear guard displaying battle order.

sentences.zh: 勞不足甄，定於朝議，而虛張功伐，扇動怨辭，自謂斯舉，勳莫己若。

translations.literal: His service did not merit reward, as court deliberation decided; yet he inflated his exploits and stirred resentful talk, claiming that in this act no merit matched his own.
translations.idiomatic: His service did not merit reward, as court deliberation decided; yet he inflated his exploits and stirred resentful talk, claiming that in this act no merit matched his own.

sentences.zh: 初踐殿守，忘犬馬之情，奔趣帑藏，頓傾天府。

translations.literal: When first entrusted to guard the hall, he forgot his duty as loyal hound and steed, rushing to the treasuries and emptying the imperial vault at a stroke.
translations.idiomatic: When first entrusted to guard the hall, he forgot his duty as loyal hound and steed, rushing to the treasuries and emptying the imperial vault at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 山海弘量，苞荒藏疾，錄其一介之心，掩其不逞之釁。

translations.literal: The mountain-and-sea breadth of magnanimity embraced his faults and recorded his slightest loyalty, covering his unruly offenses.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain-and-sea breadth of magnanimity embraced his faults and recorded his slightest loyalty, covering his unruly offenses.

sentences.zh: 遂爵首元等，職班盛級，優榮溢寵，莫與為疇。

translations.literal: Thereupon he received a peerage foremost among the realm, offices of the highest rank, honors overflowing—none could compare.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he received a peerage foremost among the realm, offices of the highest rank, honors overflowing—none could compare.

sentences.zh: 自恣醜薄，罔知涯涘，干謁陳聞，曾無紀極，請樂窮太子之英，求器盡官府之選。

translations.literal: He indulged himself shamelessly without limit, petition after petition without end, requesting music to exhaust the crown prince's finest performers and seeking instruments to deplete the government's entire selection.
translations.idiomatic: He indulged himself shamelessly without limit, petition after petition without end, requesting music to exhaust the crown prince's finest performers and seeking instruments to deplete the government's entire selection.

sentences.zh: 徐司空匪躬王室，遭罹凶禍，質與之少長，親交兼常，曾無撫孤之仁，惟聞陵侮之酷，尺田寸寶，靡有孑遺。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Xu gave himself wholly to the royal house and met violent calamity; Zhi had been close to him from youth, their intimacy ordinary—yet he showed no kindness in nurturing the orphans, only cruel oppression; not an inch of land or scrap of treasure was left untouched.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Xu gave himself wholly to the royal house and met violent calamity; Zhi had been close to him from youth, their intimacy ordinary—yet he showed no kindness in nurturing the orphans, only cruel oppression; not an inch of land or scrap of treasure was left untouched.

sentences.zh: 及受命南徂，臨路滋甚，逼奪妻嬪，略市金帛，怨動京邑，醜聞都鄙。

translations.literal: When ordered south on campaign, his conduct on the road grew worse still—seizing wives and concubines, plundering markets for gold and silk; outrage shook the capital, scandal spread through town and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: When ordered south on campaign, his conduct on the road grew worse still—seizing wives and concubines, plundering markets for gold and silk; outrage shook the capital, scandal spread through town and countryside.

sentences.zh: 棄逐舊故，委蔑忠勤，魯尚期、尹周之徒，心腹所倚，泣訴於御筵；

translations.literal: He cast off old associates and treated loyal service with contempt; Lu Shangqi, Yin Zhou, and others whom he had trusted as his inner circle wept their grievances before the imperial throne;
translations.idiomatic: He cast off old associates and treated loyal service with contempt; Lu Shangqi, Yin Zhou, and others whom he had trusted as his inner circle wept their grievances before the imperial throne;

sentences.zh: 袁同、連子敬之疇，爪牙所杖，一逝而不反。

translations.literal: Yuan Tong, Lian Zijing, and their kind, the claws and fangs he relied on, departed once and never returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tong, Lian Zijing, and their kind, the claws and fangs he relied on, departed once and never returned.

sentences.zh: 雖上旨頻煩，屢求勞牒，質但稱伐在己，不逮僚隸，託咎朝廷，歸罪有司，國士解心，有識莫附。

translations.literal: Although imperial edicts came repeatedly and repeatedly sought records of merit, Zhi only claimed the credit of conquest for himself, did not extend it to colleagues and subordinates, shifted blame to the court, and put guilt on the officials; men of the state lost heart, and men of judgment would not follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Though imperial orders came again and again demanding accounts of his service, Zhi kept every victory for himself, gave no credit to his colleagues or staff, blamed the court for failures, and pinned guilt on the bureaucracy. The realm's best men lost faith in him, and no one of discernment would stand with him.

sentences.zh: 何文敬趨走廝養，天性愚狡，質迷其奸諂，寘懷委仗，遂外擅威刑，內遊房室。

translations.literal: He Wenjing was a running servant and groom, naturally stupid and cunning; Zhi was deluded by his treachery and flattery, placed full trust in him, and so he wielded punitive authority outwardly while roaming the women's quarters inwardly.
translations.idiomatic: He Wenjing had been nothing but a running servant, stupid by nature yet sly; Zhi was taken in by his flattery and treachery and gave him his full trust. Outwardly the man wielded punishments at will; inwardly he wandered through the inner chambers.

sentences.zh: 質生與釁俱，不可詳究，擢發數罪，曾何足言！

translations.literal: Zhi was born with offenses together; they cannot be investigated in detail—counting crimes hair by hair, how could they ever suffice to speak of!
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was born steeped in guilt; no full accounting is even possible. To count his crimes strand by strand would still fall far short of the truth!

sentences.zh: 丞相威重位尊，任居分陝，宗國倚賴，實兼恆情，而不及謙沖之塗，弗見逆順之訓，蔽同郤至，理乖范燮。

translations.literal: The Chancellor holds awesome weight and honored rank, his charge at the divide of Mount Sha, the imperial house relies on him—this is indeed common sentiment; yet he does not tread the path of humility, does not heed the lesson of loyalty and rebellion, is blind like Xi Zhi, and his reasoning is at odds with Fan Xie.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor's authority is great and his rank exalted; he holds power at the divide of the realm, and the dynasty depends on him—such trust is only natural. Yet he has not walked the road of humility, has not learned the lesson of loyalty and treason, is as blind as Xi Zhi was, and his judgment runs counter to the example of Fan Xie.

sentences.zh: 遂乃遠忽世祀，近受欺構，杖納奸疏，還謀社稷。

translations.literal: Then he far neglected the ancestral sacrifices, near accepted deceitful plotting, leaned on traitorous counsel, and turned to scheming against the altars of state.
