translations.idiomatic: He cast off ancestral duty from afar, embraced deceit close at hand, leaned on traitors' advice, and turned to plotting against the throne itself.

sentences.zh: 日者宴安上流，坐觀成敗，示遣疲卒，眾裁三千，戎馬不供，軍糧靡獻。

translations.literal: Recently he feasted in ease upstream, sat watching success and failure, pretended to send weary soldiers—only three thousand in all; neither war horses nor army rations were supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Of late he has feasted in comfort upstream, watching from the sidelines as fortunes turned. He made a show of dispatching troops, yet sent only three thousand worn-out men, with neither horses for battle nor grain for the army.

sentences.zh: 皇朝直以親秩之重，酬寵兼極，近漸別子，禮越常均，苟識無所守，功弗由己，必為義不全，終於敗德。

translations.literal: The imperial court had honored him solely for the weight of kinship, with rewards and favor beyond measure, granting princely rank beyond ordinary custom; if he lacks any moral principle and merit is not his own, righteousness must be incomplete and will end in ruined virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The court had showered him with honors purely because of blood ties, lavishing rank and favor beyond all precedent. If a man holds no principle of his own and wins no merit by his own deeds, his righteousness cannot be whole—and in the end his virtue will collapse.

sentences.zh: 今茲放命，恨心於本，推諸昔歲，跡是誠非矣。

translations.literal: Now this defiance of command, with resentment rooted at the source—applied to past years, the trace was truly wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Today's defiance springs from resentment deep in the heart; traced back through the years, the course was wrong from the start.

sentences.zh: 且家國夷險，情事異常，豫是臣子，孰不星赴，而玩寇忘哀，曾無奔拽。

translations.literal: Moreover, when state and family face common peril and circumstances are extraordinary, who as a subject would not rush like stars to respond? Yet he toyed with the enemy and forgot grief, never hurrying to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When throne and realm stand in common peril and the crisis is beyond the ordinary, what subject would not fly to the rescue like a shooting star? Yet he dallied with the enemy and forgot his grief, never once rushing to aid the cause.

sentences.zh: 面蕃十稔，惠政蔑聞，重贓深掠，縱欲已甚，姬妾百房，尼僧千計，敗道傷俗，悖亂人神，民怨盈塗，國謗彌歲。

translations.literal: Ten years facing the frontier, not a word of benevolent governance was heard; heavy corruption and deep plunder, indulging desires to excess—concubines in a hundred chambers, nuns and monks by the thousand; corrupting the Way and harming custom, perverting human and divine order; popular resentment filled the roads, slander of the state for years.
translations.idiomatic: For ten years on the frontier he governed without a trace of benevolent rule. Corruption ran deep and plunder was relentless; his appetites knew no limit. He kept concubines by the hundred and nuns and monks by the thousand, debasing the Way, wounding custom, and turning human and divine order upside down. The people's anger filled every road, and slander against the state went on for years.

sentences.zh: 又賊劭未禽，凶威猶強，將毀其私墳，戮其諸子，圖成駭機，垂賴義舉，捷期雲速，不日告平，釋怨毒之心，解倒懸之急，論恩敘德，造育為重。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the villain Shao was not yet captured and ferocious power still stood strong, they would destroy his family tombs and slaughter his sons—a moment of horrifying crisis, relying on the righteous rising; victory was expected swift as clouds, peace to be proclaimed within days, releasing rancorous hearts and relieving the dire crisis; when discussing grace and recounting virtue, nurturing creation should weigh heaviest.
translations.idiomatic: When the usurper Shao had not yet been taken and his brutal power still held sway, the dynasty itself stood on the brink—family tombs about to be destroyed, sons about to be slaughtered. Only the righteous rising could avert catastrophe; victory was expected as swiftly as clouds racing across the sky, peace within days. Hearts full of poison would be eased, the realm rescued from peril. In weighing grace and virtue, the nurture of life itself should count above all.

sentences.zh: 援人自助，棄人快讒，怙亂疑功，未聞其比。

translations.literal: Using others to help oneself, abandoning others to please slanderers, relying on rebellion while doubting merit—never has the like been heard.
translations.idiomatic: To use others for one's own rescue, then cast them aside to gratify slanderers; to lean on rebellion yet distrust those who serve—such conduct has no parallel.

sentences.zh: 僕以不肖，過蒙榮私，荷佩升越，光絕倫伍。

translations.literal: I, unworthy, have unduly received private honor, bearing elevation beyond measure, glory beyond all peers.
translations.idiomatic: Unworthy though I am, I have received private honors beyond my desert, bearing rank and favor that set me apart from all my peers.

sentences.zh: 家本北邊，志存慷慨，常甘投生，以殉艱棘，惟恩思難，激氣衝襟，故以眺三湘而永慨，望九江而遐憤。

translations.literal: My family is from the northern frontier; my heart is set on generous resolve, ever willing to stake my life on hard trials—thinking only of grace and hardship, indignation swelling my breast; thus gazing on the Three Xiang with lasting sighs and looking toward the Nine Rivers with distant rage.
translations.idiomatic: My family comes from the northern marches, and my heart burns with generous resolve. I have always been ready to give my life in the hardest trials, moved by gratitude and by the nation's peril until indignation fills my breast. Gazing toward the Three Xiang I sigh without end; looking toward the Nine Rivers my anger knows no bounds.

sentences.zh: 若使身死國康，誓在殞命，況仰稟聖略，俯鞠義徒，萬全之形，愚夫所照。

translations.literal: If my death could bring the state peace, I swear my life to it; how much more under sacred strategy above and righteous followers below—the form of complete victory is visible even to a fool.
translations.idiomatic: If my death alone could restore the realm, I would gladly give my life. How much more now, under the emperor's sacred strategy above and the righteous host below—complete victory is plain even to the dullest eye.

sentences.zh: 夫薛竟陵控率突騎，陸道步馳。

translations.literal: Xue of Jingling commands and leads sudden cavalry, charging by land on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Xue of Jingling leads crack cavalry, thundering overland at a forced march.

sentences.zh: 檀右衛、申右率、垣游擊整勒銳師，飛輪構路。

translations.literal: Tan of the Right Guard, Shen of the Right Commandant, and Yuan the Strike General array sharp troops, flying wheels forming the road.
translations.idiomatic: Tan of the Right Guard, Shen of the Right Commandant, and Yuan the Strike General have drawn up elite forces, their chariots wheeling forward to block every road.

sentences.zh: 王豫州方舟繕甲，久已前驅。

translations.literal: Wang of Yuzhou has long repaired armor on the great boats and already leads the advance.
translations.idiomatic: Wang of Yuzhou has long since fitted out his fleet and already sails in the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 僕訓卒利兵，淩波電進。

translations.literal: I have trained troops and sharpened weapons, crossing waves swift as lightning.
translations.idiomatic: I have drilled my soldiers and honed their arms, and we advance across the waves swift as lightning.

sentences.zh: 沈鎮軍、蕭安南接舳連旌，首尾風合。

translations.literal: Shen the Garrison General and Xiao of Annan link ships bow to stern, flags meeting in the wind front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: Shen the Garrison General and Xiao of Annan have linked their ships stem to stern, their banners meeting in the wind from van to rear.

sentences.zh: 驃騎竟陵王懿親令譽，問望攸歸，大司馬江夏王道略明遠，徽猷茂世，並旄鉞臨塗，雲驅齊引。

translations.literal: The Honorable Jingling Prince of Cavalry Command is famed for personal command and reputation to which all look; the Grand Marshal Prince of Jiangxia has far-reaching wisdom and splendid virtue in the age—both with banners and axes on the road, driving like clouds together.
translations.idiomatic: The Honorable Jingling Prince of Cavalry Command, famed for his personal leadership and the reputation all eyes turn to; the Grand Marshal Prince of Jiangxia, of far-reaching wisdom and splendid virtue in this age—both now advance with banners and battle-axes on the road, driving forward together like clouds on the wind.

sentences.zh: 群兵競邁，秘駕徐啟。

translations.literal: Armies vie in advance, the imperial carriage slowly sets forth.
translations.idiomatic: The armies press forward in rivalry, while the imperial carriage moves slowly in their wake.

sentences.zh: 八鑾搖響，五牛舒斾。

translations.literal: Eight tinkling bells sway and ring, five oxen unfurl banners.
translations.idiomatic: Eight tinkling bells sway on the carriage, five oxen pull banners unfurled.

sentences.zh: 千乘雷動，萬舳雲回。

translations.literal: A thousand chariots thunder, ten thousand ships wheel like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand chariots roll like thunder, ten thousand ships wheel and turn like clouds.

sentences.zh: 騰威發號，星流漢轉。

translations.literal: Towering majesty issues commands, stars streaming across the Milky Way.
translations.idiomatic: Majesty rises as orders go forth, and the host moves like stars wheeling across the sky.

sentences.zh: 以上臨下，易於轉圓。

translations.literal: From above looking down, it is easy as turning a circle.
translations.idiomatic: To strike from above against those below is as easy as turning a wheel.

sentences.zh: 加以三謀協從，七緯告慶，幽顯同心，昭然易睹。

translations.literal: Add to this the three counsels in accord, the seven strands proclaiming blessing, hidden and manifest of one heart—plainly easy to see.
translations.idiomatic: Add to this counsels in accord on every side, heavenly omens proclaiming victory, the seen and unseen worlds of one mind—the outcome is plain for all to see.

sentences.zh: 諸君或世荷恩幸，或身聞教義，當知君臣大節，誓不可犯，冠屨至誨，難用倒設。

translations.literal: You gentlemen have either received grace through generations or personally heard moral teaching; you should know the great bond of lord and subject, which oath must not be violated—the teaching of cap and shoes cannot be inverted.
translations.idiomatic: Some of you have received grace for generations; some have heard the teaching of righteousness with your own ears. You must know the great bond between lord and subject, an oath that must never be broken—the lesson of cap and shoes cannot be worn upside down.

sentences.zh: 履安奉順，聲泰事全，孰與附逆居危，身害名醜，慈親垂白受戮，弱子嬰孩就誅。

translations.literal: To walk in peace adhering to obedience, voice peaceful and affairs complete—who would prefer joining rebellion and dwelling in peril, body harmed and name disgraced, aged parents with white hair executed, infant children put to death?
translations.idiomatic: To live in peace under loyal obedience, with reputation secure and affairs whole—who would choose rebellion and peril instead, body ruined and name disgraced, white-haired parents slaughtered, infant children put to the sword?

sentences.zh: 所以有詔遲回，未震雷霆者，正為諸君身拘寇手，或懷乃心。

translations.literal: Therefore the edict has hesitated and thunder has not yet struck—precisely because you gentlemen are held in the rebel's grasp, or still harbor loyal hearts.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the imperial edict has held back and thunder has not yet fallen—because you are still in the rebels' hands, or because loyal hearts may yet remain among you.

sentences.zh: 吉凶由人，無謂為遠，今而不變，後悔何及。

translations.literal: Fortune and disaster depend on the person—do not say it is far off; if you do not change now, regret will come too late.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune and ruin rest in your own hands; do not think the choice distant. If you do not turn now, regret will come too late.

sentences.zh: 授檄之日，心馳賊庭。

translations.literal: On the day this proclamation is delivered, my heart races to the rebel court.
translations.idiomatic: From the day this proclamation reaches you, my heart flies toward the rebel stronghold.

sentences.zh: 義宣亦相次係至。

translations.literal: Prince Yi of Nanqiao was also captured in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi of Nanqiao was also captured in turn.

sentences.zh: 江夏王與義宣書曰：「昔桓玄借兵於仲堪，有似今日。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Jiangxia wrote to Prince Yi of Nanqiao: "Formerly Huan Xuan borrowed troops from Yin Zhongkan—the situation resembles today."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jiangxia wrote to Prince Yi of Nanqiao: "Long ago Huan Xuan borrowed troops from Yin Zhongkan—a situation much like today's."

sentences.zh: 義宣由此與質相疑。

translations.literal: From this Prince Yi of Nanqiao and Zang Zhi became mutually suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: From that moment Prince Yi of Nanqiao and Zang Zhi grew suspicious of each other.

sentences.zh: 質進計曰：「今以萬人取南州，則梁山中絕，萬人綴玄謨，必不敢動。

translations.literal: Zang Zhi offered a plan: "Now send ten thousand men to take Southern Province—then Liangshan will be cut off; ten thousand men to pin down Xuanmo, and he will surely not dare move.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Zhi proposed a plan: "Send ten thousand men to seize Southern Province and Liangshan will be cut off; pin ten thousand against Xuanmo and he will not dare stir.

sentences.zh: 質浮舟外江，直向石頭，此上略也。」

translations.literal: Zhi will float boats on the outer river straight toward Stone City—this is the supreme strategy."
translations.idiomatic: I will sail the outer river straight for Stone City—that is the supreme strategy."

sentences.zh: 義宣將從之，腹心劉諶之曰：「質求前馳，此志難測。

translations.literal: Prince Yi of Nanqiao was about to agree when his intimate Liu Chenzhi said: "Zhi asks to advance first—his intent is hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi of Nanqiao was about to accept when his trusted adviser Liu Chenzhi said: "Zhi wants to race ahead—his intentions cannot be trusted.

sentences.zh: 不如盡銳攻梁山，事克然後長驅，萬安之計也。」

translations.literal: Better to deploy all elite forces to attack Liangshan; once that succeeds then drive forward at length—the plan of perfect safety."
translations.idiomatic: Better to throw every elite soldier against Liangshan; once that falls, advance at full strength—that is the plan of perfect safety."

sentences.zh: 質遣將尹周之攻胡子反、柳叔政於西壘，時子反渡東岸就玄謨計事，聞賊至，馳歸。

translations.literal: Zang Zhi sent his general Yin Zhouzhi to attack Hu Zifan and Liu Shuzheng at the western rampart; at the time Zifan had crossed to the eastern bank to consult with Xuanmo on plans; hearing the enemy had arrived, he galloped back.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Zhi sent his general Yin Zhouzhi to attack Hu Zifan and Liu Shuzheng at the western rampart. Zifan had crossed to the eastern bank to consult with Xuanmo; when he heard the enemy had come, he galloped back.

sentences.zh: 周之攻壘甚急，劉季之水軍殊死戰，賊勢盛，求救於玄謨。

translations.literal: Yin Zhouzhi attacked the rampart with great urgency; Liu Jizhi's naval force fought to the death; the rebel force was strong and asked Xuanmo for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhouzhi pressed the assault on the rampart; Liu Jizhi's fleet fought to the death. The rebels' strength was overwhelming, and they sent to Xuanmo for help.

sentences.zh: 玄謨不遣，崔勳之固爭，乃遣勳之救之。

translations.literal: Xuanmo would not send relief; Cui Xunzhi argued stubbornly, and only then was Xunzhi sent to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo refused to send help. Cui Xunzhi argued fiercely until at last Xunzhi was dispatched to their aid.

sentences.zh: 比至，城已陷，勳之戰死，季之收眾而退。

translations.literal: By the time he arrived the fortress had fallen; Xunzhi died in battle; Jizhi gathered his forces and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived the fortress had already fallen. Xunzhi died fighting, and Jizhi gathered what men he could and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 子反、叔政奔還東岸，玄謨斬子反軍副李文仲。

translations.literal: Zifan and Shuzheng fled back to the eastern bank; Xuanmo executed Zifan's deputy Li Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zifan and Shuzheng fled back to the eastern bank. Xuanmo executed Zifan's deputy Li Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 質欲仍攻東城，義宣黨顏樂之說義宣曰：「質若復拔東城，則大功盡歸之矣。

translations.literal: Zang Zhi wished to continue attacking the eastern city; Prince Yi of Nanqiao's partisan Yan Lezhi said to Prince Yi: "If Zhi captures the eastern city again, all great merit will go to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Zhi wanted to press the attack on the eastern city. Yan Lezhi, a partisan of Prince Yi of Nanqiao, said to the prince: "If Zhi takes the eastern city again, all the glory will be his.

sentences.zh: 宜遣麾下自行。」

translations.literal: You should send your own subordinates to act on their own."
translations.idiomatic: You should send your own men to do it instead."

sentences.zh: 義宣遣劉諶之就質，陳軍城南。

translations.literal: Prince Yi of Nanqiao sent Liu Chenzhi to Zang Zhi, and they deployed troops south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi of Nanqiao sent Liu Chenzhi to Zang Zhi, and they drew up their army south of the city.

sentences.zh: 玄謨留羸弱守城，悉精兵出戰，薛安都騎軍前出，垣護之督諸將繼之。

translations.literal: Xuanmo left the weak to guard the city and sent all elite troops out to battle; Xue Andu's cavalry went forward first, Yuan Huzhi supervising the various generals following after.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo left the weak to hold the city and marched out with every elite soldier. Xue Andu's cavalry led the way, with Yuan Huzhi directing the other generals behind him.

sentences.zh: 戰良久，賊陣小拔，騎得入。

translations.literal: The battle lasted long; the rebel formation was slightly broken and cavalry was able to enter.
translations.idiomatic: The fighting went on for a long time until the rebel line gave way slightly and the cavalry broke through.

sentences.zh: 劉季之、宗越又陷其西北，眾軍乘之，乃大潰。

translations.literal: Liu Jizhi and Zong Yue also breached their northwest; the armies pressed the advantage and a great rout ensued.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jizhi and Zong Yue broke through the northwest as well. The imperial armies pressed the advantage and the rebels collapsed in a great rout.

sentences.zh: 因風放火，船艦悉見焚燒，延及西岸。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of the wind they set fire; ships were all burned, spreading to the western bank.
translations.idiomatic: They set fires with the wind at their backs; every ship was consumed, and the flames spread to the western bank.

sentences.zh: 質求義宣欲一計事，密已出走矣。

translations.literal: Zang Zhi sought Prince Yi of Nanqiao to consult on a plan—but Prince Yi had already secretly fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Zhi went to Prince Yi of Nanqiao to discuss strategy, only to find the prince had already slipped away in secret.

sentences.zh: 質不知所為，亦走，眾悉降散。

translations.literal: Zang Zhi did not know what to do and also fled; the host all surrendered and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Zhi, at a loss, fled as well. The army surrendered and broke apart.

sentences.zh: 質至尋陽，焚燒府舍，載妓妾西奔。

translations.literal: Zang Zhi reached Xunyang, burned the government offices, loaded his singing girls and concubines, and fled west.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Zhi reached Xunyang, burned the government compound, loaded his courtesans and concubines aboard, and fled west.

sentences.zh: 使所寵何文敬領兵居前，至西陽。

translations.literal: He sent his favorite He Wenjing to lead troops in front; they reached Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his favorite He Wenjing ahead with the vanguard as far as Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 西陽太守魯方平，質之黨也，至是懷貳，誑文敬曰：「傳詔宣敕，唯捕元惡一人，餘並無所問。」

translations.literal: The prefect of Xiyang Lu Fangping, Zang Zhi's partisan, by now wavered in loyalty and deceived Wenjing: "An edict has been transmitted proclaiming that only the chief culprit is to be captured; all others will not be questioned."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Fangping, prefect of Xiyang and once Zang Zhi's ally, had by now turned doubtful. He deceived Wenjing, saying: "An edict has been issued: only the chief culprit is to be taken; all others will go unpunished."

sentences.zh: 文敬棄眾而走。

translations.literal: Wenjing abandoned his troops and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing abandoned his men and fled.

sentences.zh: 質先以妹夫羊沖為武昌郡，質往投之。

translations.literal: Zang Zhi had previously appointed his brother-in-law Yang Chong as prefect of Wuchang; Zhi went to seek refuge with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Zhi had earlier made his brother-in-law Yang Chong prefect of Wuchang, and now fled to him for refuge.

sentences.zh: 既至，沖已為郡丞胡庇之所殺。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Chong had already been killed by the assistant prefect Hu Bizhi.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, Yang Chong had already been killed by the assistant prefect Hu Bizhi.

sentences.zh: 無所歸，乃入南湖逃竄，無食，摘蓮噉之。

translations.literal: With nowhere to go, he entered South Lake and fled in hiding; without food he picked lotus to eat.
translations.idiomatic: With nowhere left to turn, he hid in South Lake. Starving, he picked lotus pods and ate them raw.

sentences.zh: 追兵至，窘急，以荷覆頭，自沈於水，出鼻。

translations.literal: Pursuers arrived; in dire straits he covered his head with lotus leaves and submerged himself in the water, leaving his nose exposed.
translations.idiomatic: When pursuers closed in, desperate, he covered his head with lotus leaves and sank beneath the water, leaving only his nose above the surface.

sentences.zh: 軍主鄭俱兒望見，射之中心，兵刃亂至，腸胃纏縈水草，隊主裘應斬質首，傳京都，時年五十五。

translations.literal: The garrison commander Zheng Ju'er saw him and shot him in the heart; weapons piled on in confusion, intestines tangled in water weeds; squad leader Qiu Ying cut off Zhi's head and sent it to the capital; he was fifty-five years old.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commander Zheng Ju'er spotted him and shot him through the heart. Troops piled in with blades; his entrails tangled in the weeds. Squad leader Qiu Ying severed Zhi's head and sent it to the capital. He was fifty-five years old.

sentences.zh: 錄尚書江夏王臣義恭、左僕射臣宏等奏曰：「臧質底棄下才，而藉遇深重，窮愚悖常，構煽凶逆，變至滔天，志圖泯夏，違恩叛德，罪過恆科。

translations.literal: The Recorder of the Master of Writing, Prince of Jiangxia Chen Yigong, Left Vice Director Chen Hong, and others memorialized: "Zang Zhi, of mean abandoned talent, yet deeply favored by grace, utterly stupid and perverse beyond nature, instigating fierce rebellion, calamity reaching to Heaven, intent to destroy the dynasty, violating grace and betraying virtue—offenses of the constant code.
translations.idiomatic: The Recorder of the Master of Writing, Prince of Jiangxia Chen Yigong, Left Vice Director Chen Hong, and others memorialized: "Zang Zhi was a man of base and worthless talent, yet he received extraordinary favor. Utterly stupid and perverse beyond all measure, he stirred up violent rebellion until calamity reached the heavens, plotted to destroy the dynasty, and betrayed every debt of grace—crimes under the standing code of punishments.

sentences.zh: 梟首之憲，有國通典，懲戾思永，去惡宜深。

translations.literal: The law of displaying the head is the common standard of states; punishing the wicked with lasting thought, removing evil should go deep.
translations.idiomatic: The law of exposing the severed head is the common practice of every state. Punishment of the wicked must look to lasting warning; evil must be uprooted to the depths.

sentences.zh: 臣等參議，須辜日限意，使依漢王莽事例，漆其頭首，藏於武庫。

translations.literal: We your ministers deliberated and believe that on the day of execution, following the Han precedent of Wang Mang, his head should be lacquered and stored in the armory.
translations.idiomatic: We your ministers have deliberated and propose that on the day of execution, following the Han precedent applied to Wang Mang, his head be lacquered and kept in the imperial armory.

sentences.zh: 庶為鑒戒，昭示將來。」

translations.literal: Thus it may serve as a mirror and warning, displayed to the future."
translations.idiomatic: Thus it may serve as a warning to all and a lesson for generations to come."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict granted approval.

sentences.zh: 質初下，義宣以質子敦為征虜將軍、雝州刺史。

translations.literal: When Zang Zhi first went out on campaign, Prince Yi of Nanqiao made Zhi's son Dun General Who Subdues Barbarians and Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Zang Zhi first marched out, Prince Yi of Nanqiao appointed Zhi's son Dun General Who Subdues Barbarians and Governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 質留子敞為監軍，將敦自隨，至是竝為武昌郡所執送。

translations.literal: Zhi left his son Chang as army supervisor and took Dun with him; at this time both were seized by Wuchang commandery and sent under guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Zhi left his son Chang behind as army supervisor and took Dun with him. Now both were captured by Wuchang commandery and sent under guard.

sentences.zh: 敦官至黃門郎。

translations.literal: Dun had reached the office of Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Dun had risen to the post of Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 敦弟敷，司徒屬。

translations.literal: Dun's younger brother Fu was an aide in the Chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: Dun's younger brother Fu served as an aide in the Chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 敷弟敞，太子洗馬。

translations.literal: Fu's younger brother Chang was a Groom in Attendance of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's younger brother Chang was Groom in Attendance to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 敞弟斁，敦子仲璋，質之二子二孫未有名，同誅。

translations.literal: Chang's younger brother Yi, Dun's son Zhongzhang, and Zhi's two sons and two grandsons who had not yet received style names were all executed together.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, Chang's younger brother; Zhongzhang, Dun's son; and Zhi's two sons and two still-nameless grandsons—all were put to death together.

sentences.zh: 質之起兵也，豫章太守任薈之、臨川內史劉懷之、鄱陽太守杜仲儒竝為盡力，發遣郡丁，并送糧運，伏誅。

translations.literal: When Zang Zhi raised troops, the prefect of Yuzhang Ren Huizhi, the Administrator of Linchuan Liu Huaizhi, and the prefect of Poyang Du Zhongru all exerted themselves fully, dispatching district militia and sending grain transports—all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zang Zhi rose in arms, the prefect of Yuzhang Ren Huizhi, the Administrator of Linchuan Liu Huaizhi, and the prefect of Poyang Du Zhongru all gave him their full support, dispatching district militia and sending grain convoys. All were put to death.

sentences.zh: 任薈之，字處茂，樂安人也。

translations.literal: Ren Huizhi, style name Chumao, was a native of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Huizhi, style name Chumao, came from Le'an.

sentences.zh: 歷世祖、南平王鑠撫軍右軍司馬、長史行事。

translations.literal: He served under Emperor Xiaowu and as Right Army Major and Chief of Staff acting on behalf of the chief of staff for Prince Shao of Nanping's Pacification Army.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Emperor Xiaowu and held the posts of Right Army Major and acting Chief of Staff on the Pacification Army staff of Prince Shao of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 太祖稱之曰：「望雖不足，才能有餘。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen praised him saying: "Though his reputation falls short, his talent exceeds the measure."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen said of him: "His reputation may fall short, but his talent more than makes up for it."

sentences.zh: 杜仲儒，杜驥兄子也。

translations.literal: Du Zhongru was the son of Du Ji's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zhongru was Du Ji's nephew.

sentences.zh: 豫章望蔡子相孫沖之起義拒質，質遣將郭會膚、史山夫討之，為沖之所破。

translations.literal: Sun Chongzhi, grandson of the Wangcai Marquis of Yuzhang, raised the righteous standard to resist Zang Zhi; Zhi sent generals Guo Huifu and Shi Shanfu to attack him and was defeated by Chongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chongzhi, grandson of the Wangcai Marquis of Yuzhang, raised the righteous banner against Zang Zhi. Zhi sent generals Guo Huifu and Shi Shanfu against him and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 世祖發詔，以為尚書都官曹郎中。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu issued an edict appointing him Secretariat Attendant in the Department of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu issued an edict appointing him Attendant in the Department of Punishments of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 沖之，太原中都人，晉秘書監盛曾孫也。

translations.literal: Chongzhi was from Zhongdu in Taiyuan, a great-grandson of the Jin Master of Writing Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi came from Zhongdu in Taiyuan and was a great-grandson of the Jin Master of Writing Sheng.

sentences.zh: 官至右軍將軍，巴東太守。

translations.literal: He reached the rank of General of the Right Army and Prefect of Badong.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General of the Right Army and Prefect of Badong.

sentences.zh: 後事在劉琬傳。

translations.literal: His later affairs are recorded in the biography of Liu Wan.
translations.idiomatic: His later career is recounted in the biography of Liu Wan.

sentences.zh: 沈靈賜以破質前軍於南陵功，封南平縣男，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Shen Lingci for his merit in defeating Zang Zhi's vanguard at Nanling was enfeoffed as Baron of Nanping county with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For defeating Zang Zhi's vanguard at Nanling, Shen Lingci was enfeoffed as Baron of Nanping county with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 贈崔勳之通直郎。

translations.literal: Cui Xunzhi was posthumously granted Gentleman for Direct Remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xunzhi was posthumously awarded the title Gentleman for Direct Remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 大司馬參軍劉天賜亦梁山戰亡，追贈給事中。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal staff officer Liu Tianci also died in the battle at Liangshan and was posthumously granted Gentleman Attendant at the Palace Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tianci, a staff officer of the Grand Marshal, also died at the battle of Liangshan and was posthumously granted Gentleman Attendant at the Palace Gates.

sentences.zh: 魯爽，小名女生，扶風郿人也。

translations.literal: Lu Shuang, childhood name Nüsheng, was a native of Mei in Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shuang, whose childhood name was Nüsheng, came from Mei in Fufeng commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖宗之，字彥仁，晉孝武太元末，自鄉里出襄陽，歷官至南郡太守。

translations.literal: His ancestor Zongzhi, style name Yanren, at the end of the Taiyuan era of Jin Emperor Xiaowu, left his home district for Xiangyang and rose through offices to Prefect of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Zongzhi, style name Yanren, left his home district for Xiangyang in the closing years of the Taiyuan era under Jin Emperor Xiaowu and rose through the ranks to Prefect of Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 義熙元年起義，襲偽雝州刺史桓蔚，進向江陵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yixi he rose in righteous revolt, attacked the false Governor of Yong Huan Wei, and advanced toward Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yixi he joined the righteous uprising, struck at the rebel Governor of Yong Huan Wei, and marched on Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 以功為輔國將軍、雝州刺史，封霄城縣侯，食邑千五百戶。

translations.literal: For merit he was made General Who Supports the State and Governor of Yong Province, enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiaocheng county with a fief of fifteen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made General Who Supports the State and Governor of Yong Province, enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiaocheng county with a fief of fifteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 桓謙、荀林逼江陵，宗之率眾馳赴，事在臨川烈武王道規傳。

translations.literal: When Huan Qian and Xun Lin pressed Jiangling, Zongzhi led his host in rapid relief—the affair is in the biography of Prince Daowu of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Qian and Xun Lin pressed Jiangling, Zongzhi raced to the city's aid—the account is given in the biography of Prince Daowu of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 進號平北將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to the title General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 高祖討劉毅，與宗之同會江陵，進號鎮北將軍，封南陽郡公，食邑二千五百戶。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor attacked Liu Yi, he joined Zongzhi at Jiangling, was promoted to General Who Guards the North, and enfeoffed as Duke of Nanyang commandery with a fief of twenty-five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When the High Ancestor marched against Liu Yi, he joined Zongzhi at Jiangling, was promoted to General Who Guards the North, and enfeoffed as Duke of Nanyang commandery with a fief of twenty-five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 子軌，一名象齒，爽之父也。

translations.literal: His son Gui, also named Xiangchi, was Shuang's father.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gui, also called Xiangchi, was Lu Shuang's father.

sentences.zh: 便弓馬，筋力絕人，為竟陵太守。

translations.literal: Skilled with bow and horse, strength beyond ordinary men, he served as Prefect of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: A master of bow and horse with strength beyond ordinary men, he served as Prefect of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 宗之自以非高祖舊隸，屢建大功，有自疑之心。

translations.literal: Zongzhi felt himself not an old follower of the High Ancestor yet had repeatedly achieved great merit, and harbored self-doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhi knew he was not one of the High Ancestor's old companions, yet he had won great merit again and again, and this bred doubt in his own heart.

sentences.zh: 會司馬休之見討，猜懼，遂與休之北奔。

translations.literal: When Sima Xiuzhi came under attack, fearful and suspicious, he fled north with Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Xiuzhi came under attack, Zongzhi, fearful and suspicious, fled north with him.

sentences.zh: 善於撫御，士民皆為盡力，衛送出境，盡室入羌，頃之病卒。

translations.literal: Skilled at governing and controlling, gentry and commoners all exerted themselves for him, escorting him beyond the border; the whole household entered the Di lands, and shortly thereafter he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at winning men to his side, he drew the full loyalty of gentry and commoners alike, who escorted him beyond the frontier. The whole household entered Di territory, and before long he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 高祖定長安，軌為寧南將軍、荊州刺史、襄陽公，鎮長社。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor secured Chang'an, Gui was made General Who Pacifies the South, Governor of Jing Province, and Duke of Xiangyang, garrisoning Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: After the High Ancestor secured Chang'an, Gui was appointed General Who Pacifies the South, Governor of Jing Province, and Duke of Xiangyang, with his seat at Changshe.

sentences.zh: 世祖鎮襄陽，軌遣親人程整奉書，規欲歸順，自拔致誠，以昔殺劉康祖、徐湛之父，故不歸。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu was garrisoning Xiangyang, Gui sent his kinsman Cheng Zheng to deliver a letter, planning to submit and surrender himself in sincerity; because he had previously killed Liu Kangzu and Xu Dan's father, they did not accept his return.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu was stationed at Xiangyang, Gui sent his kinsman Cheng Zheng with a letter offering to surrender and prove his loyalty. But because he had once killed Liu Kangzu and the father of Xu Dan, his offer was refused.

sentences.zh: 太祖累遣招納，許以為司州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen repeatedly sent envoys to recruit and win him over, promising to appoint him Governor of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen sent envoy after envoy to win him over, promising him the post of Governor of Si Province.

sentences.zh: 爽少有武藝，虜主拓跋燾知之，常置左右。

translations.literal: Shuang from youth possessed martial skill; the barbarian ruler Tuoba Tao knew of it and regularly kept him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shuang showed martial talent from an early age, and the Northern Wei ruler Tuoba Tao, knowing of it, kept him constantly at his side.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十六年，軌死，爽為寧南將軍、荊州刺史、襄陽公，鎮長社。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia, Gui died; Shuang became General Who Pacifies the South, Governor of Jing Province, and Duke of Xiangyang, garrisoning Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia, Gui died, and Lu Shuang succeeded him as General Who Pacifies the South, Governor of Jing Province, and Duke of Xiangyang, with his seat at Changshe.

sentences.zh: 幼染殊俗，無復華風。

translations.literal: In youth infected by alien customs, no longer possessing Chinese ways.
translations.idiomatic: Raised among foreign customs from childhood, he had long lost any trace of Chinese refinement.

sentences.zh: 粗中使酒，數有過失，燾將誅之。

translations.literal: Rough and given to liquor when in the middle of things, he repeatedly committed faults; Tao was about to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: He was coarse and quick to drink, and repeatedly gave offense; Tuoba Tao was on the point of putting him to death.

sentences.zh: 爽有七弟秀，小字天念，頗有意略，才力過爽。

translations.literal: Shuang had a seventh younger brother Xiu, childhood name Tiannian, who possessed considerable strategic understanding; his talent and strength surpassed Shuang's.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shuang had a younger brother, the seventh-born Xiu—childhood name Tiannian—who was quite astute in counsel and surpassed his brother in both talent and prowess.

sentences.zh: 燾以充宿衛，甚知待之。

translations.literal: Tao used him to fill the palace guard and treated him with great familiarity and regard.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Tao assigned him to the palace guard and showed him extraordinary favor.

sentences.zh: 偽高梁王阿叔泥為芮芮所圍甚急，使秀往救，燾自率大眾繼其後。

translations.literal: The false Prince of Gaoliang Ashuni was besieged by the Rouran in extreme peril; Xiu was sent to the rescue, and Tao personally led a great host in his wake.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Prince of Gaoliang, Ashuni, was hard pressed in a Rouran siege; Xiu was dispatched to relieve him while Tuoba Tao personally led a great army to follow.

sentences.zh: 燾未及至，秀已擊破之，拔阿叔泥而反。

translations.literal: Before Tao had yet arrived, Xiu had already defeated them, extricated Ashuni, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Before Tuoba Tao could arrive, Xiu had already routed the enemy, rescued Ashuni, and marched back.

sentences.zh: 燾壯其功，以為中書郎，封廣陵侯。

translations.literal: Tao admired his achievement, appointing him Secretariat Gentleman and enfeoffing him as Marquis of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Tao commended his exploit, making him a Secretariat Gentleman and enfeoffing him as Marquis of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 或告燾，鄴民欲據城反，復遣檢察，并燒石虎殘宮殿。

translations.literal: Someone reported to Tao that the people of Ye intended to seize the city in revolt; Xiu was again sent to investigate, and also burned the ruined palaces of Shi Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Someone informed Tuoba Tao that the Ye populace meant to hold the city in rebellion; Xiu was again dispatched to investigate, and burned as well the ruined palaces of Shi Hu.

sentences.zh: 秀常乘驛往反，是時病還遲，為燾所詰讓，秀復恐懼。

translations.literal: Xiu often rode post-horses back and forth on these missions; on this occasion he returned late because of illness and was rebuked by Tao, and Xiu again grew fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu often traveled these missions by post relay; this time illness delayed his return, and Tuoba Tao's rebuke left him once more in fear.

sentences.zh: 燾尋南寇，因從渡河。

translations.literal: Tao soon raided south; Xiu followed him across the river.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuoba Tao soon after launched a southern campaign, Xiu went with him across the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 先是，程天祚為虜所沒，燾引置左右，與秀囗寬，勸令歸降，秀納之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Cheng Tianzuo had been captured by the barbarians; Tao brought him to his side, grew close with Xiu, and urged him to surrender to the south; Xiu accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Cheng Tianzuo had fallen into enemy hands; Tuoba Tao kept him at court, where he met Xiu and grew close to him, urging defection to the south—a counsel Xiu took to heart.

sentences.zh: 天祚，廣平人，為殿中將軍，有武力。

translations.literal: Tianzuo was a man of Guangping, served as Palace Gate General, and possessed martial strength.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzuo came from Guangping and held the post of Palace Gate General; he was a man of proven fighting strength.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十七年，助戍彭城，會世祖遣府劉泰之輕軍襲虜於汝陽，天祚督戰，戰敗被創，為虜所獲。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia, while assisting in the garrison at Pengcheng, it happened that Emperor Xiaowu dispatched the staff officer Liu Taizhi with a light force to strike the barbarians at Ruyang; Tianzuo directed the battle, was defeated and wounded, and was captured by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia, while helping hold Pengcheng, Cheng Tianzuo found himself in the path of a light column under Liu Taizhi, dispatched by Emperor Xiaowu to strike the enemy at Ruyang. He led the defense, was defeated and wounded, and taken captive.

sentences.zh: 天祚妙善針術，燾深加愛賞，或與同輿，常不離於側，封為南安公。

translations.literal: Tianzuo was masterfully skilled in acupuncture; Tao deeply favored and rewarded him, sometimes sharing a carriage with him, never leaving his side, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzuo was an expert with the needle; Tuoba Tao prized him highly, sometimes rode with him in the same carriage, kept him always at hand, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 燾北還蕃，天祚因其沈醉，偽若受使督切後軍者，所至輕罰。

translations.literal: When Tao returned north to Fan, Tianzuo took advantage of his drunkenness, feigning to have been sent to oversee and chastise the rear guard, lightly punishing wherever he went.
translations.idiomatic: As Tuoba Tao marched north toward Fan, Tianzuo waited until he was drunk, then posed as an envoy charged with disciplining the rear guard, handing out only light punishments as he went.

sentences.zh: 天祚為燾所愛，群虜並畏之，莫敢問，因得逃歸，後為山陽太守。

translations.literal: Tianzuo was beloved by Tao; all the barbarians feared him as well and none dared question him, so he was able to escape and return; afterward he served as Prefect of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Because Tuoba Tao favored Tianzuo, the tribesmen feared him too and dared not challenge his authority; he thus made his escape home and later served as Prefect of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 太宗初，與四方同反，事在薛安都傳。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign, he joined the rebellions across the four quarters; the affair is in the biography of Xue Andu.
translations.idiomatic: In the early reign of Emperor Ming he rebelled along with others across the realm; the account is given in the biography of Xue Andu.

sentences.zh: 燾始南行，遣爽隨永昌王庫仁真向壽陽，與弟瑜共破劉祖於尉武，仍至瓜步，始得與秀定歸南之謀。

translations.literal: When Tao first marched south, he sent Shuang to follow Prince Yongchang Kurzhen toward Shouyang; with his brother Yu he jointly defeated Liu Zu at Yuwu, then proceeded to Guabu, where he at last joined Xiu in plotting return to the south.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tuoba Tao's southern march, he sent Lu Shuang with Prince Yongchang Kurzhen toward Shouyang. Shuang and his brother Yu together defeated Liu Zu at Yuwu and pressed on to Guabu, where he at last conspired with Xiu to defect south.

sentences.zh: 燾還至湖陸，爽等請曰：「奴與南有仇，每兵來，常慮禍及墳墓，乞共迎喪，還葬國都。」

translations.literal: When Tao returned to Hulu, Shuang and the others petitioned: "Your servant and the south bear a feud; whenever armies come, we constantly fear harm to our ancestral tombs. We beg leave together to recover the remains and rebury them in the capital."
translations.idiomatic: When Tuoba Tao withdrew to Hulu, Shuang and his party pleaded: "Your servant bears a blood feud with the south; with every campaign we dread for our family graves. We beg permission to fetch our forebears' remains and rebury them in the capital."

sentences.zh: 虜群下於其主稱奴，猶中國稱臣也。

translations.literal: Among the barbarians, subordinates addressed their lord as "your servant," just as in China they say "your minister."
translations.idiomatic: Among the northern tribes, retainers addressed their lord as "your servant"—the equivalent of "your minister" at the Liu Song court.

sentences.zh: 燾許之。

translations.literal: Tao granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Tao consented.

sentences.zh: 長社戍虜有六七百人，爽譎之曰：「南更有軍，可遣三百騎往界上參聽。」

translations.literal: The barbarian garrison at Changshe numbered six or seven hundred; Shuang deceived them, saying: "There are more southern troops; three hundred horsemen could be sent to the border to listen and observe."
translations.idiomatic: At Changshe the enemy garrison numbered six or seven hundred men. Shuang tricked them: "Southern reinforcements are near—send three hundred riders to the border to scout."

sentences.zh: 騎去，爽率腹心夜擊餘虜，盡殺之，馳入虎牢。

translations.literal: Once the horsemen had gone, Shuang led his trusted followers in a night attack on the remaining barbarians, killing them all, and galloped into Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: When the riders had left, Shuang led his trusted men in a night assault, slaughtered the remaining garrison, and raced into Hulao.

sentences.zh: 爽唯第三弟在北，餘家屬悉自隨，率部曲及願從合千餘家奔汝南。

translations.literal: Only Shuang's third younger brother remained in the north; the rest of the family all followed him personally; he led his followers and willing adherents, together more than a thousand households, in flight to Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Only Lu Shuang's third brother stayed behind in the north; the rest of the clan accompanied him, and he led his retainers and volunteers—more than a thousand households in all—to flee toward Runan.

sentences.zh: 遣秀從許昌還壽陽，奉辭於南平王鑠曰：「爽、秀得罪晉朝，負釁三世，生長絕域，遠身胡虜，兄弟闔門，淪點偽授，殞命不可，還國無因。

translations.literal: He sent Xiu from Xuchang back to Shouyang to present a memorial to Prince of Nanping Shuo, saying: "Shuang and Xiu have offended the Jin court, bearing guilt through three generations; we grew up in distant lands, far from Han civilization among barbarian hosts; our whole household fell into false appointments; death seemed unavoidable and return impossible.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Xiu from Xuchang to Shouyang with a formal address to Prince Shuo of Nanping: "Lu Shuang and Lu Xiu have sinned against the dynasty across three generations. Reared in the wild borderlands among the northern tribes, our entire house sank into foreign service. Death seemed our only prospect; return home, a hopeless dream.

sentences.zh: 近係南雲，傾屬東日，蓋猶痿人思步，盲者願明。

translations.literal: Recently bound to the southern clouds, we lean upon the eastern sun; it is as though a paralytic yearns to walk, or the blind long for sight.
translations.idiomatic: Long tied to southern clouds, we now turn to the eastern sun—in the manner of a cripple who aches to walk, or a blind man who craves light.

sentences.zh: 嵩、霍咫尺，江、河匪遠，夷庚壅塞，隔同天地，痛心疾首，書慨宵悲。

translations.literal: Song and Huo are within reach, the Yangtze and Yellow River not far; the Yi Geng road blocked, separated as heaven and earth; heart-rending grief, writing indignation, grieving by night.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Song and Mount Huo stand within a stone's throw; the great rivers are not far away—yet the Yi Geng road is choked, and we are sundered as if by heaven and earth. Our hearts ache; we write in anguish and weep through the night.

sentences.zh: 虜主倡狂，豺豕其志，虐遍華、戎，怨結幽顯。

translations.literal: The barbarian lord is reckless and violent, wolf and pig in his intent; his cruelty spreads through Chinese and barbarian alike; resentment binds the living and the dead.
translations.idiomatic: The northern ruler runs wild, his heart that of wolf and boar; his tyranny reaches Han and alien alike, and resentment fills both the seen and unseen worlds.

sentences.zh: 自盱眙旋軍，亡殪過半，昏酣沈湎，恣性肆身。

translations.literal: Since withdrawing from Xuyi, more than half perished; sunk in drunken stupor, he indulges his nature without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Since the retreat from Xuyi, more than half his army has perished, yet he plunges deeper into drink and debauchery.

sentences.zh: 爽、秀等因民之憤，藉將旅之願，齊契義奮，梟馘醜徒，馮恃皇威，肅清逋穢，牢、洛諸城，指期克定。

translations.literal: Shuang, Xiu, and the others, taking advantage of the people's anger and relying on the troops' desire, united in righteous zeal to behead the ugly foe; leaning on the emperor's majesty, they would sweep away fugitive filth; the cities of Lao and Luo would fall within the appointed time.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shuang and Lu Xiu, riding the people's rage and the army's will to fight, vow to march in righteous fury and cut down the enemy. Trusting in the emperor's might, they will purge the border of its scourge and take Hulao and Luoyang in short order.

sentences.zh: 規以涓塵，微雪夙負，方當束骸北闕，待戮司寇，懦節未申，伏心邊表。

translations.literal: Planning with a drop of dust to slightly wash away old guilt, we ought to bind our bodies before the northern palace gate and await execution by the minister of justice; our timid loyalty yet unproven, we prostrate our hearts on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: We offer this small service to lighten debts owed since birth; we meant to present ourselves at the northern gate for judgment by the law—our fealty still unproved, our hearts bowed at the border.

sentences.zh: 明大王殿下以叡茂居蕃，文武兼姿，遠邇欽傾，承風聞德，願垂援拯，以慰虔望。

translations.literal: Illustrious Great Prince Your Highness, with sagacious excellence dwelling in your fief, combining literary and martial gifts, near and far bow in admiration; hearing your virtue on the wind, we beg your aid and rescue to comfort our sincere longing.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness, luminous in wisdom and virtue in your princely domain, master of both pen and sword—the world looks to you. Having heard of your renown, we beg your protection to satisfy our earnest hope.

sentences.zh: 老弱百口，先遣歸庇。

translations.literal: The old and weak, a hundred mouths, we first send back for shelter.
translations.idiomatic: We have already sent ahead our hundred dependents—the aged and frail—to seek your protection.

sentences.zh: 逼逼丹心，仰希懷遠。

translations.literal: Pressing pressing is our red heart; we look up hoping for your embrace of the distant.
translations.idiomatic: Our hearts burn with longing; we look to your mercy for those far from home.

sentences.zh: 謹遣同義潁川聶元初奉詞陳聞。」

translations.literal: We respectfully send our fellow righteous man Nie Yuanchu of Yingchuan to present this address and report."
translations.idiomatic: We humbly dispatch Nie Yuanchu of Yingchuan, who shares our cause, to deliver this petition."

sentences.zh: 鑠馳驛以聞，上大說，下詔曰：「偽寧南將軍魯爽、中書郎魯秀，志幹列到，忠誠久著，撫茲福先，闔門效款，招集義銳，梟剪獯醜，肅定邊城，獻馘象魏。

translations.literal: Shuo sent word by post relay; the emperor was greatly pleased and issued an edict: "The false General Who Pacifies the South Lu Shuang and Secretariat Gentleman Lu Xiu—resolve and prowess outstanding, loyalty long manifest, leading this generation in blessing first, the whole household offering sincerity, gathering righteous elite, beheading the Xiungnu ugliness, securing the border cities, presenting heads at the Elephant Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo forwarded the memorial by express courier. The emperor was delighted and decreed: "The former Northern Wei General Who Pacifies the South, Lu Shuang, and Secretariat Gentleman Lu Xiu have long shown steadfast loyalty and martial resolve. Their whole house has proved its good faith; rallying righteous fighters, they cut down the northern foe, secured the frontier, and sent captured heads to the capital.

sentences.zh: 雖宣孟之去翟歸晉，頹當之出胡入漢，方之此日，曾何足云。

translations.literal: Though Xu Meng left the Di and returned to Jin, or Tui Dang came out of the Hu and entered Han—compared with this day, how could those be worth speaking of?
translations.idiomatic: Even Xu Meng's departure from the Di to serve Jin, or Tui Dang's crossing from the steppe into the Han world—placed beside this day, what are they worth?

sentences.zh: 朕實嘉之，宜即授任，逞其忠略。

translations.literal: I truly commend them; they should at once be given appointment to display their loyal strategy.
translations.idiomatic: I am deeply pleased and would have them appointed forthwith to put their loyalty and strategic gifts to use.

sentences.zh: 爽可督司州、陳留、東郡、濟陰、濮陽五郡諸軍事、征虜將軍、司州刺史。

translations.literal: Shuang shall be made Commander of the armies of the five commanderies of Si Province—Chenliu, Dongjun, Jiyin, and Puyang—General Who Punishes the Barbarians, and Governor of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shuang is appointed Commander over the five commanderies of Si Province—Chenliu, Dong, Jiyin, and Puyang—General Who Punishes the Barbarians, and Governor of Si Province.

sentences.zh: 秀可輔國將軍、滎陽、潁川二郡太守。

translations.literal: Xiu shall be made General Who Supports the State and Prefect of the two commanderies of Yingyang and Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiu is appointed General Who Supports the State and Prefect of Yingyang and Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 其諸子弟及同契士庶，委征虜府以時申言，詳加酬敘。」

translations.literal: His various younger brothers, sons, and fellow oath-bound gentry and commoners shall be reported in due time to the General Who Punishes the Barbarians' office for detailed recognition and reward."
translations.idiomatic: Their brothers, nephews, and all who joined their cause should be reported to Shuang's headquarters in turn for proper reward."

sentences.zh: 爽至汝南，加督豫州之義陽、宋安二郡軍事，領義陽內史，將軍、刺史如故。

translations.literal: When Shuang reached Runan, he was further made Commander of the military affairs of the two commanderies of Yiyang and Song'an in Yu Province, holding the post of Administrator of Yiyang; General and Governor as before.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Runan, Lu Shuang was additionally charged with military affairs in Yiyang and Song'an of Yu Province and named Administrator of Yiyang, while retaining his existing titles as general and governor.

sentences.zh: 秀參右將軍南平王鑠軍事、汝陰內史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Xiu served as staff to the Right General Prince of Nanping Shuo in military affairs and as Administrator of Ruyin; General as before.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiu was made military adviser to Prince Shuo of Nanping, Right General, and Administrator of Ruyin, retaining his rank as general.

sentences.zh: 餘弟姪竝授官爵，賞賜資給甚厚。

translations.literal: The remaining younger brothers and nephews were all granted office and rank; rewards and provisions were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: His other brothers and nephews received official posts and titles as well, with lavish gifts and supplies.

sentences.zh: 爽北鎮義陽。

translations.literal: Shuang garrisoned the north at Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shuang took up a northern garrison at Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 北來部曲凡六千八百八十三人，是歲二十八年也。

translations.literal: The followers who came from the north totaled six thousand eight hundred and eighty-three persons; this was the twenty-eighth year.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had followed him from the north numbered 6,883 in all—the year was the twenty-eighth year of Yuanjia.

sentences.zh: 虜毀其墳墓。

translations.literal: The barbarians destroyed their ancestral tombs.
translations.idiomatic: The northern enemy razed their family graves.

sentences.zh: 明年四月入朝，時燾已死，上更謀經略。

translations.literal: The next year in the fourth month he came to court; by then Tao was already dead, and the emperor renewed plans for strategic expansion.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the fourth month, he appeared at court. Tuoba Tao was dead by then, and the emperor turned once more to plans of northern conquest.

sentences.zh: 五月，遣爽、秀、程天祚等率步騎並荊州軍甲士四萬，出許、洛。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Shuang, Xiu, Cheng Tianzuo, and others were dispatched leading infantry and cavalry together with forty thousand armored soldiers of the Jing army, advancing from Xu and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the court sent Lu Shuang, Lu Xiu, Cheng Tianzuo, and others with infantry and cavalry—forty thousand armored men of the Jing army—to advance through Xu and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 八月，虜長社戍主永平公禿髮幡乃同棄城走。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the barbarian garrison commander of Changshe, Duke of Yongping Tufa Fan, and Nai Tong abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the enemy garrison chief at Changshe, Duke of Yongping Tufa Fan, fled the city together with Nai Tong.

sentences.zh: 進向大索戍，戍主偽豫州刺史跋僕蘭曰：「爽勇而無防，我今出城，必輕來據之，設伏檀山，必可禽也。」

translations.literal: Advancing toward the Dasuo garrison, the garrison commander, the false Governor of Yu Ba Pulan, said: "Shuang is brave but unwary; if I now leave the city, he will surely come lightly to occupy it; setting an ambush at Tanshan, he can certainly be captured."
translations.idiomatic: Marching on the Dasuo garrison, the rebel Governor of Yu, Ba Pulan, proposed: "Lu Shuang is bold but careless. If I quit the city, he will rush in to seize it—an ambush on Mount Tan will take him."

sentences.zh: 爽果夜進，秀諫不止，馳往繼之。

translations.literal: Shuang indeed advanced by night; Xiu's admonition could not stop him, and he galloped after to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shuang did advance by night; Lu Xiu's warnings failed to hold him back, and he raced after his brother.

sentences.zh: 比曉，虜騎夾發，賴秀縱兵力戰，虜乃退還虎牢。

translations.literal: By dawn, barbarian horsemen attacked from both sides; thanks to Xiu's unleashing his troops in fierce battle, the barbarians then withdrew to Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak enemy cavalry struck from both flanks; only Lu Xiu's desperate counterattack drove them back to Hulao.

sentences.zh: 爽因進攻之，本期舟師入河，斷其水門。

translations.literal: Shuang therefore pressed the attack; the original plan was for the river fleet to enter the river and cut off the water gate.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shuang pressed the assault, expecting the fleet to enter the river and block the waterworks.

sentences.zh: 王玄謨攻碻磝不拔，敗退，水軍不至，爽亦收眾南還。

translations.literal: Wang Xuamo attacked Que'ao without success and was defeated and withdrew; the river fleet did not arrive, and Shuang also gathered his troops and returned south.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuamo failed to take Que'ao and fell back in defeat; with the fleet never arriving, Lu Shuang too withdrew south.

sentences.zh: 轉鬬數百里，至曲彊，虜候其饑疲，盡銳來攻，爽身自奮擊，虜乃退走。

translations.literal: Fighting and turning for several hundred li, they reached Quqiang; the barbarians watched until they were hungry and weary, then threw their entire elite into the attack; Shuang personally fought fiercely, and the barbarians then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: After fighting retreat over hundreds of li to Quqiang, the enemy waited until Lu Shuang's men were hungry and exhausted, then threw their best troops at them. Shuang fought in the van himself and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 爽直出歷陽，自采石濟軍，與質水陸俱下。

translations.literal: Shuang went straight out through Liyang, crossed his army at Caishi, and with Zang Zhi descended together by land and water.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shuang marched straight on Liyang, ferried his army at Caishi, and joined Zang Zhi in a combined land-and-water advance.

sentences.zh: 爽遣弟瑜守蒙蘢，歷陽太守張幼緒請擊瑜，世祖配以兵力。

translations.literal: Shuang sent his brother Yu to hold Menglong; the Prefect of Liyang Zhang Youxu requested permission to attack Yu, and Emperor Xiaowu supplied him with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shuang left his brother Yu to hold Menglong. Zhang Youxu, Prefect of Liyang, asked to strike at Yu, and Emperor Xiaowu gave him the forces he requested.

sentences.zh: 遣左軍將薛安都步騎為前驅，別遣水軍入淵，分路竝會。

translations.literal: The Left Army General Xue Andu's infantry and cavalry were sent as vanguard; a separate river force was sent into the Yuan, converging by divided routes.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Andu, General of the Left Army, led infantry and cavalry as vanguard, while a separate fleet entered the Yuan—the columns to meet by separate routes.

sentences.zh: 安都進次大峴，爽已立營。

translations.literal: Andu advanced and encamped at Daxian; Shuang had already established camp.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Andu moved up to Daxian to find Lu Shuang already encamped.

sentences.zh: 世祖以賊強壘固，未可輕拔，使量宜進止。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu, because the rebels were strong and their fortifications solid, judged that they could not be lightly taken, and ordered action according to circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu judged the rebel position too strong for a hasty assault and ordered his commanders to advance or hold as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 幼緒便引軍退還，下獄。

translations.literal: Youxu then withdrew his army and returned, and was thrown into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Youxu nevertheless pulled his troops back and was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 更遣驍騎將軍垣護之代幼緒據歷陽。

translations.literal: The Valiant Cavalry General Yuan Huzhi was again dispatched to replace Youxu and hold Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: The court replaced him with Yuan Huzhi, Valiant Cavalry General, to hold Liyang.

sentences.zh: 鎮軍將軍沈慶之係安都進軍，與爽相遇於小峴。

translations.literal: The General Who Guards the Army Shen Qingzhi followed Andu in the advance and met Shuang at Xiaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qingzhi, General Who Guards the Army, followed Xue Andu's advance and encountered Lu Shuang at Xiaoxian.

sentences.zh: 爽親自前，將戰，而飲酒過醉，安都刺爽倒馬，左右范雙斬首，傳送京都。

translations.literal: Shuang personally went forward; about to fight, he was excessively drunk from wine; Andu stabbed Shuang, who fell from his horse; attendants Fan Shuang beheaded him and sent the head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shuang rode to the front to fight but was dead drunk. Xue Andu ran him through and toppled him from his horse; Fan Shuang, an attendant, took his head and sent it to the capital.

sentences.zh: 瑜亦為部下所斬送，進平壽陽，子弟竝伏誅。

translations.literal: Yu was also beheaded by his subordinates and sent in; they advanced and pacified Shouyang; younger brothers and sons were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was killed by his own men and his head sent in; the army took Shouyang, and Lu Shuang's brothers and sons were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 義宣初舉兵，召秀加節，進號征虜將軍，當繼諶之俱下。

translations.literal: When Prince Yi of Nanqiao first raised troops, he summoned Xiu with added staff, promoted him to General Who Punishes the Barbarians, and was to follow Liu Chenzhi in the descent.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yi of Nanqiao first rebelled, he called on Lu Xiu with full insignia, promoted him to General Who Punishes the Barbarians, and expected him to follow Liu Chenzhi south.

sentences.zh: 雝州刺史朱脩之起兵奉順，更遣秀擊脩之。

translations.literal: The Governor of Yong Zhu Xiuzhi raised troops in obedience to the throne; Xiu was again dispatched to attack Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Xiuzhi, Governor of Yong, rallied to the throne, Prince Yi sent Lu Xiu against him instead.

sentences.zh: 王玄謨聞之，喜曰：「魯秀不來，臧質易與耳。」

translations.literal: Wang Xuamo heard this and said with joy: "If Lu Xiu does not come, Zang Zhi will be easy to deal with."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuamo heard the news and exclaimed with delight: "Without Lu Xiu, Zang Zhi will be easy pickings."

sentences.zh: 秀至襄陽，大敗而反。

translations.literal: Xiu reached Xiangyang and returned after a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiu reached Xiangyang and was routed.

sentences.zh: 會益州刺史劉秀之遣軍襲江陵，秀擊破之。

translations.literal: It happened that the Governor of Yi Liu Xiuzhi dispatched troops to raid Jiangling; Xiu defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiuzhi, Governor of Yi, sent a column against Jiangling; Lu Xiu repulsed it.

sentences.zh: 義宣還江陵，秀與共北走，眾叛且盡。

translations.literal: Prince Yi returned to Jiangling; Xiu fled north with him; the host rebelled and was nearly gone.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi of Nanqiao withdrew to Jiangling; Lu Xiu fled north with him as their army melted away.

sentences.zh: 秀向城，上射之，中箭，赴水死，軍人宗敬叔、康僧念斬首，傳京邑。

translations.literal: Xiu turned toward the city; those above shot him, hit him with an arrow; he went into the water and died; soldiers Zong Jingshu and Kang Sengnian beheaded him and sent the head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiu turned toward the city walls; archers above struck him down. He threw himself into the water and drowned. Soldiers Zong Jingshu and Kang Sengnian cut off his head and sent it to the capital.

sentences.zh: 贈韋處穆、楊元駒給事中，庾騰之員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Wei Chumu and Yang Yuanju were posthumously granted Gentlemen Attendant at the Palace Gates; Yu Tengzhi was granted Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chumu and Yang Yuanju were posthumously made Gentlemen Attendant at the Palace Gates; Yu Tengzhi was posthumously made Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 爽初南歸，秀以爽武人，不閑吏職，白太祖請處穆為長史以輔爽，太祖以補司馬，後轉長史云。

translations.literal: When Shuang first returned south, Xiu, because Shuang was a military man unfamiliar with administrative duties, reported to Emperor Wen requesting Chumu as Chief Administrator to assist Shuang; Emperor Wen appointed him as Army Vice-Marshal, later transferred to Chief Administrator, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Shuang first defected south, Lu Xiu—knowing his brother was a soldier unversed in civil office—petitioned Emperor Wen to assign Wei Chumu as chief administrator to counsel him. The emperor first named Chumu vice-marshal, later chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之，字仲達，吳興武康人，司空慶之從父兄子也。

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi, style name Zhongda, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing, a son of the elder brother of the father of the Minister of Works Qingzhi's clan.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi, courtesy name Zhongda, came from Wukang in Wuxing commandery and was a cousin of the Minister of Works Shen Qingzhi.

sentences.zh: 父叔仁，為衡陽王義季征西長史，兼行參軍，領隊，又隨義季鎮彭城，度征北府。

translations.literal: His father Shuren served as Chief Administrator on Prince Hengyang Yiji's Western Campaign staff, concurrently Acting Staff Officer, leading a company; he also followed Yiji in garrisoning Pengcheng and crossing to the Northern Campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shuren served as chief administrator on Prince Yiji of Hengyang's western campaign staff, concurrently as acting staff officer and company commander. He followed Yiji to Pengcheng and then crossed to the northern expedition headquarters.

sentences.zh: 攸之少孤貧，元嘉二十七年，索虜南寇，發三吳民丁，攸之亦被發。

translations.literal: Youzhi from youth was orphaned and poor; in the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia, when the northern enemy raided south, the Three Wu districts conscripted civilian labor; Youzhi was also conscripted.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi was orphaned and poor as a youth. In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia, when the northern enemy invaded the south, the Three Wu districts drafted civilians—and he was among them.

sentences.zh: 既至京都，詣領軍將軍劉遵考，求補白丁隊主。

translations.literal: Having reached the capital, he went to the General Who Leads the Army Liu Zunkao and requested appointment as squad leader of common conscripts.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the capital, he sought out Liu Zunkao, General Who Leads the Army, and asked to be made squad leader of a conscript unit.

sentences.zh: 遵考謂之曰：「君形陋，不堪隊主。」

translations.literal: Zunkao said to him: "Your lordship's appearance is unsightly; you cannot serve as squad leader."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zunkao told him: "You are too homely in appearance to lead a squad."

sentences.zh: 因隨慶之征討。

translations.literal: He therefore followed Qingzhi on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore joined Shen Qingzhi on campaign instead.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，征西陽蠻，始補隊主。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, campaigning against the Xiyang barbarians, he was first appointed squad leader.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29, on the campaign against the Xiyang tribes, he received his first appointment as squad leader.

sentences.zh: 巴口建義，南中郎府板長史，兼行參軍。

translations.literal: At the righteous uprising at Bakou, the Southern Adjunct's headquarters provisionally appointed him Chief Administrator, concurrently Acting Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous cause was raised at Bakou, the southern adjunct's headquarters appointed him chief administrator and acting staff officer.

sentences.zh: 新亭之戰，身被重創，事寧，為太尉行參軍，封平洛縣五等侯。

translations.literal: In the battle at Xinting he was severely wounded; when affairs were settled, he became Acting Staff Officer of the Grand Marshal and was enfeoffed as Marquis of the fifth rank of Pingluo county.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Xinting he took grave wounds. After peace was restored he became acting staff officer to the Grand Marshal and was enfeoffed as Marquis of the fifth rank of Pingluo county.

sentences.zh: 隨府轉大司馬行參軍。

translations.literal: He followed the headquarters in transfer to Acting Staff Officer of the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the command to the post of acting staff officer to the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 晉世京邑二岸，揚州舊置都部從事，分掌二縣非違，永初以後罷省，孝建三年，復置其職。

translations.literal: In the Jin age the two banks of the capital, Yang Province formerly established Capital Department Attendants to divide supervision of offenses in the two counties; after Yongchu this was abolished; in the third year of Xiaojian the post was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jin, attendants of the capital department in Yang Province had overseen law and order on both banks of the Jiankang riverfront; the post lapsed after Yongchu but was restored in Xiaojian 3.

sentences.zh: 攸之掌北岸，會稽孔璨掌南岸，後又罷。

translations.literal: Youzhi managed the north bank; Kuaiji's Kong Can managed the south bank; afterward it was again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi took the north bank; Kong Can of Kuaiji the south—the office was abolished again soon after.

sentences.zh: 攸之遷員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Youzhi was transferred to Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi was promoted to supernumerary gentleman attendant cavalier.

sentences.zh: 又隨慶之征廣陵，屢有功，被箭破骨。

translations.literal: He again followed Qingzhi in the campaign at Guangling, repeatedly achieving merit, shot by an arrow that shattered bone.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Shen Qingzhi to Guangling, distinguishing himself repeatedly until an arrow shattered his bone.

sentences.zh: 世祖以其善戰，配以仇池步矟。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu, because of his skill in battle, paired him with a Congchi infantry pike.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu, valuing his prowess in battle, armed him with a Congchi pike.

sentences.zh: 事平，當加厚賞，為慶之所抑，遷太子旅賁中郎，攸之甚恨之。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, he ought to have received lavish reward, but was held back by Qingzhi; he was transferred to Central Commander of the Crown Prince's household guard; Youzhi greatly resented it.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign ended he deserved rich reward, but Shen Qingzhi blocked it; he was transferred to central commander of the crown prince's household guard—a slight Shen Youzhi bitterly resented.

sentences.zh: 七年，遭母憂，葬畢，起為龍驤將軍、武康令。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he suffered his mother's mourning; when the burial was complete, he was recalled as General of Agile Cavalry and Magistrate of Wukang.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven he mourned his mother; when the funeral rites were done he was recalled as General of Agile Cavalry and magistrate of Wukang.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝景和元年，除豫章王子尚車騎中兵參軍，直閣，與宗越、譚金等並為廢帝所寵，誅戮群公，攸之等皆為之用命。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinghe under the Former Deposed Emperor, he was appointed Central Army Staff Officer on Prince Zishang of Yuzhang's Chariots-and-Cavalry staff, Palace Attendant on Direct Duty; with Zong Yue, Tan Jin, and others he was all favored by the deposed emperor; when the deposed emperor executed the great nobles, Youzhi and the others all served at his command.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinghe 1 under the Former Deposed Emperor he was made central army staff officer on Prince Zishang of Yuzhang's staff and palace attendant on direct duty. He and Zong Yue, Tan Jin, and others were favorites of the tyrant; when the emperor slaughtered the great nobles, Shen Youzhi and his fellows carried out his orders.

sentences.zh: 封東興縣侯，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongxing county with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: The court enfeoffed him as Marquis of Dongxing county with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋遷右軍將軍，增邑百戶。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to General of the Right Army, with an increase of one hundred households to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to General of the Right Army with a hundred added households to his fief.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，以例削封。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming acceded, his enfeoffment was reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Shen Youzhi's fief was reduced by precedent.

sentences.zh: 宗越、譚金等謀反，攸之復召入直閣，除東海太守。

translations.literal: When Zong Yue, Tan Jin, and others plotted rebellion, Youzhi was again summoned to Palace Attendant on Direct Duty and appointed Prefect of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong Yue and Tan Jin plotted rebellion, Shen Youzhi was again called to palace duty and appointed prefect of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 未拜，會四方反叛，南賊已次近道，以攸之為寧朔將軍、尋陽太守，率軍據虎檻。

translations.literal: Before he took office, it happened that the four quarters rebelled; the southern rebels had already drawn near the route. Youzhi was made General of Pacifying the North and Prefect of Xunyang, leading troops to hold Hujian.
translations.idiomatic: Before Shen Youzhi could assume office, rebellions erupted across the realm and southern rebel forces were closing on the road. He was appointed General of Pacifying the North and Prefect of Xunyang and led troops to hold Hujian.

sentences.zh: 時王玄謨為大統，未發。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Xuamo was supreme commander and had not yet set out.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuamo then held supreme command but had not yet marched.

sentences.zh: 前鋒有五軍在虎檻，五軍後又絡驛繼至，每夜各立姓號，不相稟受。

translations.literal: The vanguard had five armies at Hujian; after them five more armies arrived in relay succession. Each night each set up its own surname and call-sign, not reporting to one another.
translations.idiomatic: Five vanguard armies were at Hujian, with more arriving in relays behind them. Each night every unit used its own family name and password, with no chain of command between them.

sentences.zh: 攸之謂軍吏曰：「今眾軍姓號不同，若有耕夫漁父，夜相呵叱，便致駭亂，取敗之道也。」

translations.literal: Youzhi said to the army clerks: "Now the armies' surname call-signs differ; if there were farmers or fishermen shouting at one another by night, it would cause panic and disorder—the way to defeat."
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi told the staff officers: "Our units all use different passwords now. If farmers or fishermen shouted at each other in the dark they would panic—and so would we. That is the road to defeat."

sentences.zh: 乃就一軍請號，眾咸從之。

translations.literal: He then went to one army to request its call-sign; all followed it.
translations.idiomatic: He unified the armies under one unit's password, and all complied.

sentences.zh: 殷孝祖為前鋒都督，而大失人情，攸之內撫將士，外諧群帥，眾並倚賴之。

translations.literal: Yin Xiaozu was vanguard commander but greatly lost men's hearts. Youzhi inwardly comforted officers and soldiers and outwardly harmonized with the various commanders; all relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Xiaozu commanded the vanguard but had lost the troops' loyalty. Shen Youzhi mollified the ranks within and kept the other generals on side; everyone looked to him.

sentences.zh: 時南賊前鋒鍾沖之、薛常寶等屯據赭圻，殷孝祖率眾軍攻之，為流矢所中死，軍主范潛率五百人投賊，人情震駭，並謂攸之宜代孝祖為統。

translations.literal: At the time the southern rebels' vanguard Zhong Chongzhi, Xue Changbao, and others were encamped at Zheqi. Yin Xiaozu led the army host to attack them, was struck by a stray arrow and died. Army Commander Fan Qian led five hundred men to defect to the rebels. Popular sentiment was shocked; all said Youzhi ought to replace Xiaozu as commander.
translations.idiomatic: Southern rebel vanguard Zhong Chongzhi and Xue Changbao held Zheqi. Yin Xiaozu attacked and was killed by a stray arrow. Army commander Fan Qian took five hundred men over to the enemy. Morale collapsed, and officers agreed Shen Youzhi should succeed Xiaozu.

sentences.zh: 時建安王休仁屯虎檻，揔統眾軍，聞孝祖死，遣寧朔將軍江方興、龍驤將軍劉靈遺各率三千人赴赭圻。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Jian'an Xiuren was encamped at Hujian, commanding all armies. Hearing of Xiaozu's death, he dispatched General of Pacifying the North Jiang Fangxing and General of Agile Cavalry Liu Lingyi, each leading three thousand men, to Zheqi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiuren of Jian'an held Hujian in overall command. On hearing of Xiaozu's death he sent Jiang Fangxing, General of Pacifying the North, and Liu Lingyi, General of Agile Cavalry, each with three thousand men, to Zheqi.

sentences.zh: 攸之以為孝祖既死，賊有乘勝之心，明日若不更攻，則示之以弱。

translations.literal: Youzhi considered that since Xiaozu was dead, the rebels had the mind to press their victory; if they did not attack again tomorrow, it would show them weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi reasoned that with Xiaozu dead the enemy would think they had won; failing to attack again the next day would look like weakness.

sentences.zh: 方興名位相亞，必不為己下，軍政不一，致敗之由。

translations.literal: Fangxing's name and rank were nearly equal; he would surely not be subordinate to himself. Military and civil affairs not unified—that was the cause of defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Fangxing's rank matched his own; he would never take orders from him. Divided command was a sure route to defeat.

sentences.zh: 乃率諸軍主詣方興，謂之曰：「四方並反，國家所保，無復百里之地。

translations.literal: He then led the army commanders to Fangxing and said to him: "The four quarters all rebel together; what the state can preserve is no longer territory of even a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: He took the army commanders to Fangxing and said: "The realm is in revolt; what the throne still holds is less than a hundred li of ground.

sentences.zh: 唯有殷孝祖為朝廷所委賴，鋒鏑裁交，輿尸而反，文武喪氣，朝野危心。

translations.literal: Only Yin Xiaozu was entrusted and relied upon by the court; blades had barely crossed when they returned bearing the corpse on a cart. Civil and military lost spirit; court and country were in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yin Xiaozu was the court's chosen champion—blades had barely crossed when his body came back on a cart. Officers and officials alike lost heart; court and country trembled.

sentences.zh: 事之濟否，唯在明旦一戰，戰若不捷，則大事去矣。

translations.literal: Whether the affair succeeds depends solely on tomorrow's one battle; if the battle is not victorious, then the great enterprise is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Success or failure hangs on tomorrow's fight alone. Lose it and all is lost.

sentences.zh: 詰朝之事，諸人咸謂吾應統之，自卜懦薄，幹略不辦及卿，今輒相推為統。

translations.literal: For tomorrow's affair, all men say I ought to take command. Measuring myself as timid and shallow, my capacity and strategy cannot match yours; now I rashly defer to you as commander.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone expects me to take command tomorrow. I know myself too timid and my generalship no match for yours—so I am deferring command to you.

sentences.zh: 但當相與戮力爾。」

translations.literal: Only let us exert strength together."
translations.idiomatic: We need only fight together with all our strength.

sentences.zh: 方興甚悅。

translations.literal: Fangxing was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Fangxing was delighted.

sentences.zh: 攸之既出，諸軍主並尤之，攸之曰：「卿忘廉、藺、寇、賈之事邪？

translations.literal: After Youzhi went out, all the army commanders together faulted him. Youzhi said: "Have you forgotten the affairs of Lian and Lin, Kou and Jia?
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi left, the other commanders blamed him. He said: "Have you forgotten Lian Po and Lin Xiangru—or Kou Yun and Jia Yi?

sentences.zh: 吾本以濟國活家，豈計彼此之升降。

translations.literal: I originally meant to save the state and preserve the family—how could I reckon mutual rise and fall?
translations.idiomatic: I aim to save the realm and our households—not to haggle over who ranks above whom.

sentences.zh: 且我能下彼，彼必不能下我，共濟艱難，豈可自厝同異！」
