translations.literal: Moreover, I can subordinate myself to him, but he surely cannot subordinate himself to me. Together crossing difficulties—how can one set aside differences!"
translations.idiomatic: I can yield to him; he would never yield to me. In crisis we must pull together—not pick quarrels!"

sentences.zh: 明旦進戰，自寅訖午，大破賊於赭圻城外，追奔至姥山，分遣水軍乘勢進討；

translations.literal: The next morning they advanced to battle; from the yin hour till noon they greatly defeated the rebels outside Zheqi city, pursued the rout to Laoshan, and separately dispatched the river army to press the advantage in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Next morning they fought from dawn till noon, routing the rebels outside Zheqi and chasing them to Laoshan, while a river column pressed the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 又破其水軍，拔胡、白二城。

translations.literal: They again defeated the rebels' river army and took the two cities Hu and Bai.
translations.idiomatic: They crushed the enemy fleet too and took the cities of Hu and Bai.

sentences.zh: 尋假攸之節，進號輔國將軍，代孝祖督前鋒諸軍事。

translations.literal: Soon Youzhi was granted a staff, promoted to General Who Supports the State, replacing Xiaozu in supervising vanguard military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given full insignia and promoted to General Who Supports the State, succeeding Xiaozu as commander of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 薛常寶在赭圻食盡，南賊大帥劉胡屯濃湖，以囊盛米繫流查及船腹，陽覆船，順風流下，以餉赭圻。

translations.literal: Xue Changbao at Zheqi had exhausted food. The southern rebels' grand commander Liu Hu was encamped at Nonghu; using sacks holding rice tied to floating rafts and ship bellies, feigning capsized ships, they drifted down with the wind to supply Zheqi.
translations.idiomatic: With Xue Changbao starving at Zheqi, rebel commander Liu Hu at Nonghu loaded rice into sacks lashed to rafts and hulls, feigning wrecks to drift supplies downwind to Zheqi.

sentences.zh: 攸之疑其有異，遣人取船及流查，大得囊米。

translations.literal: Youzhi suspected something amiss, sent men to take the ships and floating rafts, and greatly obtained sack rice.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi suspected a trick, seized the craft and rafts, and captured a great haul of rice.

sentences.zh: 攸之從子懷寶，為賊將帥，在赭圻，遣親人楊公贊齎密書招誘攸之，攸之斬公贊，封懷寶書呈太宗。

translations.literal: Youzhi's nephew Huaibao served as a rebel commander at Zheqi; he sent his kinsman Yang Gongzan bearing a secret letter to entice Youzhi. Youzhi beheaded Gongzan, sealed Huaibao's letter and presented it to Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Huaibao commanded rebels at Zheqi and sent Yang Gongzan with a secret letter to win Shen Youzhi over. Shen Youzhi executed Gongzan and forwarded the sealed letter to Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 尋克赭圻，遷使持節、督雍、梁、南、北秦四州、郢州之竟陵諸軍事、冠軍將軍、領寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon Zheqi was taken. He was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Commander of military affairs for Yong, Liang, South Qin, and North Qin four provinces and Ying's Jingling, General Who Championed the State, Colonel Director of Barbarian Affairs, and Governor of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Zheqi fell soon after. He was made Bearer of the Staff, commander of Yong, Liang, southern and northern Qin, and Ying's Jingling, General Who Championed the State, Colonel Director of Barbarian Affairs, and Governor of Yong.

sentences.zh: 袁顗復率大眾來入鵲尾，相持既久，軍主張興世越鵲尾上據錢溪，劉胡自攻之。

translations.literal: Yuan Yi again led a great host to enter Quewei. After a long standoff, Army Commander Zhang Xingshi crossed above Quewei and seized Qianxi; Liu Hu himself attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi returned with a great army at Quewei. After a long stalemate Zhang Xingshi slipped above Quewei to hold Qianxi, and Liu Hu attacked him in person.

sentences.zh: 攸之率諸將攻濃湖，顗遣人傳唱錢溪已平，眾竝懼。

translations.literal: Youzhi led the generals to attack Nonghu. Yi sent men to spread word that Qianxi had fallen; the host together feared.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi led the generals against Nonghu. Yuan Yi spread word that Qianxi had fallen, and panic spread through the ranks.

sentences.zh: 攸之曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Youzhi said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi said: "That cannot be true.

sentences.zh: 若錢溪實敗，萬人中應有逃亡得還者。

translations.literal: If Qianxi were truly defeated, among ten thousand men there ought to be fugitives who escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: If Qianxi had truly fallen, some of ten thousand men would have fled back to us.

sentences.zh: 必是彼戰失利，唱空聲以惑眾耳。」

translations.literal: It must be that they suffered defeat in battle and are spreading empty rumors to confuse the host."
translations.idiomatic: They lost a fight and are bluffing to unsettle us."

sentences.zh: 勒軍中不得妄動。

translations.literal: He ordered the army not to move rashly.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade any rash movement in the ranks.

sentences.zh: 錢溪信尋至，果大破賊。

translations.literal: Report from Qianxi soon arrived; indeed the rebels were greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: News from Qianxi soon arrived: Zhang Xingshi had indeed routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 攸之悉以錢溪所送胡軍耳鼻示之，顗駭懼，急追胡還。

translations.literal: Youzhi fully displayed the noses and ears of Liu Hu's army sent from Qianxi. Yi was shocked and afraid and urgently recalled Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi paraded the severed noses and ears Liu Hu's men had sent from Qianxi. Yuan Yi panicked and recalled Liu Hu at once.

sentences.zh: 攸之諸軍悉力進攻，多所斬獲，日暮引歸。

translations.literal: Youzhi's armies all exerted strength in the attack, beheading and capturing many; at dusk they withdrew and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi's columns pressed the attack hard, taking many heads and prisoners, then withdrew at dusk.

sentences.zh: 鵲尾食盡，遣千人往南陵迎米，為臺軍所破，燒其資實，胡於是棄眾而奔，顗亦叛走。

translations.literal: Quewei's food was exhausted; they sent a thousand men to Nanling to fetch rice. They were defeated by the imperial army, which burned their supplies. Hu thereupon abandoned the host and fled; Yi also rebelled and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Starving at Quewei, the rebels sent a thousand men to Nanling for grain. Imperial troops destroyed them and burned their stores. Liu Hu fled with a remnant; Yuan Yi bolted too.

sentences.zh: 赭圻、濃湖之平也，賊軍委棄資財，珍貨殷積，諸軍各競收斂，以強弱為少多。

translations.literal: When Zheqi and Nonghu were pacified, the rebel army abandoned supplies and treasures piled in abundance; each army competed to gather them, more or less according to strength.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheqi and Nonghu fell the rebels left fortunes behind. Every unit scrambled for loot, each according to its strength.

sentences.zh: 唯攸之、張興世約勒所部，不犯秋毫，諸將以此多之。

translations.literal: Only Youzhi and Zhang Xingshi restrained their troops, not violating the slightest; the generals for this praised them.
translations.idiomatic: Only Shen Youzhi and Zhang Xingshi kept their men from touching a thing. The other generals respected them for it.

sentences.zh: 攸之進平尋陽，徙監郢州諸軍事、前將軍、郢州刺史，持節如故。

translations.literal: Youzhi advanced and pacified Xunyang; was transferred to Supervisor of Military Affairs for Ying Province, General of the Vanguard, and Governor of Ying, Bearer of the Staff as before.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi took Xunyang and was appointed supervisor of Ying military affairs, General of the Vanguard, and Governor of Ying, retaining Bearer of the Staff.

sentences.zh: 不拜，遷中領軍，封貞陽縣公，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: He did not accept; was transferred to Central Army Commander, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhenyang county with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the post and was made Central Army Commander instead, enfeoffed Duke of Zhenyang with two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 時四方皆已平定，徐州刺史薛安都據彭城請降，上雖相酬許，而辭旨簡略。

translations.literal: At the time the four quarters were all already pacified. Xue Andu, Governor of Xu, holding Pengcheng, requested surrender. The emperor though reciprocating agreement, yet his wording was brief and sparse.
translations.idiomatic: With the realm pacified, Xue Andu holding Pengcheng as Governor of Xu offered surrender. The emperor agreed in principle but his reply was terse and cool.

sentences.zh: 攸之前將軍，置佐吏，假節，與鎮軍將軍張永以重兵徵安都。

translations.literal: Youzhi as General of the Vanguard, with aides appointed and granted staff, together with General Who Guards the Army Zhang Yong with heavy troops summoned Andu.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi went as General of the Vanguard with a full staff and delegated authority, joining Zhang Yong, General Who Guards the Army, with a strong force to accept Andu's surrender.

sentences.zh: 安都懼，要引索虜；

translations.literal: Andu feared and sought to bring in the northern enemy;
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a trap, Andu called in the northern enemy;

sentences.zh: 索虜引大眾援之。

translations.literal: the northern enemy brought a great host to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: who sent a great army to his aid.

sentences.zh: 攸之等米船在呂梁，又遣軍主王穆之上民口；

translations.literal: Youzhi and the others' rice ships were at Lüliang; they also dispatched Army Commander Wang Muzhi upriver with the civilian population;
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi's grain fleet lay at Lüliang, and he sent Wang Muzhi upriver with the civilian population;

sentences.zh: 穆之為虜攻覆米船，又破運車於武原，攸之等引退，為虜所乘，又值寒雪，士眾墮指十二三。

translations.literal: Muzhi was attacked by the barbarians and the rice ships were capsized; they also defeated transport carts at Wuyuan. Youzhi and the others withdrew, pursued by the barbarians; moreover encountering cold snow, ten or twenty percent of soldiers and host lost fingers to frostbite.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy overturned the grain ships and smashed transport wagons at Wuyuan. Shen Youzhi fell back under pursuit in driving snow; ten or twenty percent of his men lost fingers to frostbite.

sentences.zh: 留長水校尉王玄載守下邳，積射將軍沈韶守宿豫，睢陵、淮陽亦置戍，攸之還淮陰。

translations.literal: Long Waters Colonel Wang Xuanzai was left to guard Xiapi; General of Accumulated Archers Shen Shao to guard Suyu; Suiling and Huaiyang also had garrisons placed; Youzhi returned to Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuanzai, Long Waters Colonel, held Xiapi; Shen Shao, General of Accumulated Archers, held Suyu; garrisons were posted at Suiling and Huaiyang; Shen Youzhi withdrew to Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 免官，以公領職。

translations.literal: He was dismissed from office, yet served in his ducal capacity.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of office but kept his title and duties as duke.

sentences.zh: 復求進討，上不聽，入朝面陳，又不許，復歸淮陰。

translations.literal: He again requested to advance in attack; the emperor did not assent. He came to court to state in person, again was not permitted, and again returned to Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to resume the offensive; the emperor refused. He came to court to plead in person and was refused again, then returned to Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 三年六月，自率運送米下邳，并鑿四周深塹，遣龍驤將軍垣護之領民口還淮陰。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year, he personally led transport of rice to Xiapi, and dug deep moats on all four sides, dispatching General of Agile Cavalry Yuan Huzhi to lead the civilian population back to Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year three he personally convoyed grain to Xiapi, dug deep outer trenches, and sent Yuan Huzhi, General of Agile Cavalry, to escort the civilian population back to Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 時軍主陳顯達當領千兵守下邳，攸之留待顯達至，虜遣清泗間人詐告攸之云：「安都欲降，求軍迎接。」

translations.literal: At the time Army Commander Chen Xianda was to lead a thousand troops to guard Xiapi; Youzhi stayed waiting for Xianda to arrive. The barbarians sent men of the Qing and Si region with a false report to Youzhi saying: "Andu wishes to surrender and requests the army come receive him."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xianda was due to take a thousand men to Xiapi; Shen Youzhi waited for him. Enemy agents from the Qing and Si region falsely told Shen Youzhi that Andu wanted to surrender and asked for an escort.

sentences.zh: 攸之副吳喜納其說，咸謂宜遣千人參之，既而來者轉多，喜所執彌固。

translations.literal: Youzhi's aide Wu Xi accepted the story; all said a thousand men ought to be sent to join. Thereafter those coming gradually increased, and Xi's insistence grew firmer.
translations.idiomatic: His aide Wu Xi believed it, and others urged sending a thousand men. More messengers kept coming, and Wu Xi dug in.

sentences.zh: 攸之乃集來者告之，語曰：「薛徐州早宜還朝，今能爾，深副本望。

translations.literal: Youzhi then assembled those who came and told them, saying: "Prefect Xue of Xu ought long ago to have returned to court; that he can do so now deeply matches my hope.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi then gathered the messengers and said: "Prefect Xue of Xu should have returned to court long ago. That he is ready now is exactly what I hoped for.

sentences.zh: 但遣子弟一人來，便當遣大軍相接。

translations.literal: But send one younger kinsman, and I shall at once dispatch a great army to meet you.
translations.idiomatic: Send one of his younger kinsmen and I will dispatch a great force to receive you.

sentences.zh: 君諸人既有志心，若能與薛子弟俱來者，皆即假君以本鄉縣，唯意所欲；

translations.literal: You gentlemen already have loyal intent; if you can come together with Xue's younger kinsmen, I shall at once provisionally grant you your native commanderies and counties, as you wish;
translations.idiomatic: If you are truly loyal and come with Xue's kinsmen, I will appoint each of you magistrate of your home district, as you choose;

sentences.zh: 如其不爾，無為空勞往還。」

translations.literal: if it is not so, do not toil in vain going back and forth."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise do not waste your time on empty journeys."

sentences.zh: 自此一去不反。

translations.literal: From this one dispatch, none returned.
translations.idiomatic: None of those who went ever came back.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，太宗復令攸之進圍彭城。

translations.literal: That autumn, Emperor Ming again ordered Youzhi to advance and besiege Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Emperor Ming again ordered Shen Youzhi to besiege Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 攸之以清泗既乾，糧運不繼，固執以為非宜，往反者七。

translations.literal: Youzhi, because the Qing and Si were already dry and grain transport could not continue, stubbornly held it was not suitable; seven round trips of debate.
translations.idiomatic: With the Qing and Si rivers dry and supplies cut off, Shen Youzhi argued hard that the campaign was ill-advised—seven exchanges back and forth.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，詔攸之曰：「卿春中求伐彭城，吾恐軍士疲勞，且去冬奔散，人心未宜復用，不許卿所啟。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and issued an edict to Youzhi: "You in spring requested to attack Pengcheng; I feared the soldiers would be weary and moreover last winter's rout—men's hearts were not yet fit to be used again; I did not permit your petition.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and wrote Shen Youzhi: "In spring you asked to attack Pengcheng. I feared your men were exhausted and, after last winter's rout, not fit to fight again—so I refused.

sentences.zh: 今便不肯為吾行邪？

translations.literal: Now you refuse to act for me?
translations.idiomatic: Now you refuse to march for me?

sentences.zh: 卿若不行，便可使吳喜獨去。」

translations.literal: If you will not go, I can send Wu Xi alone."
translations.idiomatic: If you refuse to march, Wu Xi can go in your place."

sentences.zh: 攸之懼，乃奉旨進軍。

translations.literal: Youzhi feared and then obeyed the edict and advanced the army.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Shen Youzhi obeyed and marched.

sentences.zh: 行至遲墟，上悔，追軍令反。

translations.literal: Marching to Chixu, the emperor regretted and sent orders to recall the army.
translations.idiomatic: At Chixu the emperor changed his mind and ordered the army back.

sentences.zh: 攸之還至下邳，而陳顯達於睢口為虜所破，龍驤將軍姜產之、司徒參軍高遵世戰沒。

translations.literal: Youzhi returned to Xiapi, while Chen Xianda at Sui mouth was defeated by the barbarians; General of Agile Cavalry Jiang Chanzhi and Staff Officer of the Minister of Works Gao Zunshi died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi was back at Xiapi when Chen Xianda was crushed at Sui mouth; Jiang Chanzhi, General of Agile Cavalry, and Gao Zunshi, staff officer to the Minister of Works, were killed.

sentences.zh: 虜追攸之甚急，因交戰，被矟創，會暮，引軍入顯達壘，夕眾散，八月十八日也。

translations.literal: The barbarians pursued Youzhi very urgently; in the fighting he received a pike wound. Meeting dusk, he led the army into Xianda's fort; by evening the host dispersed—the eighteenth day of the eighth month.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy pressed Shen Youzhi hard. He took a pike wound in the fighting, reached Chen Xianda's camp at dusk, and by nightfall his army had melted away—on the eighteenth of the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 攸之棄眾南奔。

translations.literal: Youzhi abandoned the host and fled south.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi abandoned his army and fled south.

sentences.zh: 初，吳興丘幼弼、丘隆先、沈誕、沈榮守、吳陸道量，並以文記之才隨攸之，及張永北討，永一奔，攸之再敗，幼弼等並皆陷沒。

translations.literal: Initially, Wuxing's Qiu Youbi, Qiu Longxian, Shen Dan, Shen Rongshou, and Wu Ludao all followed Youzhi for their literary and record-keeping talent. When Zhang Yong's northern campaign—Yong fled once, Youzhi was defeated twice—Youbi and the others all perished.
translations.idiomatic: Wuxing men Qiu Youbi, Qiu Longxian, Shen Dan, Shen Rongshou, and Wu Ludao had joined Shen Youzhi for their clerical and literary skills. Zhang Yong fled once in the northern campaign; Shen Youzhi lost twice—and all of them perished.

sentences.zh: 攸之之還淮陰，以為持節、假冠軍將軍、行南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: When Youzhi returned to Huaiyin, he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Acting General Who Champions the State, and Acting Governor of South Yan.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to Huaiyin he was made Bearer of the Staff, acting General Who Champions the State, and acting Governor of South Yan.

sentences.zh: 追贈姜產之左軍將軍，高遵世屯騎校尉。

translations.literal: Jiang Chanzhi was posthumously granted General of the Left Army; Gao Zunshi Colonel of Garrison Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Chanzhi was posthumously made General of the Left Army; Gao Zunshi Colonel of Garrison Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 四年，徵攸之為吳興太守，辭不拜。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Youzhi was summoned as Prefect of Wuxing; he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In year four the court summoned him as Prefect of Wuxing; he refused.

sentences.zh: 乃除左衛將軍，領太子中庶子。

translations.literal: He was then appointed General of the Left Guard, concurrently Grand Supervisor of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General of the Left Guard and grand supervisor of the crown prince's household instead.

sentences.zh: 五年，出為持節、監郢州諸軍、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he went out as Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of Military Affairs for Ying Province, and Governor of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he was posted as Bearer of the Staff, supervisor of Ying military affairs, and Governor of Ying.

sentences.zh: 為政刻暴，或鞭士大夫，上佐以下有忤意，輒面加詈辱。

translations.literal: In governing he was harsh and cruel; sometimes he whipped scholar-officials. From chief aides downward, whoever offended his mind, he immediately added curses and insults to their faces.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was brutal: he whipped gentry officials and publicly abused any subordinate who crossed him, chief aides on down.

sentences.zh: 將吏一人亡叛，同籍符伍充代者十餘人。

translations.literal: When one officer or clerk deserted, more than ten men of the same household register and mutual-responsibility groups were pressed as replacements.
translations.idiomatic: One deserter meant more than ten men from his register and mutual-responsibility group were conscripted to replace him.

sentences.zh: 而曉達吏事，自強不息，士民畏憚，人莫敢欺。

translations.literal: Yet he was skilled in administrative affairs, ceaselessly strengthening himself; officers and people feared and respected him; no one dared deceive.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he knew administration inside out, drove himself relentlessly, and was so feared that no one dared cheat him.

sentences.zh: 聞有虎，輒自圍捕，往無不得，一日或得兩三。

translations.literal: Hearing there was a tiger, he always personally encircled and captured it; going, none were not obtained; in one day sometimes two or three.
translations.idiomatic: At word of a tiger he hunted it in person and never missed—sometimes two or three in a day.

sentences.zh: 若逼暮不獲禽，則宿昔圍守，須曉自出。

translations.literal: If near dusk he did not capture the beast, then he encamped overnight encircling it and waited till dawn to come out himself.
translations.idiomatic: If dusk found him empty-handed he camped on the ring and waited till morning to bring the beast out.

sentences.zh: 賦斂嚴苦，徵發無度，繕治船舸，營造器甲。

translations.literal: Tax levies were severe and bitter; conscription without measure; repairing ships and boats, building weapons and armor.
translations.idiomatic: He taxed harshly, conscripted without limit, and built ships and arms.

sentences.zh: 自至夏口，便有異圖。

translations.literal: From the time he reached Xiakou, he already had a separate design.
translations.idiomatic: From the moment he reached Xiakou he was already plotting.

sentences.zh: 六年，進監豫州之西陽、司州之義陽二郡軍事，進號鎮軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he advanced to supervising military affairs of Xiyang in Yu and Yiyang in Si two commanderies, promoted to General Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he was made supervisor of Xiyang in Yu and Yiyang in Si and promoted to General Who Guards the Army.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史桂陽王休範密有異志，以微旨動攸之，使道士陳公昭作天公書一函，題云「沈丞相」，送付攸之門者；

translations.literal: Governor of Jiang Liu Xiufan of Guiyang secretly harbored a separate intent; with subtle words he moved Youzhi, having the Daoist Chen Gongzhao compose one letter from the Lord of Heaven, inscribed "Minister Shen," sent to Youzhi's gate;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiufan of Guiyang, Governor of Jiang, nursed secret ambitions and sounded Shen Youzhi out, having the Daoist Chen Gongzhao write a "heavenly decree" addressed to "Minister Shen" and deliver it to Shen Youzhi's gate;

sentences.zh: 攸之不開書，推得公昭，送之朝廷。

translations.literal: Youzhi did not open the letter, tracked down Gongzhao, and sent him to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi never opened the letter, traced the messenger to Chen Gongzhao, and sent him to court.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽二年，休範舉兵襲京邑，攸之謂僚佐曰：「桂陽今反朝廷，必聲云與攸之同。

translations.literal: Later, in the second year of Yuanhui under the Deposed Emperor Houfei, Xiufan raised troops and raided the capital. Youzhi said to his aides: "Guiyang now rebels against the court; he is sure to claim aloud that he acts with Youzhi.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhui year two under Emperor Houfei, Xiufan rebelled and struck the capital. Shen Youzhi told his staff: "Xiufan will surely claim I am in league with him.

sentences.zh: 若不顛沛勤王，必增朝野之惑。」

translations.literal: If we do not rush in turmoil to serve the throne, we will only increase court and country's confusion."
translations.idiomatic: Unless we march at once to defend the throne, court and country will only grow more confused."

sentences.zh: 於是遣軍主孫同、沈懷奧興軍馳下，受郢州刺史晉熙王燮節度。

translations.literal: Thereupon he dispatched Army Commanders Sun Tong and Shen Huai'ao to raise troops and race down, accepting the orders of Jinxi Prince Xie, Governor of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: He sent army commanders Sun Tong and Shen Huai'ao south at speed under the command of Prince Xie of Jinxi, Governor of Ying.

sentences.zh: 同等始過夏口，會休範平，還。

translations.literal: Tong and the others had just passed Xiakou when Xiufan was pacified; they returned.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Tong's column had barely passed Xiakou when Xiufan was crushed, and they turned back.

sentences.zh: 進攸之號征西大將軍、開府儀同三司，固讓開府。

translations.literal: Youzhi was promoted to General on Campaign West, Grand Master with honors equal to the Three Excellencies; he firmly declined the Grand Master establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi was promoted to General on Campaign West with Grand Master honors equal to the Three Excellencies, but firmly declined the grand establishment.

sentences.zh: 攸之自擅閫外，朝廷疑憚之，累欲徵入，慮不受命，乃止。

translations.literal: Youzhi on his own monopolized power beyond the borders; the court suspected and feared him, repeatedly wished to summon him in, fearing he would not accept orders, and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Holding power on the frontier, Shen Youzhi alarmed the court, which repeatedly tried to recall him but desisted for fear he would refuse.

sentences.zh: 群公稱皇太后令，遣中使問攸之曰：「久勞於外，宜還京輦，然任寄之重，換代殊為未易，還止之宜，一以相委。」

translations.literal: The high ministers invoked an order of the Empress Dowager and dispatched a palace envoy to ask Youzhi: "Long laboring abroad, you ought to return to the capital carriage; yet the weight of your commission makes replacement especially difficult. Whether to return or remain—the choice is entirely entrusted to you."
translations.idiomatic: Senior officials cited an empress-dowager order and sent a palace envoy to ask Shen Youzhi: "You have long served on the frontier and ought to return to the capital; yet your post is too weighty to replace easily. Whether to come back or stay—we leave the decision to you.

sentences.zh: 欲以觀察其意。

translations.literal: They wished thereby to observe his intent.
translations.idiomatic: They meant to read his intentions.

sentences.zh: 攸之答曰：「荷國重恩，名器至此，自惟凡陋，本無廊廟之姿。

translations.literal: Youzhi replied: "Bearing the state's heavy grace, my name and office have reached this point. Reflecting on myself as common and base, I originally had no stature for the hall of state.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi replied: "The throne has heaped honor on me, yet I know my own mediocrity—I was never cut out for court.

sentences.zh: 至如戍防一蕃，撲討蠻蜓，可強充斯任。

translations.literal: As for guarding one frontier and striking down barbarian tribes, I can barely fill that post.
translations.idiomatic: Guarding a frontier and fighting barbarians is work I can just manage.

sentences.zh: 雖自上如此，豈敢厝心去留，歸還之事，伏聽朝旨。」

translations.literal: Though the throne speaks so, how dare I set my heart on staying or leaving? On returning to court, I await the court's command."
translations.idiomatic: Whatever Your Majesty prefers, I dare not choose for myself. If I am to return, I await your order."

sentences.zh: 朝廷逾懾憚，徵議遂息。

translations.literal: The court increasingly feared; the summons plan then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The court grew only more alarmed, and talk of recall died away.

sentences.zh: 四年，建平王景素據京城反，攸之復應朝廷；

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Prince of Jianping Jing Su held the capital and rebelled; Youzhi again responded to the court;
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhui year four Prince Jing Su of Jianping rebelled in the capital; Shen Youzhi again rallied to the throne;

sentences.zh: 景素尋平。

translations.literal: Jing Su was soon pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Su was soon crushed.

sentences.zh: 初元嘉中，巴東、建平二郡，軍府富實，與江夏、竟陵、武陵並為名郡。

translations.literal: At the beginning, in Yuanjia, the two commanderies Badong and Jianping—the military headquarters were rich and solid, together with Jiangxia, Jingling, and Wuling all famed commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: In early Yuanjia, Badong and Jianping—with their military headquarters—ranked with Jiangxia, Jingling, and Wuling among the empire's richest commanderies.

sentences.zh: 世祖于江夏置郢州，郡罷軍府，竟陵、武陵亦並殘壞，巴東、建平為峽中蠻所破，至是民人流散，存者無幾。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu at Jiangxia established Ying Province; the commandery abolished the military headquarters; Jingling and Wuling also together were ruined; Badong and Jianping were broken by barbarians in the gorges; by this time the people scattered, those surviving were few.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu created Ying Province at Jiangxia, abolishing those headquarters. Jingling and Wuling fell to ruin too; gorge tribes ravaged Badong and Jianping until almost no one remained.

sentences.zh: 其年春，攸之遣軍入峽討蠻帥田五郡等。

translations.literal: That spring, Youzhi dispatched troops into the gorges to punish barbarian chieftain Tian Wujun and others.
translations.idiomatic: That spring Shen Youzhi sent troops into the gorges against the tribal chief Tian Wujun and others.

sentences.zh: 及景素反，攸之急追峽中軍，巴東太守劉攘兵、建平太守劉道欣並疑攸之自有異志，阻兵斷峽，不聽軍下。

translations.literal: When Jing Su rebelled, Youzhi urgently pursued the gorge army; Liu Rangbing, Prefect of Badong, and Liu Daoxin, Prefect of Jianping, both suspected Youzhi of harboring his own ambitions, blocked troops and cut the gorges, and would not let the army descend.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jing Su rebelled, Shen Youzhi pressed hard after the gorge army. Liu Rangbing, Prefect of Badong, and Liu Daoxin, Prefect of Jianping, both suspected Shen Youzhi of his own designs; they blocked the passes with troops and would not let his army come down.

sentences.zh: 時攘兵元子天賜為荊州西曹，攸之遣天賜譬說之，令其解甲，一無所問。

translations.literal: At the time Rangbing's eldest son Tianci served as Western Assistant of Jing Province; Youzhi sent Tianci to persuade him, ordering him to lay down arms with no questions asked.
translations.idiomatic: Rangbing's eldest son Tianci was then Western Assistant of Jing Province. Shen Youzhi sent Tianci to persuade his father, promising that if he disarmed, no account would be taken of the offense.

sentences.zh: 攘兵見天賜，知景素實反，乃釋甲謝愆，攸之待之如故，後以攘兵為府司馬。

translations.literal: Rangbing saw Tianci and learned Jing Su had truly rebelled; he then laid down arms and apologized for his fault. Youzhi treated him as before, and later made Rangbing Chief of Staff of his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Rangbing saw Tianci, he learned that Jing Su had indeed rebelled. He laid down his arms and apologized for his fault. Shen Youzhi treated him as before and later appointed him chief of staff of his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 劉道欣堅守建平，攘兵譬說不回，乃與伐蠻軍攻之，破建平，斬道欣。

translations.literal: Liu Daoxin held firm at Jianping; Rangbing's persuasion did not turn him back. Youzhi then joined the barbarian-suppression army in attacking him, broke Jianping, and beheaded Daoxin.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daoxin held fast at Jianping and would not be swayed even by Rangbing's pleading. Shen Youzhi then joined the barbarian-suppression force in the attack, took Jianping, and executed Daoxin.

sentences.zh: 臺直閣高道慶家在江陵，攸之初至州，道慶時在家，牒其親戚十餘人，求州從事西曹，攸之為用三人。

translations.literal: Gao Daoqing of the Direct Retinue of the Palace had his family in Jiangling. When Youzhi first arrived at the province, Daoqing was at home; he petitioned on behalf of more than ten relatives, seeking posts as provincial attendants or western assistants. Youzhi employed three of them.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Daoqing of the palace direct retinue had his family in Jiangling. When Shen Youzhi first arrived in the province, Daoqing was at home and petitioned on behalf of more than ten relatives for posts as provincial attendants or western assistants. Shen Youzhi took on three of them.

sentences.zh: 道慶大怒，自入州取教，毀之而去。

translations.literal: Daoqing was furious; he entered the province office himself, took the appointment document, tore it up, and left.
translations.idiomatic: Daoqing was furious. He entered the provincial office himself, seized the appointment order, tore it up, and walked out.

sentences.zh: 及還都，不詣攸之別。

translations.literal: When he returned to the capital, he did not call on Youzhi to bid farewell.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to the capital, he did not call on Shen Youzhi to take his leave.

sentences.zh: 道慶至都，云：「攸之聚眾繕甲，姦逆不久。」

translations.literal: Arriving at the capital, Daoqing said: "Youzhi is gathering troops and repairing armor; treason will come soon."
translations.idiomatic: Arriving at the capital, Daoqing said: "Shen Youzhi is gathering troops and repairing armor; treason will come soon."

sentences.zh: 楊運長等常相疑畏，乃與道慶密遣刺客，齎廢帝手詔，以金餅賜攸之州府佐吏，進其階級。

translations.literal: Yang Yunchang and others constantly feared and suspected each other; they then secretly sent assassins with Daoqing, bearing the Deposed Emperor's handwritten edict, presenting gold cakes to Youzhi's provincial and headquarters staff, and promoting their ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yunchang and his circle lived in mutual fear and suspicion. Together with Daoqing they secretly sent assassins bearing the Deposed Emperor's handwritten edict, rewarding Shen Youzhi's provincial and headquarters staff with gold cakes and promoting their ranks.

sentences.zh: 時有象三頭至江陵城北數里，攸之自出格殺之，忽有流矢集攸之馬障泥，其後刺客事發。

translations.literal: At the time three elephants came within several li north of Jiangling city. Youzhi went out himself and killed them. Suddenly a stray arrow struck the mudguard of Youzhi's horse; afterward the assassination plot was exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Three elephants appeared several li north of Jiangling. Shen Youzhi went out himself and killed them. Suddenly a stray arrow struck the mudguard of his horse; afterward the assassination plot came to light.

sentences.zh: 廢帝既殞，順帝即位，進攸之號車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，加班劍二十人。

translations.literal: After the Deposed Emperor died, Emperor Shun ascended the throne and promoted Youzhi to General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master with Establishment Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies, with twenty added swords of office.
translations.idiomatic: After the Deposed Emperor died and Emperor Shun took the throne, Shen Youzhi was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master with Establishment Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies, with twenty added swords of office.

sentences.zh: 遣攸之長子司徒左長史元琰齎廢帝刳斮之具以示攸之。

translations.literal: They sent Youzhi's eldest son Yuan Yan, Left Chief Administrator of the Minister of Education, bearing the instruments with which the Deposed Emperor had been dismembered to show Youzhi.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Shen Youzhi's eldest son Yuan Yan, left chief administrator of the Minister of Education, bearing the instruments with which the Deposed Emperor had been dismembered to show his father.

sentences.zh: 元琰既至江陵，攸之便有異志，腹心議有不同，故其事不果。

translations.literal: When Yuan Yan reached Jiangling, Youzhi already harbored rebellious intent; his closest advisers disagreed among themselves, so the scheme did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Yan reached Jiangling, Shen Youzhi already harbored rebellious intent. His closest advisers were divided, and the plot came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月，乃發兵反叛。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year he finally raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of that year he finally raised troops in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 攸之素蓄士馬，資用豐積，至是戰士十萬，鐵馬二千。

translations.literal: Youzhi had long stocked soldiers and horses and amassed rich supplies; by then he had a hundred thousand fighting men and two thousand armored cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi had long stocked troops and horses and amassed rich supplies. By then he had a hundred thousand fighting men and two thousand armored cavalry.

sentences.zh: 遣使要雝州刺史張敬兒、梁州刺史范伯年、司州刺史姚道和、湘州行事庾佩玉、巴陵內史王文和等。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to summon Zhang Jinger, Inspector of Yong; Fan Bonian, Inspector of Liang; Yao Daodao, Inspector of Si; Yu Peiyu, acting Inspector of Xiang; Wang Wenhe, Administrator of Baling; and others.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to summon Zhang Jinger, Inspector of Yong; Fan Bonian, Inspector of Liang; Yao Daodao, Inspector of Si; Yu Peiyu, acting Inspector of Xiang; Wang Wenhe, Administrator of Baling; and others.

sentences.zh: 敬兒、文和斬其使，馳表以聞；

translations.literal: Jinger and Wenhe beheaded his envoys and sent urgent reports to inform the throne;
translations.idiomatic: Jinger and Wenhe beheaded his envoys and sent urgent reports to the throne;

sentences.zh: 伯年、道和、佩玉懷兩端，密相應和。

translations.literal: Bonian, Daodao, and Peiyu hedged on both sides and secretly responded in agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Bonian, Daodao, and Peiyu hedged on both sides and secretly answered in agreement.

sentences.zh: 十二月十二日，攸之遣其輔國將軍、中兵參軍、督前鋒軍事孫同，率寧朔將軍中兵參軍武寶、龍驤將軍騎兵參軍朱君拔、寧朔將軍沈慧真、龍驤將軍中兵參軍王道起；

translations.literal: On the twelfth day of the twelfth month, Youzhi dispatched his General Who Assists the State, Central Army Staff Officer, and Supervisor of Vanguard Military Affairs Sun Tong, leading Central Army Staff Officer Wu Bao, General Who Pacifies the North; Cavalry Staff Officer Zhu Junba, General of Dragon Cavalry; General Who Pacifies the North Shen Huizhen; and Central Army Staff Officer Wang Daoqi, General of Dragon Cavalry;
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth day of the twelfth month Shen Youzhi dispatched Sun Tong, General Who Assists the State, central army staff officer, and supervisor of vanguard operations, leading Wu Bao, central army staff officer and General Who Pacifies the North; Zhu Junba, cavalry staff officer and General of Dragon Cavalry; Shen Huizhen, General Who Pacifies the North; and Wang Daoqi, central army staff officer and General of Dragon Cavalry;

sentences.zh: 又遣司馬、冠軍將軍劉攘兵，率寧朔將軍外兵參軍公孫方平、龍驤將軍騎兵參軍朱靈寶、龍驤將軍騎兵參軍沈僧敬、龍驤將軍高茂；

translations.literal: He also dispatched Chief of Staff and General of Champions Liu Rangbing, leading External Army Staff Officer Gongsun Fangping, General Who Pacifies the North; Cavalry Staff Officer Zhu Lingbao, General of Dragon Cavalry; Cavalry Staff Officer Shen Sengjing, General of Dragon Cavalry; and Gao Mao, General of Dragon Cavalry;
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Chief of Staff and General of Champions Liu Rangbing, leading Gongsun Fangping, external army staff officer and General Who Pacifies the North; Zhu Lingbao, cavalry staff officer and General of Dragon Cavalry; Shen Sengjing, cavalry staff officer and General of Dragon Cavalry; and Gao Mao, General of Dragon Cavalry;

sentences.zh: 又遣輔國將軍中兵參軍王靈秀、輔國將軍中兵參軍丁珍東，率寧朔將軍中兵參軍王珍之、寧朔將軍外兵參軍楊景穆，相繼俱下。

translations.literal: He also dispatched Central Army Staff Officer Wang Lingxiu, General Who Assists the State, and Central Army Staff Officer Ding Zhendong, General Who Assists the State, leading Central Army Staff Officer Wang Zhenzhi, General Who Pacifies the North, and External Army Staff Officer Yang Jingmu, General Who Pacifies the North, all descending in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Wang Lingxiu and Ding Zhendong, central army staff officers and Generals Who Assist the State, leading Wang Zhenzhi, central army staff officer and General Who Pacifies the North, and Yang Jingmu, external army staff officer and General Who Pacifies the North, all marching down in succession.

sentences.zh: 攸之自率輔國將軍錄事參軍兼司馬武茂宗、輔國將軍中兵參軍沈韶、寧朔將軍中兵參軍皇甫賢、寧朔將軍中兵參軍胡欽之、龍驤將軍中兵參軍東門道順，閏十二月四日至夏口。

translations.literal: Youzhi himself led Recording Staff Officer and Concurrent Chief of Staff Wu Maozong, General Who Assists the State; Central Army Staff Officer Shen Shao, General Who Assists the State; Central Army Staff Officer Huangfu Xian, General Who Pacifies the North; Central Army Staff Officer Hu Qinzhi, General Who Pacifies the North; and Central Army Staff Officer Dongmen Daoshun, General of Dragon Cavalry, reaching Xiakou on the fourth day of the intercalary twelfth month.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi himself led Wu Maozong, recording staff officer, concurrent chief of staff, and General Who Assists the State; Shen Shao and Huangfu Xian, central army staff officers and Generals Who Assist the State; Hu Qinzhi, central army staff officer and General Who Pacifies the North; and Dongmen Daoshun, central army staff officer and General of Dragon Cavalry. They reached Xiakou on the fourth day of the intercalary twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 攸之將發江陵，使沙門釋僧桀筮之，曰：「不至京邑，當自郢州回還。」

translations.literal: When Youzhi was about to depart Jiangling, he had the monk Shi Jiejie perform divination. It said: "You will not reach the capital; you will turn back from Ying Province."
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving Jiangling, Shen Youzhi had the monk Shi Jiejie perform divination. The answer came: "You will not reach the capital; you will turn back from Ying Province."

sentences.zh: 意甚不悅。

translations.literal: He was very displeased at heart.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply displeased.

sentences.zh: 初，江津有雲氣，狀如塵霧，從西北來，正蓋軍上。

translations.literal: At first, at the river crossing there was cloud-vapor shaped like dust and mist, coming from the northwest and settling directly over the army.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, at the river crossing a cloud of vapor like dust and mist rolled in from the northwest and settled directly over the army.

sentences.zh: 至沌口，云：「當問訊安西，暫泊黃金浦。」

translations.literal: At Zhunkou he said: "We shall go to inquire after the Guarding-West army and moor briefly at Huangjin Ford."
translations.idiomatic: At Zhunkou he said: "We shall go to inquire after the Guarding-West army and moor briefly at Huangjin Ford."

sentences.zh: 既登岸，郢城出軍擊之。

translations.literal: Having gone ashore, Ying city sent out troops to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Once ashore, Ying city sent out troops to attack them.

sentences.zh: 攸之聞齊王世子據盆口，震懾不敢下，因攻郢城。

translations.literal: Youzhi heard the Prince of Qi's heir was holding Pankou and, shaken with fear, dared not descend; he therefore attacked Ying city.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi heard that the Prince of Qi's heir held Pankou and, shaken with fear, dared not press on. He therefore turned to attack Ying city.

sentences.zh: 時齊王輔政，遣眾軍西討。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Qi was regent and dispatched the armies west to punish the rebel.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Prince of Qi was regent and dispatched the armies west to punish the rebel.

sentences.zh: 尚書符征西府曰：

translations.literal: An order from the Secretariat to the Western Campaign headquarters said:
translations.idiomatic: An order from the Secretariat to the Western Campaign headquarters said:

sentences.zh: 尊冠賤屨，君臣之位，奉順忌逆，成敗斯兆，未有憑陵我郊圻，侵軼我河縣，而不焚師殪甲，靡旗亂轍者也。

translations.literal: The lofty cap and lowly shoes mark the station of lord and subject; obedience to what is proper and dread of what is forbidden are the augury of success and failure. Never yet has one who overran our outskirts and trampled our river counties failed to see his army burned, his armor destroyed, his banners scattered, and his chariot tracks in chaos.
translations.idiomatic: The lofty cap and lowly shoes mark the station of lord and subject; to obey what is right and dread rebellion is to read success and failure in advance. Never yet has anyone who overran our outskirts and trampled our river counties escaped with his army burned, his armor destroyed, his banners scattered, and his chariot tracks in chaos.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之少長庸賤，擢自閻伍，邀百戰之運，乘一捷之功，鐫山裂地，腰金扡紫，窮貴於國，極富於家。

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi from youth to age was lowborn and base, plucked from common ranks, riding the fortune of a hundred battles and the wind of one quick victory—carving mountains and splitting earth, girding gold and grasping purple, exalted to the highest nobility in the state and wealth beyond measure in his house.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi was lowborn from youth to age, plucked from common ranks. He rode the fortune of a hundred battles and the wind of one quick victory—carving mountains and splitting earth, girding gold and grasping purple—until he stood at the summit of state rank and wealth in his house.

sentences.zh: 擁旄蕃伯，便無北面之禮；

translations.literal: Wielding a commander's banner as a frontier lord, he no longer observed the rites of facing north;
translations.idiomatic: Wielding a commander's banner as a frontier lord, he no longer observed the rites of facing north toward the throne;

sentences.zh: 受督志屏，即有專征之釁。

translations.literal: Receiving supervision over a border province, he already bore the taint of independent command.
translations.idiomatic: Once entrusted with supervision over a border province, he already bore the taint of independent command.

sentences.zh: 橘柚不薦，璆{王替}罕入，箕賦深斂，毒被南郢，枉繩矯墨，害著西荊，饕餮其心，谿壑其性，從始至終，沿壯得老。

translations.literal: He offered no tribute of oranges and pomelos; precious jade seldom reached court; he taxed heavily with winnowing-basket levies and spread poison through southern Ying; he bent the plumb line and falsified the law, and harm showed plainly in western Jing. Gluttony filled his heart and ravines and gullies his nature—from beginning to end he grew old in the very fullness of his violence.
translations.idiomatic: He offered no tribute of oranges and pomelos; precious jade seldom reached court; he taxed heavily with winnowing-basket levies and spread poison through southern Ying; he bent the plumb line and falsified the law, and harm showed plainly in western Jing. Gluttony filled his heart and ravines and gullies his nature—from beginning to end he grew old in the very fullness of his violence.

sentences.zh: 今遂驅迫妖黨，繕集尪卒，結釁外城，送死中甸，是而可忍，孰不可懷！

translations.literal: Now he drives and presses demonic factions, gathers weakened soldiers, strikes provocation beyond the walls, and sends them to die in the central plains. If this can be borne, what can stir the heart!
translations.idiomatic: Now he drives demonic factions, gathers weakened soldiers, strikes provocation beyond the walls, and sends them to die in the central plains. If this can be borne, what outrage cannot stir the heart!

sentences.zh: 今遣新除使持節、督郢州之義陽諸軍事、平西將軍、郢州刺史、聞喜縣開國侯黃回、員外散騎常侍、冠軍、驍騎將軍、南臨淮太守、重安縣開國子、軍主王敬則、輔國將軍、屯騎校尉、長壽縣開國男王宜與、輔國將軍、南高平太守、軍主陳承叔、輔國將軍、左軍將軍、南濮陽太守、葛陽縣開國男、軍主彭文之、龍驤將軍、驃騎行參軍、軍主召宰，精甲二萬，前鋒雲騰。

translations.literal: Now we dispatch the newly appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Military Affairs for Yiyang and related regions of Ying Province, General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Ying, and Marquis of Wenxi county Huang Hui; Supernumerary Senior Adjunct in the Palace Secretariat, General of Champions and General of Valiant Cavalry, Prefect of Nanlinhuai, Viscount of Chong'an county, and Army Commander Wang Jingze; General Who Assists the State, Commandant of Escort Cavalry, Baron of Changshou county Wang Yiyu; General Who Assists the State, Prefect of Nan Gaoping, and Army Commander Chen Chengshu; General Who Assists the State, General of the Left Army, Prefect of Nan Puyang, Baron of Geyang county, and Army Commander Peng Wenzhi; General of Dragon Cavalry, Acting Staff Officer of the Rapid Cavalry General, and Army Commander Shao Zai—with twenty thousand elite armored troops, the vanguard rising like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: We now dispatch Huang Hui, newly appointed Bearer of the Staff, commander of military affairs for Yiyang and related regions of Ying Province, General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Ying, and Marquis of Wenxi county; Wang Jingze, supernumerary senior adjunct in the palace secretariat, General of Champions and General of Valiant Cavalry, Prefect of Nanlinhuai, Viscount of Chong'an county, and army commander; Wang Yiyu, General Who Assists the State, Commandant of Escort Cavalry, and Baron of Changshou county; Chen Chengshu, General Who Assists the State, Prefect of Nan Gaoping, and army commander; Peng Wenzhi, General Who Assists the State, General of the Left Army, Prefect of Nan Puyang, Baron of Geyang county, and army commander; and Shao Zai, General of Dragon Cavalry, acting staff officer of the Rapid Cavalry General, and army commander—with twenty thousand elite armored troops, the vanguard rising like clouds.

sentences.zh: 又遣散騎常侍、領游擊將軍、湘南縣開國男、新除使持節、督湘州諸軍事、征虜將軍、湘州刺史、軍主呂安國、屯騎校尉、寧朔將軍崔慧景、輔國將軍、軍主任候伯、輔國將軍、驍騎將軍、軍主蕭順之、輔國將軍、游擊將軍、軍主垣崇祖、寧朔將軍、虎賁中郎將、軍主尹略、屯騎校尉、南城令曹虎頭，舳艫二萬，駱驛繼邁。

translations.literal: We also dispatch Senior Adjunct in the Palace Secretariat, General of Mobile Attack, Baron of Xiangnan county, newly appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Military Affairs for Xiang Province, General Who Campaigns against Barbarians, Governor of Xiang, and Army Commander Lu Anguo; Commandant of Escort Cavalry and General Who Pacifies the North Cui Huijing; General Who Assists the State and Army Commander Ren Houbo; General Who Assists the State, General of Valiant Cavalry, and Army Commander Xiao Shunzhi; General Who Assists the State, General of Mobile Attack, and Army Commander Yuan Chongzu; General Who Pacifies the North, Central Commander of the Tiger Guard, and Army Commander Yin Lue; Commandant of Escort Cavalry and Magistrate of Nancheng Cao Hutou—with twenty thousand warships, advancing in relay without pause.
translations.idiomatic: We also dispatch Lu Anguo, senior adjunct in the palace secretariat, General of Mobile Attack, Baron of Xiangnan county, newly appointed Bearer of the Staff, commander of military affairs for Xiang Province, General Who Campaigns against Barbarians, Governor of Xiang, and army commander; Cui Huijing, Commandant of Escort Cavalry and General Who Pacifies the North; Ren Houbo, General Who Assists the State and army commander; Xiao Shunzhi, General Who Assists the State, General of Valiant Cavalry, and army commander; Yuan Chongzu, General Who Assists the State, General of Mobile Attack, and army commander; Yin Lue, General Who Pacifies the North, Central Commander of the Tiger Guard, and army commander; and Cao Hutou, Commandant of Escort Cavalry and Magistrate of Nancheng—with twenty thousand warships advancing in relay without pause.

sentences.zh: 又遣輔國將軍、後軍將軍、右軍中兵參軍事、軍主苟元賓、寧朔將軍、撫軍中兵參軍事、軍主郭文孝、龍驤將軍、撫軍中兵參軍事、軍主程隱雋，輕艓一萬，截其津要。

translations.literal: We also dispatch General Who Assists the State, General of the Rear Army, Right Army Central Army Staff Officer, and Army Commander Gou Yuanbin; General Who Pacifies the North, Pacification Army Central Army Staff Officer, and Army Commander Guo Wenxiao; General of Dragon Cavalry, Pacification Army Central Army Staff Officer, and Army Commander Cheng Yinjun—with ten thousand light boats to cut off the strategic crossings.
translations.idiomatic: We also dispatch Gou Yuanbin, General Who Assists the State, General of the Rear Army, right army central army staff officer, and army commander; Guo Wenxiao, General Who Pacifies the North, pacification army central army staff officer, and army commander; and Cheng Yinjun, General of Dragon Cavalry, pacification army central army staff officer, and army commander—with ten thousand light boats to cut off the strategic crossings.

sentences.zh: 新除持節督廣、交、越、寧、湘州之廣興諸軍事、領平越中郎將、征虜將軍、廣州刺史、統馬軍主、沌陽縣開國子周盤龍、輔國將軍、後軍統馬軍主張文憘、龍驤將軍、軍主薛道淵、冠軍將軍、游擊將軍、并州刺史、南清河太守、太原公、軍主王敕勤、龍驤將軍、射聲校尉王洪軌、龍驤將軍、冗從僕射、軍主成置等，鐵馬五千，龍驤後陳。

translations.literal: The newly appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Military Affairs for Guangxing and related regions of Guang, Jiao, Yue, Ning, and Xiang Provinces, Concurrent Central Commander of Pacifying the Yue, General Who Campaigns against Barbarians, Governor of Guang, Commander of Cavalry Forces, and Viscount of Zhunyang county Zhou Panlong; General Who Assists the State and Rear Army Commander of Cavalry Forces Zhang Wenxi; General of Dragon Cavalry and Army Commander Xue Daoyuan; General of Champions, General of Mobile Attack, Inspector of Bing, Prefect of Nan Qinghe, Duke of Taiyuan, and Army Commander Wang Chiqin; General of Dragon Cavalry and Commandant of Archers Wang Honggui; General of Dragon Cavalry, Supernumerary Master of Attendants, and Army Commander Cheng Zhi, and others—with five thousand armored cavalry as the dragon-cavalry rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: We also dispatch Zhou Panlong, newly appointed Bearer of the Staff, commander of military affairs for Guangxing and related regions of Guang, Jiao, Yue, Ning, and Xiang Provinces, concurrent Central Commander of Pacifying the Yue, General Who Campaigns against Barbarians, Governor of Guang, commander of cavalry forces, and Viscount of Zhunyang county; Zhang Wenxi, General Who Assists the State and rear army commander of cavalry forces; Xue Daoyuan, General of Dragon Cavalry and army commander; Wang Chiqin, General of Champions, General of Mobile Attack, Inspector of Bing, Prefect of Nan Qinghe, Duke of Taiyuan, and army commander; Wang Honggui, General of Dragon Cavalry and Commandant of Archers; and Cheng Zhi, General of Dragon Cavalry, supernumerary master of attendants, and army commander—with five thousand armored cavalry as the dragon-cavalry rear guard.

sentences.zh: 凡此諸帥，莫不勇力動天，勁志駕日，接衝拔距，鷹瞵鶚視，顧盼則前後風生，喑嗚則左右電起，以此攻城，何城不克，以此赴敵，何陳能堅。

translations.literal: None of these commanders fail to have courage that moves heaven and resolve that outrides the sun. Meeting the charge, they pull up the stakes; like hawks and eagles they stare. A glance to fore or aft and the wind rises; a battle cry to left or right and lightning flashes. With such men to storm a city, what city would not fall? With such men to meet the foe, what formation could hold?
translations.idiomatic: None of these commanders lacks courage that moves heaven or resolve that outrides the sun. They meet the charge and pull up the stakes; like hawks and eagles they stare. A glance fore or aft and the wind rises; a battle cry left or right and lightning flashes. With such men to storm a city, what city would not fall? With such men to meet the foe, what formation could hold?

sentences.zh: 然後鑾戎薄臨，龍虎百萬，六軍齊軌，五輅舒斾，丹檻發照，素甲生波，樓煩白羽，投鞍成岳，漁陽墨騎，浴鐵為群，芝艾同焚，悔將何及。

translations.literal: Then the imperial army draws near, dragon and tiger hosts number in the millions; the six armies march in unison and the five chariots unfurl their banners. Red rails blaze with light, white armor ripples like waves; Loufan's white-feathered arrows heap saddles like hills; Yuyang's black cavalry bathe iron into a horde. Wormwood and mugwort burn together—what remorse will there be time for?
translations.idiomatic: Then the imperial army draws near—dragon and tiger hosts in the millions; the six armies march in unison and the five chariots unfurl their banners. Red rails blaze with light, white armor ripples like waves; Loufan's white-feathered arrows heap saddles like hills; Yuyang's black cavalry bathe iron into a horde. Wormwood and mugwort burn together—what remorse will there be time for?

sentences.zh: 符到之日，幸加三省。

translations.literal: When this order arrives, may you reflect thrice upon it.
translations.idiomatic: When this order arrives, may you reflect thrice upon it.

sentences.zh: 其鋒陳營壁之主，驅逼寇手之人，若有投命軍門，一無所問。

translations.literal: Commanders of vanguard formations and camp walls, men driven by the rebel's hand—if any surrender at the army gate, not one question will be asked.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders of vanguard formations and camp walls, men driven by the rebel's hand—if any surrender at the army gate, no question will be asked.

sentences.zh: 或能因罪立績，終不爾欺，斬裾射玦，唯功是與。

translations.literal: Some may, by turning crime into merit, prove at last no deceit; to cut a sleeve or shoot a jade ring—merit alone shall be rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Some may turn crime into merit and prove at last no deceit; whether one cuts a sleeve or shoots a jade ring, merit alone shall be rewarded.

sentences.zh: 能斬送攸之首，封三千戶縣公，賜布、絹各五千匹。

translations.literal: Whoever can behead Youzhi and deliver his head shall be enfeoffed Marquis of a three-thousand-household county and granted five thousand bolts each of cloth and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever can behead Shen Youzhi and deliver his head shall be enfeoffed Marquis of a three-thousand-household county and granted five thousand bolts each of cloth and silk.

sentences.zh: 信如河海，皎然無貳。

translations.literal: The pledge is as sure as river and sea, bright and without duplicity.
translations.idiomatic: The pledge is as sure as river and sea, bright and without duplicity.

sentences.zh: 飛火軍攝文書，千里驛行。

translations.literal: Flying Fire Army conveys the document; a thousand li by post relay.
translations.idiomatic: The Flying Fire Army conveys the document; a thousand li by post relay.

sentences.zh: 齊王出頓新亭，馳檄數攸之罪惡，曰：

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi went out and encamped at Xinting, galloping proclamations enumerating Youzhi's crimes, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi went out and encamped at Xinting, sending proclamations at speed enumerating Shen Youzhi's crimes. He said:

sentences.zh: 夫彎弓射天，未見能至；

translations.literal: To bend a bow and shoot at heaven—no one has ever seen it reach;
translations.idiomatic: To bend a bow and shoot at heaven—no one has ever seen it reach;

sentences.zh: 揮戈擊地，多力安施。

translations.literal: To brandish a halberd and strike the earth—what use is mere strength?
translations.idiomatic: To brandish a halberd and strike the earth—what use is mere strength?

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 逆順之勢定殊，禍福之驗易原也。

translations.literal: Because the momentum of rebellion and obedience is utterly different, and the signs of disaster and fortune are easy to trace.
translations.idiomatic: Because the momentum of rebellion and obedience is utterly different, and the signs of disaster and fortune are easy to trace.

sentences.zh: 是以違乎天者，鬼神不能使其成；

translations.literal: Therefore one who goes against Heaven—neither ghosts nor spirits can make him succeed;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore one who goes against Heaven—neither ghosts nor spirits can make him succeed;

sentences.zh: 會乎人者，聖哲不能令其毀。

translations.literal: One who goes with the people—neither sages nor worthies can cause his ruin.
translations.idiomatic: One who goes with the people—neither sages nor worthies can cause his ruin.

sentences.zh: 故劉濞賴七國連兵之勢，隗囂恃跨河據隴之資，毋丘儉伐其逾海越島之功，諸葛誕矜其待士愛民之德，彼四子者，皆當世雄傑，以犯順取禍，覆窟傾巢，為豎子笑。

translations.literal: Liu Pi relied on the power of the Seven States massed in arms; Wei Xiao trusted his resource of holding the Yellow River and occupying Long; Guanqiu Jian boasted his merit of crossing the sea to islands; Zhuge Dan prided himself on treating scholars and loving the people. Those four were all heroes of their age—yet by rebellion they brought disaster, their nests overturned and their dens destroyed, made the laughingstock of children.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pi relied on the power of the Seven States massed in arms; Wei Xiao trusted his hold on the Yellow River and Long; Guanqiu Jian boasted of crossing the sea to distant islands; Zhuge Dan prided himself on treating scholars and loving the people. Those four were heroes of their age—yet by rebellion they brought disaster, their nests overturned and their dens destroyed, made the laughingstock of children.

sentences.zh: 況乎行陳凡才，斗筲小器，而懷問鼎之志，敢構無君之逆哉！

translations.literal: How much more for a common talent in the ranks, a dipper-and-measure small vessel, to cherish ambition to seize the tripod and dare to contrive rebellion without a lord!
translations.idiomatic: How much more for a common talent in the ranks, a dipper-and-measure small vessel, to cherish ambition to seize the tripod and dare to contrive rebellion without a lord!

sentences.zh: 逆賊沈攸之，出自萊畝，寂寥累世，故司空沈公以從父宗蔭，愛之若子，卵翼吹噓，得升官秩。

translations.literal: The rebel Shen Youzhi came from the fields; for generations his house was obscure. Former Minister of Works Shen Gong, through clan relation on the father's side, loved him as a son—sheltered and nurtured him with wings and breath until he rose in office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Shen Youzhi came from the fields; for generations his house was obscure. Former Minister of Works Shen Gong, through clan relation on the father's side, loved him as a son—sheltered and nurtured him until he rose in office and rank.

sentences.zh: 廢帝昏悖，猜畏柱臣，攸之貪競乘機，凶忍趨利，躬行反噬，請銜誅旨。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor was muddled and perverse, fearful and suspicious of his pillar ministers. Youzhi, greedy and contentious, seized the moment; cruel and ruthless, he rushed after profit—personally carrying out a counter-bite and requesting to bear the execution orders.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor was muddled and perverse, fearful and suspicious of his pillar ministers. Shen Youzhi, greedy and contentious, seized the moment; cruel and ruthless, he rushed after profit—personally carrying out a counter-bite and requesting to bear the execution orders.

sentences.zh: 又攸之與譚金、童太壹等並受寵任，朝為牙爪，同功共體，世號三侯，當時親昵，情過管、鮑。

translations.literal: Moreover Youzhi, together with Tan Jin and Tong Taiyi and others, all received favor and trust—court fangs and claws in the morning, sharing merit and sharing body. Their age called them the Three Marquises; the intimacy of the time exceeded even Guan Zhong and Bao Shuya.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Shen Youzhi, together with Tan Jin and Tong Taiyi and others, all received favor and trust—court fangs and claws in the morning, sharing merit and sharing body. Their age called them the Three Marquises; the intimacy of the time exceeded even Guan Zhong and Bao Shuya.

sentences.zh: 遭仰革運，凶黨懼戮，攸之狡猾用數，圖全賣禍，既殺從父，又害良朋。

translations.literal: When the upward turn of fate came, the wicked faction feared punishment. Youzhi, sly and scheming, sought to save himself by selling disaster—he killed his father's-cousin and also destroyed a good friend.
translations.idiomatic: When the upward turn of fate came, the wicked faction feared punishment. Shen Youzhi, sly and scheming, sought to save himself by selling disaster—he killed his father's-cousin and also destroyed a good friend.

sentences.zh: 雖呂布販君，酈寄賣友，方之斯人，未足為酷。

translations.literal: Though Lü Bu sold out his lord and Li Ji sold out his friend, compared with this man they hardly count as cruel.
translations.idiomatic: Though Lü Bu sold out his lord and Li Ji sold out his friend, compared with this man they hardly count as cruel.

sentences.zh: 此其不信不義，言詐翻覆，諸夏之所未有，夷狄之所不為也。

translations.literal: This faithlessness and unrighteousness, deceitful words and reversed pledges—what the civilized lands have never seen, what even the barbarians would not do.
translations.idiomatic: This faithlessness and unrighteousness, deceitful words and reversed pledges—what the civilized lands have never seen, what even the barbarians would not do.

sentences.zh: 泰始開闢，網漏吞舟，略其兇險，取其搏噬，故得階亂獲全，因禍保福。

translations.literal: At the Taishi founding the net leaked, swallowing even great fish; his viciousness and danger were overlooked, his devouring bite taken in—so he survived the age of chaos whole and turned disaster into blessing.
translations.idiomatic: At the Taishi founding the net leaked, swallowing even great fish; his viciousness and danger were overlooked, his devouring bite taken in—so he survived the age of chaos whole and turned disaster into blessing.

sentences.zh: 攸之空淺，躁而無謀，濃湖崩挫，本非己力；

translations.literal: Youzhi was shallow and empty, rash and without strategy; the collapse at Nong Lake was never his own strength;
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi was shallow and empty, rash and without strategy; the collapse at Nong Lake was never his own strength;

sentences.zh: 及北伐彭、泗，望賊宵奔；

translations.literal: When the northern campaign reached Peng and Si, he fled at the sight of the enemy by night;
translations.idiomatic: When the northern campaign reached Peng and Si, he fled at the sight of the enemy by night;

sentences.zh: 重討下邳，一鼓而遁；

translations.literal: The second siege of Xiapi—one drum and he fled;
translations.idiomatic: At the second siege of Xiapi, one drumbeat and he fled;

sentences.zh: 再鄙王師，又應肆法。

translations.literal: Twice he disgraced the royal army—he should again have been put to law.
translations.idiomatic: Twice he disgraced the royal army—he should again have been put to the law.

sentences.zh: 先帝英聖，量深河海，宥其回谿之敗，冀收曲崤之捷，故得推遷幸會，頓升崇顯，內端戎禁，外臨方牧。

translations.literal: The Former Emperor was sage and brilliant, his magnanimity deep as rivers and seas; he pardoned his defeat at the winding ravine and hoped to reap victory at the crooked pass—so Youzhi was promoted by accumulated fortune to sudden eminence, inwardly guarding the army, outwardly facing frontier command.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming was sage and brilliant, his magnanimity deep as rivers and seas; he pardoned Shen Youzhi's defeat at the winding ravine and hoped to reap victory at the crooked pass—so Shen Youzhi was promoted by accumulated fortune to sudden eminence, inwardly guarding the army, outwardly facing frontier command.

sentences.zh: 聖靈鼎湖，遠頒顧命，託寄崇深，義感金石。

translations.literal: When the Sacred Spirit ascended to Ding Lake, a final charge was issued from afar—the entrustment was profound, the righteousness moving as metal and stone.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sacred Spirit ascended to Ding Lake, a final charge was issued from afar—the entrustment was profound, the righteousness moving as metal and stone.

sentences.zh: 而攸之始奉國諱，喜見於容，普天同哀，己以為慶。

translations.literal: Yet when Youzhi first observed the state mourning, joy showed on his face; when all under heaven mourned alike, he took it for celebration.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Shen Youzhi first observed the state mourning, joy showed on his face; when all under heaven mourned alike, he took it for celebration.

sentences.zh: 此其樂禍幸災，大逆之罪一也。

translations.literal: This rejoicing in disaster and good fortune at others' misfortune—the first of his great-rebellion crimes.
translations.idiomatic: This rejoicing in disaster and good fortune at others' misfortune—the first of his great-rebellion crimes.

sentences.zh: 又攸之累登蕃兵，自郢遷荊，晉熙殿下以皇弟代鎮，地尊望重，攸之肆情陵侮，斷割候迎，料擇士馬，簡筭器甲，精器銳士，竝取自隨，郢城所留，十不遺一，專擅略虜，罔顧國典。

translations.literal: Also Youzhi repeatedly held frontier command, moving from Ying to Jing. Prince Jinxi as imperial younger brother replaced him in the garrison—high in station and heavy in prestige. Youzhi indulged his passions in insult, cut off reception escorts, counted out soldiers and horses, sorted weapons and armor, took the finest arms and sharpest troops all for himself; of what Ying city retained, not one in ten remained. He usurped and pillaged at will, heedless of state law.
translations.idiomatic: Also Shen Youzhi repeatedly held frontier command, moving from Ying to Jing. Prince Jinxi, the emperor's younger brother, replaced him in the garrison—high in station and heavy in prestige. Shen Youzhi indulged his passions in insult, cut off reception escorts, counted out soldiers and horses, sorted weapons and armor, and took the finest arms and sharpest troops all for himself; of what Ying city retained, not one in ten remained. He usurped and pillaged at will, heedless of state law.

sentences.zh: 此其苞藏禍志，不恭不虔，大逆之罪二也。

translations.literal: This harboring of evil intent, lacking respect and devotion—the second great-rebellion crime.
translations.idiomatic: This harboring of evil intent, lacking respect and devotion—the second great-rebellion crime.

sentences.zh: 又攸之踐荊以來，恆用姦數，既欲發兵，宜有因假，遂乃蹙迫群蠻，騷擾山谷，揚聲討伐，盡戶發上，蟻聚郭邑，伺國盛衰，從來積年，永不解甲。

translations.literal: Also since taking Jing, Youzhi constantly used deceit; when he wished to raise troops he needed a pretext. He then pressurized the tribal groups, harassed the valleys, raised the cry of punitive campaign, and conscripted every household; they swarmed like ants at city walls, watching whether the state flourished or declined. Year after year they never put off armor.
translations.idiomatic: Also since taking Jing, Shen Youzhi constantly used deceit; when he wished to raise troops he needed a pretext. He pressurized the tribal groups, harassed the valleys, raised the cry of punitive campaign, and conscripted every household; they swarmed like ants at city walls, watching whether the state flourished or declined. Year after year they never put off armor.

sentences.zh: 遂使四野百縣，路無男人；

translations.literal: Thus in the four wilds and hundred counties there were no men on the roads;
translations.idiomatic: Thus in the four wilds and hundred counties there were no men on the roads;

sentences.zh: 耕田載租，皆驅女弱。

translations.literal: Plowing fields and carrying rent—all were driven by women and the weak.
translations.idiomatic: Plowing fields and carrying rent—all were driven by women and the weak.

sentences.zh: 自古酷虐，未聞有此。

translations.literal: Since antiquity, in cruel oppression nothing like this has been heard.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, in cruel oppression nothing like this has been heard.

sentences.zh: 其侮蔑朝廷，大逆之罪三也。

translations.literal: This contempt for the court—the third great-rebellion crime.
translations.idiomatic: This contempt for the court—the third great-rebellion crime.

sentences.zh: 去昔桂陽奇兵□起，京師內{畾大}，宗廟阽危。

translations.literal: In years past the surprise army of Guiyang suddenly rose; the capital was thrown into internal turmoil; the ancestral temples stood on the brink of peril.
translations.idiomatic: In years past the surprise army of Guiyang suddenly rose; the capital was thrown into internal turmoil; the ancestral temples stood on the brink of peril.

sentences.zh: 攸之任居上流，兵強地廣，救援顛沛，實宜悉力。

translations.literal: Youzhi held the upper reach with strong troops and broad territory; when the throne tottered in distress, he should truly have exerted all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi held the upper reach with strong troops and broad territory; when the throne tottered in distress, he should truly have exerted all his strength.

sentences.zh: 國家倒懸，方思身慮，威遣弱卒三千，竝皆羸老，使就郢州，稟受節度，欲令判否之日，委罪晉熙。

translations.literal: The state hung inverted; while others pondered their own bodies, he dispatched only three thousand weak troops, all old and enfeebled, ordering them to Ying Province to receive command—intending on the day of judgment to cast blame on Prince Jinxi.
translations.idiomatic: The state hung inverted; while others pondered their own bodies, he dispatched only three thousand weak troops, all old and enfeebled, ordering them to Ying Province to receive command—intending on the day of judgment to cast blame on Prince Jinxi.

sentences.zh: 何其平日輈張，實輕周、邵，爾時恭謹，虛重皇戚。

translations.literal: How in daily life he was arrogant and overbearing, truly belittling the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao; how in that hour he was merely feigning reverence, hollowly honoring the imperial kin.
translations.idiomatic: How in daily life he was arrogant and overbearing, truly belittling the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao; how in that hour he was merely feigning reverence, hollowly honoring the imperial kin.

sentences.zh: 此其伏慝藏詐，持疑兩端，大逆之罪四也。

translations.literal: This hiding of malice and hoarding of deceit, holding doubt on both sides—the fourth great-rebellion crime.
translations.idiomatic: This hiding of malice and hoarding of deceit, holding doubt on both sides—the fourth great-rebellion crime.

sentences.zh: 又攸之累據方州，跋扈滋甚，招誘輕狡，往者咸納；

translations.literal: Also Youzhi repeatedly held provincial command; his arrogance grew ever worse. He recruited the frivolous and cunning; whoever came, all were taken in;
translations.idiomatic: Also Shen Youzhi repeatedly held provincial command; his arrogance grew ever worse. He recruited the frivolous and cunning; whoever came, all were taken in;

sentences.zh: 羈絆行侶，過境必留。

translations.literal: Travelers passing through were detained and never allowed to go on.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers passing through were detained and never allowed to go on.

sentences.zh: 仕子窮困，不得歸其鄉；

translations.literal: Scholars in poverty could not return to their home districts;
translations.idiomatic: Scholars in poverty could not return to their home districts;

sentences.zh: 商人畢命，無由還其土。

translations.literal: Merchants gave up their lives, with no way to return to their native soil.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants gave up their lives, with no way to return to their native soil.

sentences.zh: 叛亡入境，輒加擁護；

translations.literal: Deserters entering his borders were at once sheltered;
translations.idiomatic: Deserters entering his borders were at once sheltered;

sentences.zh: 逋逃出界，必遣窮追。

translations.literal: Fugitives leaving his borders were surely pursued to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Fugitives leaving his borders were surely pursued to the end.

sentences.zh: 此其大逆之罪五也。

translations.literal: This is the fifth great-rebellion crime.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fifth great-rebellion crime.

sentences.zh: 又攸之自任專恣，恃行慘酷，視吏若仇，遇民如草。

translations.literal: Also Youzhi entrusted himself with arbitrary power, relying on cruel conduct; he looked on officials as enemies and treated the people like grass.
translations.idiomatic: Also Shen Youzhi entrusted himself with arbitrary power, relying on cruel conduct; he looked on officials as enemies and treated the people like grass.

sentences.zh: 峻太半之賦，暴參夷之刑。

translations.literal: He imposed taxes taking more than half; he inflicted punishment by execution of whole clans.
translations.idiomatic: He imposed taxes taking more than half; he inflicted punishment by execution of whole clans.

sentences.zh: 鞭捶國士，全用虜法；

translations.literal: Flogging state officers—all by barbarian law;
translations.idiomatic: Flogging state officers—all by barbarian law;

sentences.zh: 一人逃亡，闔宗補代。

translations.literal: When one man fled, the whole clan was seized to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When one man fled, the whole clan was seized to replace him.

sentences.zh: 毒遍嬰孩，虐加斑白。

translations.literal: Poison spread even to infants; cruelty extended even to the gray-haired.
translations.idiomatic: Poison spread even to infants; cruelty extended even to the gray-haired.

sentences.zh: 獄囚恆滿，市血常流。

translations.literal: Prisons were always full; the marketplace ran with blood.
translations.idiomatic: Prisons were always full; the marketplace ran with blood.

sentences.zh: 男不得耕，女不得織。

translations.literal: Men could not plow; women could not weave.
translations.idiomatic: Men could not plow; women could not weave.

sentences.zh: 奔馳道路，號哭動天。

translations.literal: They raced along the roads, wailing that shook heaven.
translations.idiomatic: They raced along the roads, wailing that shook heaven.

sentences.zh: 皇朝赦令，初不遵奉，欲殺欲擊，故曠蕩之澤，長隔彼州。

translations.literal: The dynastic amnesties he at first never obeyed; whether to kill or strike lay entirely in his hands—so the broad forgiving mercy of the throne forever stayed beyond that province.
translations.idiomatic: The dynastic amnesties he at first never obeyed; whether to kill or strike lay entirely in his hands—so the broad forgiving mercy of the throne forever stayed beyond that province.

sentences.zh: 此其無君陵上，大逆之罪六也。

translations.literal: This is his lacking a lord and bullying superiors—the sixth great-rebellion crime.
translations.idiomatic: This is his crime of disloyalty to his sovereign and contempt for superiors—the sixth capital offense of treason.

sentences.zh: 蒼梧狂凶，釁深桀、紂，猜貳外蕃，鴞目西顧。

translations.literal: Cangwu was wildly vicious, malice deeper than Jie and Zhou; doubly suspicious of outer provinces, owl-eyes cast westward.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Cangwu was wildly brutal, his wickedness surpassing even Jie and Zhou; he was doubly suspicious of the frontier provinces and cast predatory eyes toward the west.

sentences.zh: 留其長息元琰，以為交質；

translations.literal: He kept his eldest son Yuan Yan as a diplomatic hostage;
translations.idiomatic: He kept his eldest son Yuan Yan as a hostage to guarantee their dealings;

sentences.zh: 父子分張，彌積年稔。

translations.literal: Father and son were separated, years piling up ripe.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son were torn apart, and the years of separation only deepened.

sentences.zh: 賴社稷靈長，獨夫遄戮，攸之豫稟心靈，宜同歡幸。

translations.literal: Thanks to the altars' enduring fortune, the lone tyrant was swiftly executed; Youzhi had long received this in his heart and ought to have shared the joy.
translations.idiomatic: By the enduring fortune of the state, the tyrant was swiftly put to death; Youzhi had long known this in his heart and ought to have rejoiced with all others.

sentences.zh: 遂迷惑顛倒，深相嗟惜。

translations.literal: Yet he became confused and perverse, deeply lamenting and pitying.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he turned confused and perverse, deeply mourning and pitying the fallen tyrant.

sentences.zh: 舉言哀桀，揚聲吠堯。

translations.literal: He raised his voice to mourn Jie and barked out against Yao.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke in grief for the tyrant and barked invective against the sage ruler.

sentences.zh: 此其不辨是非，罔識善惡，違情背理，大逆之罪七也。

translations.literal: This is his failure to distinguish right from wrong, blindness to good and evil, violation of feeling and betrayal of reason—the seventh great-rebellion crime.
translations.idiomatic: This is his failure to tell right from wrong, his blindness to good and evil, his defiance of human feeling and betrayal of reason—the seventh capital offense of treason.

sentences.zh: 廢昏立明，先代盛典，交、廣先到，梁、秦蚤及，而攸之密邇內畿，川塗弗遠，驛書至止，晏若不聞，未遣章表，奄積旬朔。

translations.literal: Deposing the dark and raising the bright was a classic rite of former ages; Jiao and Guang came first, Liang and Qin soon followed; yet Youzhi was close to the inner capital, rivers and roads not far—when dispatch orders arrived he was untroubled as if unheard, sent no memorial, and let full weeks and months pass.
translations.idiomatic: Deposing the unworthy and enthroning the worthy was a classic rite of former dynasties; Jiao and Guang submitted first, Liang and Qin soon followed. Yet Youzhi lay close to the inner capital, with rivers and roads not far away—when imperial dispatches arrived he was serene as if he had not heard, sent no memorial of allegiance, and let weeks and months slip by.

sentences.zh: 防風後至，夏典所誅，此其大逆之罪八也。

translations.literal: Fangfeng arrived late and was punished per the Xia code—this is his eighth great-rebellion crime.
translations.idiomatic: Fangfeng arrived late and was punished under the code of Xia—this is his eighth capital offense of treason.

sentences.zh: 昇明肇曆，恩深澤遠，申其父子之情，矜其骨肉之恩，馳遣元琰，銜使西歸，竝加崇授，寵貴重疊。

translations.literal: When the Shengming reign began, grace ran deep and favor far; the bond between father and son was affirmed, family ties cherished; Yuan Yan was hastily sent back west with envoys bearing orders; both received elevated appointments, honors stacked upon honors.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shengming reign began, imperial grace ran deep and favor reached far; the bond between father and son was honored and family ties cherished. Yuan Yan was hastily sent home to the west with envoys bearing orders, and both father and son received elevated appointments, honors heaped upon honors.

sentences.zh: 元琰達西，便應反命，攸之得此集聚，蒙誰之恩？

translations.literal: When Yuan Yan reached the west he should at once have reported back; Youzhi with this gathering—whose grace did he receive?
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Yan reached the west he should at once have reported back his mission—yet with this army Youzhi assembled, whose grace was he repaying?

sentences.zh: 不荷盛德，反生仇釁，此其大逆之罪九也。

translations.literal: He did not bear the great virtue but instead stirred enmity and strife—this is his ninth great-rebellion crime.
translations.idiomatic: He did not accept this great kindness but instead stirred up enmity and rebellion—this is his ninth capital offense of treason.

sentences.zh: 攸之以谿壑之性，含梟鴆之腸，直置天壤，已稱醜穢。

translations.literal: Youzhi, with the nature of a ravine or gully, harboring owl-and-poisonous-bird entrails—even set bare upon heaven and earth he would already be called foul and filthy.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi, with the greed of a bottomless gorge and the heart of a bird of prey—even standing alone under heaven and earth he would already be called foul and vile.

sentences.zh: 況乃舉兵內侮，逞肆奸回，斯實惡熟罪成之辰，決癰潰疽之日。

translations.literal: How much more now that he raises troops to insult the realm within and gives free rein to treachery—this is truly the hour when evil ripens and guilt is complete, the day when the abscess bursts.
