translations.idiomatic: How much more now that he raises troops to strike at the heart of the realm and gives free rein to treachery—this is truly the hour when evil has ripened and guilt is complete, the day when the abscess must be lanced.

sentences.zh: 幕府過荷朝寄，義百常憤，董司元戎，龔行天罰。

translations.literal: The headquarters has overmuch borne the court's trust, justice daily inflamed; it oversees the chief army and marches to execute heaven's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The command has long borne the court's heavy trust, and righteous anger burns daily within it; it now directs the main army and marches to carry out heaven's punishment.

sentences.zh: 今皇上聖明，將相仁厚，約法三章，輕刑緩賦，年登歲阜，家給人足，上有惠和之澤，下無樂亂之心。

translations.literal: Now the emperor is sage and bright, generals and ministers humane and generous; law is simplified to three articles, punishments light and taxes eased; harvests succeed and years prosper, every household provided for and every person satisfied; grace and harmony flow from above, and below there is no heart that delights in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor is sage and enlightened, his generals and ministers humane and generous; the law has been simplified, punishments lightened and taxes eased; harvests are abundant and years prosperous, every household provided for and every person content; grace and harmony flow from above, and below there is no heart that delights in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 攸之不識天時，妄圖奸逆，舉無名之師，驅怨仇之黨。

translations.literal: Youzhi does not recognize heaven's seasons, vainly plots treachery, raises an army without just cause, and drives a band of resentful enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi does not read the signs of heaven, vainly plots treason, raises an army without just cause, and drives a host of embittered malcontents.

sentences.zh: 是以朝野審其易取，含識判其成禽。

translations.literal: Therefore court and country see him as easy to take; those with understanding judge that he will be captured.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore court and country alike see him as easy prey; all who understand the times judge that he is already as good as captured.

sentences.zh: 熊羆厲爪，蓄攫裂之心；

translations.literal: Bears and grizzlies sharpen claws, storing hearts of tearing and rending;
translations.idiomatic: Bears and grizzlies sharpen their claws, hearts full of tearing fury;

sentences.zh: 虎豹摩牙，起吞噬之憤。

translations.literal: Tigers and leopards whetting fangs, rousing fury of devouring.
translations.idiomatic: tigers and leopards grind their teeth, roused to devouring rage.

sentences.zh: 鼓怒則冰原激電，奮發則霜野奔靁，以此定亂，豈移晷刻。

translations.literal: When anger is roused, ice plains flash with lightning; when they strike, frosted fields thunder—by this rebellion is quelled; will it take more than a turning of the sundial?
translations.idiomatic: When wrath is roused, ice fields crack with lightning; when they strike, frostbound plains thunder—by such force rebellion will be quelled, and not a sundial's turn need pass.

sentences.zh: 雖復眾徒梗陸，舉郡阻川，何足以抗沸海之濤，當燒山之焰。

translations.literal: Even if multitudes block the land and whole commanderies block the rivers, how could they resist the boiling sea's surge or stand against the flame that burns mountains?
translations.idiomatic: Even if his followers choke the roads and whole commanderies bar the rivers, how could they withstand the surge of a boiling sea or the blaze of mountains set afire?

sentences.zh: 彼土士民，罹毒日久，逃竄無路，常所憫然。

translations.literal: The gentry and people of that land have long suffered poison, fleeing with no road—we have always pitied them.
translations.idiomatic: The gentry and common people of that region have long suffered under his cruelty, fleeing with nowhere to go—a plight we have always pitied.

sentences.zh: 今復相逼，起接鋒刃，交戰之日，蘭艾難分。

translations.literal: Now again they are pressed together, thrust against the blade's edge; on the day of battle, orchid and mugwort are hard to separate.
translations.idiomatic: Now they are pressed again into the path of swords; on the day battle is joined, the innocent and the guilty will be hard to tell apart.

sentences.zh: 土崩倒戈，宜為蚤計，無使一人迷昧，而九族就禍也。

translations.literal: When earth collapses and swords turn inward, you should plan early; do not let one man's delusion bring ruin upon nine clans.
translations.idiomatic: When the earth splits and swords turn inward, you should act early; do not let one man's folly bring destruction upon nine generations of kin.

sentences.zh: 弘宥之典，有如皎日。

translations.literal: The great amnesty is bright as the noonday sun.
translations.idiomatic: The promise of broad pardon shines bright as the noonday sun.

sentences.zh: 攸之盡銳攻郢州，行事柳世隆隨宜距應，屢摧破之。

translations.literal: Youzhi threw his full strength against Ying Province; the acting governor Liu Shilong adapted his defense and repeatedly broke him.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi threw his full strength against Ying Province; the acting governor Liu Shilong adapted his defense as needed and repeatedly routed him.

sentences.zh: 攸之與武陵王贊箋曰：「江陵一緫八州，地居形勝，鎮撫之重，宜以上歸。

translations.literal: Youzhi wrote a letter to Prince Liu Zan of Wuling saying: "Jiangling commands eight provinces in one, occupies commanding terrain—the weight of garrison and pacification ought to be returned above.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi wrote to Prince Liu Zan of Wuling, saying: "Jiangling commands eight provinces at once and occupies commanding terrain—the weight of garrison and pacification ought properly to rest with the throne above.

sentences.zh: 本欲仰移節蓋，改臨荊部，所以未具上聞者，欲待至止，面自咨申。

translations.literal: I originally intended to transfer my authority and turn to oversee Jing; the reason I have not yet fully reported upward is that I wished to wait until arrival and consult in person.
translations.idiomatic: I originally meant to transfer my seal of authority and turn to oversee Jing; the reason I have not yet made a full report to the throne is that I wished to wait until I arrived and could speak face to face.

sentences.zh: 不圖重關擊柝，覲接莫由。

translations.literal: I did not expect heavy passes to beat the watch—audience has no path.
translations.idiomatic: I did not expect the passes to be barred and watch drums sounded—I have no way to gain audience.

sentences.zh: 若使匡朝之誠，終蔽於聖察，襲遠之舉，近擁於郢都，則無以謝烈士之心，何用塞義夫之志，便不犯關陵漢，期一接奉。

translations.literal: If loyalty to right the dynasty should end hidden from imperial scrutiny, if the distant strike is held close at Ying—there is no way to answer loyal martyrs' hearts, how to satisfy righteous men's resolve—I shall not violate passes or climb the Han's banks, expecting one audience.
translations.idiomatic: If loyalty to restore the dynasty should remain hidden from imperial sight, if a march meant to strike far is stalled before Ying—there is no way to answer the hearts of loyal dead, no way to satisfy men of honor—I shall not force the passes or cross the Han, but expect only one audience.

sentences.zh: 若夫斬蛟陷石之卒，裂骼卷鐵之將，煙騰飆迅，容或驚動左右，苟不獲已，敢不先布下情。」

translations.literal: As for troops that cut dragons and crush stone, generals of torn flesh and coiled iron—as smoke rises and storms rush, they may perhaps startle those nearby; if it cannot be avoided, I dare not fail first to announce my intent below."
translations.idiomatic: As for soldiers who cut dragons and shatter stone, generals hardened as iron—as smoke rises and storms rush, they may perhaps alarm those nearby; if it cannot be helped, I dare not fail first to declare my intent."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「下官位重分陝，富兼金穴，子弟勝衣，爵命已及，親黨辨菽，抽序便加，耳倦弦歌，口厭粱肉，布衣若此，復欲何求？

translations.literal: He also said: "Your servant's rank weighs like the divided Zhou domains, wealth rivals golden vaults; sons and brothers overflow—titles and orders already granted; kin and allies distinguish grain at a glance—promotion follows on the draw; ears weary of strings and song, mouth sated with fine grain and meat—a commoner like this, what more could he seek?
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Your servant's rank is as weighty as the Zhou domains divided between Duke Zhou and the Duke of Shao, his wealth rivals the vaults of gold; sons and brothers crowd his halls, titles and honors already granted; kin and allies receive promotion at a word; his ears are weary of music, his mouth sated with fine grain and meat—a man already so favored, what more could he desire?

sentences.zh: 豈不知俛眉苟安，保養餘齒，何為不計百口，甘冒危難。

translations.literal: Do I not know to bow the brow and live at ease, preserve my remaining years—why not count my hundred mouths and gladly risk danger?
translations.idiomatic: Do I not know how to bow my head, live at ease, and preserve my remaining years? Why then would I ignore the lives of a hundred kin and willingly court disaster?

sentences.zh: 誠感歷朝之遇，欲報之於皇家爾。

translations.literal: Truly moved by kindness across reigns, I wish only to repay the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by kindness shown across successive reigns, I wish only to repay the imperial house.

sentences.zh: 昧理之徒，謂下官懷無厭之願，既貫誠於白日，不復明心於殿下。

translations.literal: Those blind to reason say your servant harbors insatiable desire—but having pledged loyalty in broad daylight, I need no longer bare my heart to Your Highness.
translations.idiomatic: Men blind to reason say your servant harbors boundless ambition—but having pledged my loyalty in the open light of day, I need no longer lay bare my heart before Your Highness.

sentences.zh: 若使天必喪道，忠節不立，政復闔門碎滅，百死無恨。

translations.literal: If heaven must abandon the Way and loyalty cannot stand, then even whole-house destruction and a hundred deaths bring no regret.
translations.idiomatic: If heaven has truly abandoned the Way and loyalty can no longer stand, then even the destruction of my whole house and a hundred deaths would bring no regret.

sentences.zh: 但高祖王業艱難，太祖劬勞日昃，卜世不盡七百之期，宗社已成他人之有。

translations.literal: Yet the Founding Emperor's royal work was hard-won, the Grand Ancestor toiled until the sun slanted west—the augured age did not reach the full seven hundred years; altar and state have already become another's possession.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Founding Emperor's royal enterprise was won through hardship, and the Grand Ancestor toiled until the sun stood in the west—the dynasty's allotted span did not reach the full seven hundred years, and altar and state have already passed into another's hands.

sentences.zh: 家國之事，未審於聖心何如？」

translations.literal: The affairs of house and state—I do not know what Your Majesty's heart holds of them?"
translations.idiomatic: As for the affairs of house and state—I do not know what Your Majesty's sacred heart thinks of them?"

sentences.zh: 攸之遣中兵參軍公孫方平馬步三千向武昌，太守臧渙棄郡投西陽太守王毓，奔於盆口，方平因據西陽。

translations.literal: Youzhi sent Central Army Attendant Gongsun Fangping with three thousand horse and foot toward Wuchang; the prefect Zang Huan abandoned his commandery and went to Wang Yu, prefect of Xiyang, fleeing to Pankou; Fangping then seized Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi sent Central Army Attendant Gongsun Fangping with three thousand horse and foot toward Wuchang. Prefect Zang Huan abandoned his commandery, joined Xiyang Prefect Wang Yu, and fled to Pankou; Fangping then occupied Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 建寧太守張謨率二守千人攻之，方平破走。

translations.literal: Jianning Prefect Zhang Mo led two guard units with a thousand men to attack; Fangping was routed and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Jianning Prefect Zhang Mo led two guard units, a thousand men in all, to attack him; Fangping was defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 攸之攻郢城久不決，眾心離沮。

translations.literal: Youzhi's assault on Ying city dragged on unresolved; hearts in the host turned estranged and downcast.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi's assault on Ying city dragged on without decision, and morale in the army collapsed.

sentences.zh: 昇明二年正月十九日夜，劉攘兵燒營入降郢城，眾於是離散，不可復制。

translations.literal: On the night of the nineteenth day of the first month of the second year of Shengming, Liu Rangbing burned his camp and surrendered into Ying city; the host then scattered, beyond recovery.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the nineteenth day of the first month in the second year of Shengming, Liu Rangbing burned his camp and surrendered to Ying city; the army then scattered beyond all control.

sentences.zh: 將曉，攸之斬劉天賜，率大眾過江，至魯山，諸軍因此散走。

translations.literal: Near dawn, Youzhi executed Liu Tianci, led the great host across the river to Lushan; the armies thereupon scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Near dawn, Youzhi executed Liu Tianci, led the main force across the river to Lushan, and the armies thereupon broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 還向江陵，未百餘里，聞城已為雍州刺史張敬兒所據，無所歸，乃與第三子中書侍郎文和至華容界，為封人所斬送。

translations.literal: Turning back toward Jiangling, not yet a hundred li on, he heard the city was already held by Zhang Jing'er, governor of Yong—nowhere to go; he went with his third son Wenhe, Attendant of the Secretariat, to the border of Huarong, where a frontier man cut off his head and sent it in.
translations.idiomatic: Turning back toward Jiangling, he had gone less than a hundred li when he learned the city had already been taken by Yong Governor Zhang Jing'er. With nowhere to go, he went with his third son Wenhe, Attendant of the Secretariat, to the border of Huarong, where a frontier man cut off his head and sent it in.

sentences.zh: 攸之晚好讀書，手不釋卷，《史》、《漢》事多所諳憶，常歎曰：「早知窮達有命，恨不十年讀書。」

translations.literal: In his later years Youzhi loved reading, hand never leaving the scroll; affairs of the Records and the Han he knew well from memory; he often sighed: "Had I known early that rise and fall are fated, I would regret not reading ten years."
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Youzhi loved reading and never let a scroll leave his hand; he knew many events from the Records and the Book of Han by heart and often sighed: "Had I known sooner that fortune and failure are fated, I would regret not having read for ten years."

sentences.zh: 及攻郢城，夜遇風浪，米船沉沒，倉曹參軍崔靈鳳女幼適柳世隆子，攸之正色謂曰：「當今軍糧要急，而卿不以在意，將由與城內婚姻邪？」

translations.literal: When besieging Ying city, one night they met wind and waves; grain boats sank; Storehouse Attendant Cui Lingfeng's young daughter was married to Liu Shilong's son; Youzhi sternly said: "Now army grain is urgently needed, yet you pay no heed—is it because of marriage ties within the city?"
translations.idiomatic: During the siege of Ying city, one night wind and waves struck and grain boats sank. Storehouse Attendant Cui Lingfeng's young daughter had married Liu Shilong's son. Youzhi said sternly: "Army grain is urgently needed, yet you show no concern—is this because of your marriage ties with the city?"

sentences.zh: 靈鳳答曰：「樂廣有言，下官豈以五男易一女。」

translations.literal: Lingfeng replied: "Yue Guang once said—would your servant trade five sons for one daughter?"
translations.idiomatic: Lingfeng replied: "As Yue Guang once said—would I trade five sons for one daughter?"

sentences.zh: 攸之歡然意解。

translations.literal: Youzhi was pleased and his suspicion cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi was pleased, and his suspicion vanished.

sentences.zh: 初，攸之招集才力之士，隨郡人雙泰真有幹力，召不肯來。

translations.literal: At first Youzhi gathered men of talent and strength; Shuang Taizhen of Suiping had real ability— summoned, he would not come.
translations.idiomatic: At first Youzhi gathered men of talent and strength. Shuang Taizhen of Suiping was capable, but when summoned he refused to come.

sentences.zh: 後泰真至江陵賣買，有以告攸之者，攸之因留之，補隊副，厚加料理。

translations.literal: Later Taizhen came to Jiangling on business; someone informed Youzhi; Youzhi kept him, appointed him deputy squad chief, and treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Later Taizhen came to Jiangling on business; someone informed Youzhi, who detained him, appointed him deputy squad chief, and treated him generously.

sentences.zh: 泰真無停志，少日叛走，攸之遣二十人被甲追之，逐討甚急。

translations.literal: Taizhen had no pause in his resolve; within days he fled in revolt; Youzhi sent twenty armored men in pursuit, pressing hard.
translations.idiomatic: Taizhen never wavered in his resolve; within days he fled. Youzhi sent twenty armored men in hot pursuit.

sentences.zh: 泰真殺數人，餘者不敢近。

translations.literal: Taizhen killed several; the rest dared not approach.
translations.idiomatic: Taizhen killed several of them, and the rest dared not come near.

sentences.zh: 欲過家將母去，事迫不獲，單身走入蠻；

translations.literal: He wished to pass home and take his mother away; circumstances pressed and he could not; alone he fled into the frontier barbarians;
translations.idiomatic: He wanted to stop at home and take his mother with him, but events pressed and he could not; alone he fled into the barbarian lands;

sentences.zh: 追者既失之，錄其母而去。

translations.literal: The pursuers having lost him, seized his mother and left.
translations.idiomatic: the pursuers, having lost him, seized his mother and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 泰真既失母，乃出自歸，攸之不罪，曰：「此孝子也。」

translations.literal: Taizhen having lost his mother then came out and surrendered; Youzhi did not punish him, saying: "This is a filial son."
translations.idiomatic: After losing his mother, Taizhen came out and surrendered. Youzhi did not punish him, saying: "This is a filial son."

sentences.zh: 賜錢一萬，轉補隊主，其矯情任笇皆如此。

translations.literal: He granted ten thousand cash and promoted him to squad chief—all his feigned sentiment and calculated conduct were like this.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him ten thousand cash and promoted him to squad chief—all his feigned virtue and calculated showmanship were like this.

sentences.zh: 初，攸之賤時，與吳郡孫超之、全景文共乘小船出京都，三人共上引埭，有一人止而相之曰：「君三人皆當至方伯。」

translations.literal: At first, when Youzhi was low in station, he shared a small boat out of the capital with Sun Chaozhi of Wu and Quan Jingwen; the three together ascended Yin Embankment; a man stopped and read their features: "You three will all reach regional lord."
translations.idiomatic: In his early days, when Youzhi was still obscure, he shared a small boat leaving the capital with Sun Chaozhi of Wu and Quan Jingwen. As the three climbed Yin Embankment together, a man stopped them and read their features, saying: "All three of you will rise to regional lord."

sentences.zh: 攸之曰：「豈有三人俱有此相？」

translations.literal: Youzhi said: "Can all three share such a fate?"
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi said: "Can all three of us share such a destiny?"

sentences.zh: 相者曰：「骨法如此，若有不驗，便是相書誤耳。」

translations.literal: The reader said: "The bone pattern is so—if it fails, then the physiognomy texts are wrong."
translations.idiomatic: The reader said: "Your bone structure says so—if it fails to come true, then the books of physiognomy are wrong."

sentences.zh: 其後攸之為郢、荊二州，超之廣州，景文豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Afterward Youzhi held Ying and Jing; Chaozhi Guangzhou; Jingwen Yuzhou governor.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Youzhi became governor of Ying and Jing, Chaozhi governor of Guangzhou, and Jingwen governor of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 攸之初至郢州，有順流之志。

translations.literal: When Youzhi first reached Ying Province, he had a mind to sail downstream.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhi first reached Ying Province, he intended to sail downstream toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 府主簿宗儼之勸攻郢城，功曹臧寅以為：「攻守勢異，非旬日所拔，若不時舉，挫銳損威。

translations.literal: Registrar Zong Yanzhi urged attacking Ying city; Personnel Officer Zang Yin argued: "Attack and defense differ in strength; it is not taken in ten days; if you do not move in season, sharpness is blunted and prestige lost.
translations.idiomatic: Registrar Zong Yanzhi urged an attack on Ying city, but Personnel Officer Zang Yin argued: "The balance of attack and defense differs; the city cannot be taken in ten days. If you do not move at the right moment, your edge will dull and your prestige suffer.

sentences.zh: 今順流長驅，計日可捷，既傾根本，則郢城豈能自固。」

translations.literal: Now sweep downstream in long drive—victory in counted days; once the root is overturned, how can Ying city hold itself?"
translations.idiomatic: Now sweep downstream in a long drive—victory may come in counted days. Once the root is overturned, how can Ying city hold out on its own?"

sentences.zh: 攸之不從，既敗，諸將帥皆奔散，惟寅曰：「我委質事人，豈可苟免。

translations.literal: Youzhi did not follow; once defeated, all commanders scattered—only Yin said: "I pledged my substance to serve a man—how could I seek easy escape?
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi did not listen. After defeat, all the commanders fled—only Yin said: "I pledged myself to serve a lord; how could I seek an easy escape?

sentences.zh: 我之不負公，猶公之不負朝廷也。」

translations.literal: My not failing the lord is like the lord's not failing the court."
translations.idiomatic: My loyalty to my lord is like my lord's loyalty to the court."

sentences.zh: 乃投水死。

translations.literal: He cast himself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself into the water and drowned.

sentences.zh: 寅，字士若，東莞莒人也。

translations.literal: Yin, styled Shiruo, was a native of Ju in Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, styled Shiruo, was a native of Ju in Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 先是，攸之在郢州，州從事輒與府錄事鞭，攸之免從事官，而更鞭錄事五十。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Youzhi was in Ying Province, a provincial aide often flogged the headquarters recorder; Youzhi removed the aide from office and instead flogged the recorder fifty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Youzhi was in Ying Province, a provincial aide repeatedly flogged the headquarters recorder. Youzhi removed the aide from office and instead gave the recorder fifty strokes.

sentences.zh: 謂人曰：「州官鞭府職，誠非體要，由小人凌侮士大夫。」

translations.literal: He told others: "A provincial officer flogging a headquarters post is truly improper—but it comes of petty men bullying gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: He told others: "For a provincial officer to flog a headquarters official is truly improper—but it happens because petty men bully their betters."

sentences.zh: 倉曹參軍事邊榮為府錄事所辱，攸之自為榮鞭殺錄事。

translations.literal: Storehouse Attendant Bian Rong was insulted by the headquarters recorder; Youzhi personally flogged the recorder to death for Rong's sake.
translations.idiomatic: Storehouse Attendant Bian Rong was insulted by the headquarters recorder, and Youzhi personally flogged the recorder to death on Rong's behalf.

sentences.zh: 攸之自江陵下，以榮為留府司馬，守城。

translations.literal: When Youzhi marched down from Jiangling, he made Rong remain as garrison marshal to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhi marched down from Jiangling, he left Rong behind as garrison marshal to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 張敬兒將至，人或說之使詣敬兒降，榮曰：「受沈公厚恩，共如此大事，一朝緩急，便改易本心，不能行也。」

translations.literal: When Zhang Jing'er was about to arrive, some urged Rong to go and surrender; Rong said: "Having received Lord Shen's deep grace, sharing so great an affair—at one turn of crisis to change my heart—I cannot do it."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jing'er was about to arrive, some urged Rong to go over to him in surrender. Rong said: "I received Lord Shen's deep kindness and shared in this great undertaking; at the first turn of crisis to change my heart—I cannot do that."

sentences.zh: 城敗，見敬兒，敬兒問曰：「邊公何不早來？」

translations.literal: The city fell; he saw Jing'er; Jing'er asked: "Lord Bian, why did you not come sooner?"
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, he was brought before Jing'er, who asked: "Lord Bian, why did you not come sooner?"

sentences.zh: 榮曰：「沈公見留守城，而委城求活，所不忍也。

translations.literal: Rong said: "Lord Shen looked to me to hold the city—yet I would abandon the city to save my life; I cannot bear that.
translations.idiomatic: Rong said: "Lord Shen entrusted me to hold the city, yet I would abandon the city to save my life—that I cannot bear.

sentences.zh: 本不蘄生，何須見問。」

translations.literal: I never hoped to live—why ask?"
translations.idiomatic: I never hoped to live—why ask me that?"

sentences.zh: 敬兒曰：「死何難得。」

translations.literal: Jing'er said: "Death—how hard is it to obtain?"
translations.idiomatic: Jing'er said: "Death—how hard is that to obtain?"

sentences.zh: 命斬之，歡笑而去，容無異色。

translations.literal: He ordered him beheaded; Rong went laughing, countenance unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered him beheaded. Rong went to his death laughing, his expression unchanged.

sentences.zh: 泰山程邕之者，素依隨榮，至是抱持榮曰：「與邊公周遊，不忍見邊公前死，乞見殺。」

translations.literal: Cheng Yinzhi of Taishan had long followed Rong; now he embraced Rong and said: "Having traveled with Lord Bian, I cannot bear to see Lord Bian die first—I beg to be killed."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yinzhi of Taishan had long followed Rong. Now he embraced Rong and said: "I have traveled with Lord Bian; I cannot bear to see him die before me—I beg to be killed as well."

sentences.zh: 兵不得行戮，以告敬兒，敬兒曰：「求死甚易，何為不許。」

translations.literal: The soldiers could not execute him; they told Jing'er; Jing'er said: "Seeking death is very easy—why not grant it?"
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers hesitated to kill him and reported to Jing'er, who said: "If he seeks death, that is easily granted—why refuse?"

sentences.zh: 先殺邕之，然後及榮。

translations.literal: First Yinzhi was killed, then Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Yinzhi was killed first, then Rong.

sentences.zh: 三軍莫不垂泣，曰：「奈何一日殺二義士。」

translations.literal: The whole army wept: "How—two righteous men killed in one day?"
translations.idiomatic: The whole army wept and said: "How can two righteous men be killed in a single day?"

sentences.zh: 比之臧洪及陳容。

translations.literal: They were compared to Zang Hong and Chen Rong.
translations.idiomatic: People compared them to Zang Hong and Chen Rong.

sentences.zh: 榮，金城人也。

translations.literal: Rong was a native of Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was a native of Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 廢帝之殞也，攸之欲起兵，問其知星人葛珂之。

translations.literal: When the deposed emperor perished, Youzhi wished to raise troops and asked the star-knowing Ge Kezhi.
translations.idiomatic: When the deposed emperor died, Youzhi wished to raise troops and consulted the astrologer Ge Kezhi.

sentences.zh: 珂之曰：「自古起兵，皆候太白。

translations.literal: Kezhi said: "Since antiquity raising troops—all watch Venus.
translations.idiomatic: Kezhi said: "Since antiquity, all who raise troops watch the planet Venus.

sentences.zh: 太白見則成，伏則敗。

translations.literal: When Venus appears—success; when hidden—defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When Venus is visible, campaigns succeed; when it is hidden, they fail.

sentences.zh: 昔桂陽以太白伏時舉兵，一戰授首，此近世明驗。

translations.literal: Formerly Guiyang raised troops when Venus was hidden—one battle and his head was taken; this is a clear recent proof.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the Prince of Guiyang raised troops while Venus was hidden; after one battle his head was taken—this is a clear recent proof.

sentences.zh: 今蕭公廢昏立明，政值太白伏時，此與天合也。

translations.literal: Now Lord Xiao deposed the dark and raised the bright—just as Venus is hidden; this accords with heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Now Lord Xiao has deposed the unworthy and enthroned the worthy—just as Venus is hidden. This accords with heaven.

sentences.zh: 且太白尋出東方，東方利用兵，西方不利。」

translations.literal: Moreover Venus will soon rise in the east—the east favors arms, the west is unlucky."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Venus will soon appear in the east; the east favors military action, the west is unlucky."

sentences.zh: 故攸之止不反。

translations.literal: Therefore Youzhi stopped and did not rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Youzhi held back and did not rebel.

sentences.zh: 及後舉兵，珂之又曰：「今歲星守南斗，其國不可伐。」

translations.literal: When he later raised troops, Kezhi again said: "Now Jupiter guards the Southern Dipper—that state cannot be attacked."
translations.idiomatic: When he later raised troops, Kezhi again said: "Jupiter now guards the Southern Dipper; that state cannot be attacked."

sentences.zh: 攸之不從。

translations.literal: Youzhi did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi did not listen.

sentences.zh: 凡同逆丁珍東、孫同、裴茂仲、武茂宗、宗儼之竝伏誅。

translations.literal: All fellow rebels Ding Zhendong, Sun Tong, Pei Maozhong, Wu Maozong, and Zong Yanzhi were executed together.
translations.idiomatic: All fellow conspirators Ding Zhendong, Sun Tong, Pei Maozhong, Wu Maozong, and Zong Yanzhi were executed together.

sentences.zh: 攸之表檄文疏，皆儼之詞也。

translations.literal: Youzhi's memorials, proclamations, essays, and dispatches—all were Yanzhi's words.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi's memorials, proclamations, essays, and dispatches were all written by Yanzhi.

sentences.zh: 臧渙詣盆城自歸，今皇帝命斬之。

translations.literal: Zang Huan went to Pancheng and surrendered himself; the present emperor ordered him executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Huan went to Pancheng and surrendered; the present emperor ordered him executed.

sentences.zh: 餘同惡或為亂軍所殺，或遇赦得原。

translations.literal: The rest of the co-conspirators were either killed by disorderly troops or pardoned by amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining conspirators were either killed in the chaos or pardoned by amnesty.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：臧質雖貪虐夙樹，問望多闕，奉義治流，本無吞噬之志也。

translations.literal: The historian says: Though Zang Zhi was long known for greed and cruelty, with much lacking in reputation, governing Fengyi—he originally had no mind to devour.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Although Zang Zhi had long been known for greed and cruelty and lacked much in public esteem, in governing Fengyi he originally had no ambition to swallow the realm.

sentences.zh: 徒欲以幼君弱政，期之於世祖，據有中流，嗣桓、庾之業。

translations.literal: He merely wished, with a young ruler and weak government, to look toward Emperor Shizu, hold the midstream, and inherit the enterprise of Huan and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He merely hoped that under a young ruler and weak government he might look to Emperor Shizu, hold the middle Yangzi, and inherit the legacy of Huan Wen and Yu Liang.

sentences.zh: 既主異穆、哀，臣皆代黨，雖禮秩外厚，而疑防內深，功高位重，終非自安之地，至於陵天犯順，其出於此乎！

translations.literal: Since the ruler was of a different branch from Mu and Ai, and the ministers were all of the founding faction, though ritual rank was generous outwardly, suspicion and guard inwardly ran deep; merit high and position weighty were in the end no place of self-security—to reach the point of towering against Heaven and violating the right, did it not spring from this!
translations.idiomatic: The throne had passed to a different line from Mu and Ai, while the ministers remained men of the founding generation. Outwardly honors were lavish, yet inwardly suspicion ran deep. With merit so great and rank so high, there was no lasting security—and to climb against Heaven and violate the right, did not that rebellion spring from this very soil?

sentences.zh: 攸之伺隙西郢，年逾十載，擅命專威，無君已積。

translations.literal: Youzhi watched for openings in Western Yong for more than ten years; he usurped command and monopolized authority, his lordlessness long accumulated.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years Shen Youzhi watched for his chance in Western Yong, issuing orders on his own authority and hoarding power, his defiance of the throne long since ingrained.

sentences.zh: 及天厭宋道，鼎運將離，不識代德之紀，獨迷樂推之數，公休既覆其族，攸之亦屠厥身。

translations.literal: When Heaven grew weary of the Song Way and the tripod's fortune was about to depart, he did not recognize the cycle of dynastic virtue but was alone deluded by the reckoning of willing elevation; Gong Xiu had already overturned his clan, and Youzhi too slaughtered his own person.
translations.idiomatic: When Heaven turned against the house of Song and the imperial mandate was about to shift, he failed to read the turning of dynastic virtue and clung alone to the fantasy that the people would thrust greatness upon him. Gong Xiu had already destroyed his house, and Youzhi in turn brought ruin on himself.

sentences.zh: 夫以釁亂自終，固異代如一也。

translations.literal: To end through stain and rebellion—across different ages it is ever the same.
translations.idiomatic: To perish by treason and rebellion is, in every age, much the same.
